mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.latents_local_dependence_table <- function(x) {
  pairs <- x$local_dependence
  if (is.null(pairs) || nrow(pairs) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "This fit has no locally dependent pairs; fit with",
      "`local_dependence = \"item1:item2\"` to model one."),
      class = "latents_no_local_dependence", call = NULL))
  }
  kinds <- pairs$kind %||% rep("categorical", nrow(pairs))
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(index) {
    pair <- pairs[index, ]
    if (identical(kinds[index], "continuous")) {
      # The pair's covariance in each profile, and the correlation it implies.
      continuous <- .multilpa_continuous_names(x)
      first <- match(pair$item_1, continuous)
      second <- match(pair$item_2, continuous)
      return(do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(x$n_profiles), function(profile) {
        covariance <- matrix(x$covariances[, , profile], length(continuous))
        data.frame(pair = pair$name, kind = "continuous", profile = profile,
                   item_1 = pair$item_1, category_1 = NA_character_,
                   item_2 = pair$item_2, category_2 = NA_character_,
                   probability = NA_real_, independent = NA_real_, ratio = NA_real_,
                   covariance = covariance[first, second],
                   correlation = covariance[first, second] /
                     sqrt(covariance[first, first] * covariance[second, second]),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      })))
    }
    probabilities <- x$response_probabilities[[pair$name]]
    labels <- x$categorical_levels[[pair$name]]
    categories <- x$local_dependence_categories[[pair$name]]
    at <- match(labels, categories$label)
    first_items <- categories$level_1[at]
    second_items <- categories$level_2[at]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(probabilities)), function(profile) {
      joint <- probabilities[profile, ]
      marginal_1 <- tapply(joint, first_items, sum)[first_items]
      marginal_2 <- tapply(joint, second_items, sum)[second_items]
      independent <- unname(marginal_1 * marginal_2)
      data.frame(pair = pair$name, kind = "categorical", profile = profile,
                 item_1 = pair$item_1, category_1 = first_items,
                 item_2 = pair$item_2, category_2 = second_items,
                 probability = unname(joint), independent = independent,
                 ratio = unname(joint) / independent, covariance = NA_real_,
                 correlation = NA_real_, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  })
  result <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  result
}

.multilpa_run_start <- function(start_index, initial, pause = Inf, resume = NULL,
                                context) {
  with(context, {
    # A resumed start continues from its checkpoint, not from new values.
    if (!is.null(resume)) initial <- resume$state else
      initial <- .latents_mask_covariances(initial, covariance_pattern)
    .multilpa_em(x, group_index, initial,
               variance_model, min_variance, max_iter,
               tol, covariance_model, codes, n_categories, min_probability,
               held, structure, prior_parameters,
               accelerate_em = identical(acceleration, "squarem"),
               sampling_weights = sampling_weights, extra = fitting_extra,
               covariance_pattern = covariance_pattern, pause = pause,
               resume = resume)
  })
}

review_record.purpose: Finalise a profile fit from its selected starts

inputs.interpretation: Formal/default and guard syntax are read from the current parsed body. Documentation describes the intended contract; implicit callee requirements are not claimed exhaustively validated.

outputs.documented_return: A fitted multilpa object.
outputs.terminal_expression:
with(context, {
    found <- starts
    attempts <- starts$attempts
    valid <- starts$valid
    scores <- starts$scores
    best_start <- starts$best_start
    final_stage <- .latents_final_stage(found)
    best <- attempts[[best_start]]
    parameters <- best$parameters
    weighted_expectation <- best$expectation
    if (!is.null(sampling_weights)) {
        best$expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(x, group_index, parameters, codes, extra = fitting_extra)
    }
    subject_posteriors <- best$expectation$subject_posteriors
    subject_profiles <- max.col(subject_posteriors, ties.method = "first")
    noise_fields <- list(noise = isTRUE(noise))
    if (isTRUE(noise)) {
        split <- .multilpa_split_noise(parameters, subject_posteriors)
        parameters <- split$parameters
        subject_posteriors <- split$posteriors
        subject_profiles <- split$classes
        noise_fields <- list(noise = TRUE, noise_probability = split$noise_probability, noise_posteriors = stats::setNames(split$noise_posteriors, 
            rownames(data)), hypervolume = exp(-noise_log_density), n_noise = sum(subject_profiles == 0L))
    }
    parameters$means <- sweep(parameters$means, 2L, centers, "+")
    parameters <- .latents_uncenter_direct(parameters, fitting_extra)
    profile_names <- paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_profiles))
    type_names <- paste0("group_class_", seq_len(n_group_classes))
    parameters <- .multilpa_label_parameters(parameters, profile_names, continuous, categorical, encoded$levels)
    parameters <- .latents_label_extra(parameters, extra, profile_names)
    dimnames(parameters$profile_probabilities) <- list(type_names, profile_names)
    names(parameters$group_probabilities) <- type_names
    group_posteriors <- best$expectation$group_posteriors
    dimnames(subject_posteriors) <- list(rownames(data), profile_names)
    dimnames(group_posteriors) <- list(group_ids, type_names)
    n_parameters_unconstrained <- .multilpa_count_parameters(structure = structure, n_profiles, n_group_classes, ncol(x), 
        n_categories, variance_model, covariance_model)
    if (isTRUE(noise)) 
        n_parameters_unconstrained <- n_parameters_unconstrained + 2L
    if (!is.null(covariance_pattern)) {
        n_parameters_unconstrained <- n_parameters_unconstrained - .latents_pattern_zeros(covariance_pattern) * if (identical(variance_model, 
            "equal")) 
            1L
        else n_profiles
    }
    n_parameters_unconstrained <- n_parameters_unconstrained + .latents_extra_n_parameters(extra, n_profiles)
    n_parameters <- n_parameters_unconstrained - .multilpa_fixed_parameters(fixed, n_profiles, ncol(x), n_categories, variance_model, 
        covariance_model)
    n_parameters_with_measurement <- if (length(fixed) == 0L) 
        NULL
    else n_parameters_unconstrained
    log_likelihood <- weighted_expectation$log_likelihood
    starts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(attempts), function(start_index) {
        attempt <- attempts[[start_index]]
        data.frame(start = start_index, log_likelihood = scores[start_index], converged = if (valid[start_index]) 
            attempt$converged
        else FALSE, iterations = if (valid[start_index]) 
            attempt$iterations
        else NA_integer_, error = if (valid[start_index]) 
            NA_character_
        else attempt$error, boundary = if (valid[start_index]) 
            .multilpa_covariance_boundary(attempt$parameters %||% attempt$state, min_variance)
        else NA)
    }))
    starts <- .latents_search_columns(starts, found, n_starts, supplied = !is.null(start))
    observed_per_row <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) + (if (is.null(codes)) 
        0L
    else rowSums(!is.na(codes))) + if (is.null(.latents_extra_matrix(extra))) 
        0L
    else rowSums(!is.na(.latents_extra_matrix(extra)))
    n_informative <- sum(observed_per_row > 0L)
    n_informative_groups <- length(unique(group_index[observed_per_row > 0L]))
    boundary <- .multilpa_covariance_boundary(parameters, min_variance)
    counted_rows <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) 
        observed_per_row > 0L
    else rep(TRUE, nrow(x))
    counted_groups <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) 
        seq_len(n_groups) %in% group_index[observed_per_row > 0L]
    else rep(TRUE, n_groups)
    effective_profile_counts <- if (is.null(sampling_weights)) 
        colSums(subject_posteriors[counted_rows, , drop = FALSE])
    else setNames(colSums(weighted_expectation$subject_posteriors[counted_rows, , drop = FALSE]), profile_names)
    effective_group_counts <- if (is.null(sampling_weights)) 
        colSums(group_posteriors[counted_groups, , drop = FALSE])
    else setNames(colSums(weighted_expectation$group_posteriors[counted_groups, , drop = FALSE]), type_names)
    group_sample_size <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) 
        n_informative_groups
    else n_groups
    small_classes <- any(effective_profile_counts < 1) || any(effective_group_counts < 1)
    result <- c(parameters, list(call = call, vars = vars, continuous = continuous, continuous_types = vapply(data[continuous], 
        typeof, character(1)), ordinal = ordinal, count = count, extra_data = extra, categorical = categorical, categorical_levels = encoded$levels, 
        min_probability = min_probability, categorical_values = .multilpa_categorical_values(data, categorical, encoded), 
        indicator_data = as.matrix(indicator_frame), centering = centering, centering_offsets = centred$offsets, scaling = scaling, 
        scaling_factors = centred$scales, categorical_data = codes, id = id, group_ids = group_ids, single_level = single_level, 
        weights = weights, sampling_weights = if (is.null(sampling_weights)) NULL else setNames(sampling_weights, group_ids), 
        time = time, time_values = time_values, group_values = group_values, group_index = group_index, group_sizes = setNames(group_sizes, 
            group_ids), n_observations = nrow(x), n_informative = n_informative, informative = observed_per_row > 0L, n_informative_groups = n_informative_groups, 
        drop_empty = drop_empty, n_groups = n_groups, n_profiles = as.integer(n_profiles), n_group_classes = as.integer(n_group_classes), 
        variance_model = variance_model, covariance_model = covariance_model, covariance_structure = structure, prior = prior, 
        acceleration = acceleration, prior_parameters = if (is.null(prior_parameters)) NULL else utils::modifyList(prior_parameters, 
            list(mean = unname(prior_parameters$mean + centers))), missing = missing, max_iter = max_iter, tol = tol, n_observed_by_indicator = setNames(c(colSums(!is.na(x)), 
            if (is.null(codes)) NULL else colSums(!is.na(codes))), c(continuous, categorical)), min_variance = min_variance, 
        standard_deviations = sqrt(parameters$variances), fixed = fixed, measurement_model = .latents_measurement_model(ncol(x) > 
            0L, !is.null(codes), ordinal, count), subject_posteriors = subject_posteriors, group_posteriors = group_posteriors, 
        subject_profiles = subject_profiles, group_classes = max.col(group_posteriors, ties.method = "first"), log_likelihood = log_likelihood, 
        group_log_likelihood = setNames(best$expectation$group_log_likelihood, group_ids), n_parameters = n_parameters, n_parameters_with_measurement = n_parameters_with_measurement, 
        aic = -2 * log_likelihood + 2 * n_parameters, bic = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters, 
        bic_groups = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters, bic_individual = -2 * log_likelihood + 
            log(n_informative) * n_parameters, converged = best$converged, iterations = best$iterations, log_likelihood_history = best$history, 
        starts = starts, best_start = best_start, n_failed_starts = sum(!valid), boundary = boundary, small_classes = small_classes, 
        effective_profile_counts = effective_profile_counts, effective_group_counts = effective_group_counts, n_best_replicated = sum(valid & 
            final_stage & abs(scores - log_likelihood) <= 1e-06 * (1 + abs(log_likelihood))), replication_tolerance = 1e-06 * 
            (1 + abs(log_likelihood))), noise_fields, .latents_search_record(search, n_starts, screen, select_start, if (exclude_boundary) "exclude" else "allow"))
    class(result) <- "multilpa"
    if (!is.null(covariance_pattern)) {
        result$covariance_pattern <- covariance_pattern
        result$local_dependence <- .latents_classify_pairs(.latents_parse_pairs(local_dependence), categorical)
    }
    if (any(!valid)) {
        warning(warningCondition(sprintf("%d of %d starts failed; see get_results(fit, \"starts\").", sum(!valid), length(attempts)), 
            class = "latents_failed_starts", call = NULL))
    }
    if (!best$converged && max_iter > 0L) {
        warning(warningCondition("The best start did not converge; increase max_iter and see get_results(fit, \"starts\").", 
            class = "latents_unconverged", call = NULL))
    }
    if (boundary) {
        warning(warningCondition(if (covariance_model == "full") 
            "A covariance eigenvalue reached min_variance; this is a bound-active constrained fit."
        else "A variance reached min_variance; this is a bound-active constrained fit.", class = "latents_boundary", call = NULL))
    }
    if (small_classes) {
        warning(warningCondition("A profile or group class has effective membership below one.", class = "latents_small_classes", 
            call = NULL))
    }
    gaussian_rows <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) > 0L
    gaussian_counts <- colSums(weighted_expectation$subject_posteriors[gaussian_rows, seq_len(n_profiles), drop = FALSE])
    .latents_warn_thin_profiles(gaussian_counts, .latents_profile_parameters(ncol(x), variance_model, covariance_model, structure, 
        covariance_pattern = covariance_pattern, fixed = fixed))
    result$gaussian_diagnostics <- .latents_gaussian_diagnostics(parameters, x, subject_posteriors, weights = if (is.null(sampling_weights)) 
        NULL
    else sampling_weights[group_index], min_variance = min_variance)
    .latents_warn_poisson_limit(result$count_dispersion)
    result
})

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_finalise <- function(starts, context) {
  with(context, {
    found <- starts
    attempts <- starts$attempts
    valid <- starts$valid
    scores <- starts$scores
    best_start <- starts$best_start
    final_stage <- .latents_final_stage(found)
    best <- attempts[[best_start]]
    parameters <- best$parameters
    # The weighted expectation carries weighted posteriors, which are counts for
    # the M-step; each unit's own classification is the unweighted posterior.
    weighted_expectation <- best$expectation
    if (!is.null(sampling_weights)) {
      best$expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(x, group_index, parameters, codes,
                                                extra = fitting_extra)
    }
    subject_posteriors <- best$expectation$subject_posteriors
    subject_profiles <- max.col(subject_posteriors, ties.method = "first")
    noise_fields <- list(noise = isTRUE(noise))
    if (isTRUE(noise)) {
      split <- .multilpa_split_noise(parameters, subject_posteriors)
      parameters <- split$parameters
      subject_posteriors <- split$posteriors
      subject_profiles <- split$classes
      noise_fields <- list(
        noise = TRUE, noise_probability = split$noise_probability,
        noise_posteriors = stats::setNames(split$noise_posteriors, rownames(data)),
        hypervolume = exp(-noise_log_density),
        n_noise = sum(subject_profiles == 0L))
    }
    parameters$means <- sweep(parameters$means, 2L, centers, "+")
    parameters <- .latents_uncenter_direct(parameters, fitting_extra)
    profile_names <- paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_profiles))
    type_names <- paste0("group_class_", seq_len(n_group_classes))
    parameters <- .multilpa_label_parameters(parameters, profile_names, continuous,
                                           categorical, encoded$levels)
    parameters <- .latents_label_extra(parameters, extra, profile_names)
    dimnames(parameters$profile_probabilities) <- list(type_names, profile_names)
    names(parameters$group_probabilities) <- type_names
    group_posteriors <- best$expectation$group_posteriors
    dimnames(subject_posteriors) <- list(rownames(data), profile_names)
    dimnames(group_posteriors) <- list(group_ids, type_names)
    # A noise component adds its mixing proportion and, as mclust counts it
    # (`nMclustParams(noise = TRUE)`), the hypervolume estimated from the data:
    # two, so that every criterion equals mclust's.
    n_parameters_unconstrained <- .multilpa_count_parameters(structure = structure,
      n_profiles, n_group_classes, ncol(x), n_categories, variance_model,
      covariance_model)
    if (isTRUE(noise)) n_parameters_unconstrained <- n_parameters_unconstrained + 2L
    # The covariances a pattern holds at zero are not parameters.
    if (!is.null(covariance_pattern)) {
      n_parameters_unconstrained <- n_parameters_unconstrained -
        .latents_pattern_zeros(covariance_pattern) *
        if (identical(variance_model, "equal")) 1L else n_profiles
    }
    n_parameters_unconstrained <- n_parameters_unconstrained +
      .latents_extra_n_parameters(extra, n_profiles)
    n_parameters <- n_parameters_unconstrained -
      .multilpa_fixed_parameters(fixed, n_profiles, ncol(x), n_categories,
                                 variance_model, covariance_model)
    ## A held fit is comparable with other held fits on `n_parameters` and with a
    ## joint fit on the count that includes the measurement it was handed. Only
    ## `fit_staged()` used to record the second one, so `print()` fell through
    ## `%||%` on a `multilpa(fixed = )` fit and reported the same number twice.
    n_parameters_with_measurement <- if (length(fixed) == 0L) NULL else
      n_parameters_unconstrained
    log_likelihood <- weighted_expectation$log_likelihood
    starts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(attempts), function(start_index) {
      attempt <- attempts[[start_index]]
      data.frame(start = start_index, log_likelihood = scores[start_index],
                 converged = if (valid[start_index]) attempt$converged else FALSE,
                 iterations = if (valid[start_index]) attempt$iterations else NA_integer_,
                 error = if (valid[start_index]) NA_character_ else attempt$error,
                 boundary = if (valid[start_index])
                   .multilpa_covariance_boundary(attempt$parameters %||% attempt$state,
                                                 min_variance) else NA)
    }))
    starts <- .latents_search_columns(starts, found, n_starts, supplied = !is.null(start))
    # A row with no observed indicator contributes nothing to the likelihood and
    # nothing to any estimate, so it must not enlarge the sample size the
    # individual-level BIC penalizes against.
    observed_per_row <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) +
      (if (is.null(codes)) 0L else rowSums(!is.na(codes))) +
      if (is.null(.latents_extra_matrix(extra))) 0L else
        rowSums(!is.na(.latents_extra_matrix(extra)))
    # Reported by print() and summary() rather than warned about: resampling verbs
    # refit the same data many times, and a warning would fire once per replicate.
    n_informative <- sum(observed_per_row > 0L)
    # A group whose every row observes nothing is left out of the group sample
    # size the same way, as Mplus leaves it out of its clusters.
    n_informative_groups <- length(unique(group_index[observed_per_row > 0L]))
    boundary <- .multilpa_covariance_boundary(parameters, min_variance)
    # Effective memberships are the counts the fit reports: weighted for a
    # weighted fit, so the flag, its warning and the printed counts agree.
    # Under `drop_empty`, the counts are of the rows and groups that were
    # classified, as Mplus counts them; otherwise of every row and group.
    counted_rows <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) observed_per_row > 0L else
      rep(TRUE, nrow(x))
    counted_groups <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty))
      seq_len(n_groups) %in% group_index[observed_per_row > 0L] else rep(TRUE, n_groups)
    effective_profile_counts <- if (is.null(sampling_weights))
      colSums(subject_posteriors[counted_rows, , drop = FALSE]) else
        setNames(colSums(weighted_expectation$subject_posteriors[counted_rows, , drop = FALSE]),
                 profile_names)
    effective_group_counts <- if (is.null(sampling_weights))
      colSums(group_posteriors[counted_groups, , drop = FALSE]) else
        setNames(colSums(weighted_expectation$group_posteriors[counted_groups, , drop = FALSE]),
                 type_names)
    group_sample_size <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) n_informative_groups else n_groups
    small_classes <- any(effective_profile_counts < 1) ||
      any(effective_group_counts < 1)
    result <- c(parameters, list(
      call = call, vars = vars, continuous = continuous,
      continuous_types = vapply(data[continuous], typeof, character(1)),
      ordinal = ordinal, count = count, extra_data = extra,
      categorical = categorical,
      categorical_levels = encoded$levels, min_probability = min_probability,
      categorical_values = .multilpa_categorical_values(data, categorical, encoded),
      indicator_data = as.matrix(indicator_frame),
      centering = centering, centering_offsets = centred$offsets,
      scaling = scaling, scaling_factors = centred$scales,
      categorical_data = codes,
      id = id, group_ids = group_ids, single_level = single_level,
      weights = weights,
      sampling_weights = if (is.null(sampling_weights)) NULL else
        setNames(sampling_weights, group_ids),
      time = time, time_values = time_values,
      group_values = group_values, group_index = group_index,
      group_sizes = setNames(group_sizes, group_ids),
      n_observations = nrow(x), n_informative = n_informative,
      informative = observed_per_row > 0L,
      n_informative_groups = n_informative_groups, drop_empty = drop_empty,
      n_groups = n_groups, n_profiles = as.integer(n_profiles),
      n_group_classes = as.integer(n_group_classes), variance_model = variance_model,
      covariance_model = covariance_model, covariance_structure = structure,
      prior = prior, acceleration = acceleration,
      prior_parameters = if (is.null(prior_parameters)) NULL else
        utils::modifyList(prior_parameters,
                          list(mean = unname(prior_parameters$mean + centers))),
      missing = missing, max_iter = max_iter, tol = tol,
      n_observed_by_indicator = setNames(
        c(colSums(!is.na(x)), if (is.null(codes)) NULL else colSums(!is.na(codes))),
        c(continuous, categorical)),
      min_variance = min_variance, standard_deviations = sqrt(parameters$variances),
      fixed = fixed,
      measurement_model = .latents_measurement_model(ncol(x) > 0L, !is.null(codes),
                                                     ordinal, count),
      subject_posteriors = subject_posteriors, group_posteriors = group_posteriors,
      subject_profiles = subject_profiles,
      group_classes = max.col(group_posteriors, ties.method = "first"),
      log_likelihood = log_likelihood,
      group_log_likelihood = setNames(best$expectation$group_log_likelihood, group_ids),
      n_parameters = n_parameters,
      n_parameters_with_measurement = n_parameters_with_measurement,
      aic = -2 * log_likelihood + 2 * n_parameters,
      bic = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters,
      bic_groups = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters,
      bic_individual = -2 * log_likelihood + log(n_informative) * n_parameters,
      converged = best$converged, iterations = best$iterations,
      log_likelihood_history = best$history, starts = starts, best_start = best_start,
      n_failed_starts = sum(!valid), boundary = boundary, small_classes = small_classes,
      effective_profile_counts = effective_profile_counts,
      effective_group_counts = effective_group_counts,
      n_best_replicated = sum(valid & final_stage &
                                abs(scores - log_likelihood) <=
                               1e-6 * (1 + abs(log_likelihood))),
      replication_tolerance = 1e-6 * (1 + abs(log_likelihood))), noise_fields,
      .latents_search_record(search, n_starts, screen, select_start,
                             if (exclude_boundary) "exclude" else "allow"))
    class(result) <- "multilpa"
    # Recorded only when used, so a fit without local dependence has exactly the
    # fields it always had.
    if (!is.null(covariance_pattern)) {
      result$covariance_pattern <- covariance_pattern
      result$local_dependence <- .latents_classify_pairs(
        .latents_parse_pairs(local_dependence), categorical)
    }
    if (any(!valid)) {
      warning(warningCondition(sprintf(
        "%d of %d starts failed; see get_results(fit, \"starts\").",
        sum(!valid), length(attempts)), class = "latents_failed_starts", call = NULL))
    }
    # max_iter = 0 is a deliberate evaluate-only call, so non-convergence is
    # expected rather than an anomaly worth reporting.
    if (!best$converged && max_iter > 0L) {
      warning(warningCondition(
        "The best start did not converge; increase max_iter and see get_results(fit, \"starts\").",
        class = "latents_unconverged", call = NULL))
    }
    if (boundary) {
      warning(warningCondition(if (covariance_model == "full")
        "A covariance eigenvalue reached min_variance; this is a bound-active constrained fit." else
        "A variance reached min_variance; this is a bound-active constrained fit.",
        class = "latents_boundary", call = NULL))
    }
    if (small_classes) {
      warning(warningCondition(
        "A profile or group class has effective membership below one.",
        class = "latents_small_classes", call = NULL))
    }
    # Classification can include categorical-only or retained empty rows;
    # those rows do not support a Gaussian measurement density.
    gaussian_rows <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) > 0L
    gaussian_counts <- colSums(weighted_expectation$subject_posteriors[
      gaussian_rows, seq_len(n_profiles), drop = FALSE])
    .latents_warn_thin_profiles(
      gaussian_counts,
      .latents_profile_parameters(ncol(x), variance_model, covariance_model, structure,
                                  covariance_pattern = covariance_pattern, fixed = fixed))
    result$gaussian_diagnostics <- .latents_gaussian_diagnostics(
      parameters, x, subject_posteriors,
      weights = if (is.null(sampling_weights)) NULL else sampling_weights[group_index],
      min_variance = min_variance)
    .latents_warn_poisson_limit(result$count_dispersion)
    result
  })
}

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_expectation <- function(x, group_index, parameters, codes = NULL,
                                  weights = NULL, extra = NULL) {
  stopifnot(is.matrix(x), is.numeric(x), !any(is.infinite(x)),
            length(group_index) == nrow(x), is.list(parameters),
            is.null(weights) || length(weights) == max(group_index))
  # A noise component is one more column: a constant density over the data's
  # hypervolume, with its own mixing proportion last in the profile row.
  measurement <- .latents_measurement_log_density(
    x, parameters, codes, extra, noise_log_density = parameters$noise_log_density)
  result <- c(.multilpa_nested_structure(measurement$log_density, measurement$offset,
                                         group_index, parameters),
              list(gaussian_moments = measurement$moments))
  if (is.null(weights)) result else .multilpa_weigh(result, weights, group_index)
}

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_ward_assignments <- function(input, n_clusters) {
  stopifnot("`input` must be a numeric matrix" = is.matrix(input),
            "`n_clusters` must not exceed the rows" = n_clusters <= nrow(input))
  used <- unique(round(seq(1, nrow(input),
                           length.out = min(nrow(input), 2000L))))
  tree <- stats::hclust(stats::dist(input[used, , drop = FALSE]), "ward.D2")
  labels <- stats::cutree(tree, n_clusters)
  centres <- rowsum(input[used, , drop = FALSE], labels) /
    as.vector(tabulate(labels, n_clusters))
  distance <- vapply(seq_len(n_clusters), function(cluster) {
    colSums((t(input) - centres[cluster, ])^2)
  }, numeric(nrow(input)))
  assignments <- max.col(-matrix(distance, nrow(input)), ties.method = "first")
  # Nearest-centre assignment can leave a small cluster empty on the full
  # data; its sampled members keep it.
  empty <- setdiff(seq_len(n_clusters), assignments)
  if (length(empty) > 0L) {
    keep <- labels %in% empty
    assignments[used[keep]] <- labels[keep]
  }
  assignments
}

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_em <- function(x, group_index, parameters, variance_model,
                        min_variance, max_iter, tol, covariance_model = "diagonal",
                        codes = NULL, n_categories = NULL, min_probability = 1e-10,
                        held = NULL, structure = NULL, prior = NULL,
                        accelerate_em = TRUE, sampling_weights = NULL,
                        extra = NULL, covariance_pattern = NULL, pause = Inf,
                        resume = NULL) {
  stopifnot(is.matrix(x), is.list(parameters), max_iter >= 0L, tol > 0,
            length(group_index) == nrow(x), min_variance > 0,
            variance_model %in% c("varying", "equal"))
  # Under a prior the iteration climbs the posterior, not the likelihood, so
  # the likelihood may legitimately fall; convergence is still read off the
  # likelihood's relative change, which is mclust's rule. SQUAREM needs a
  # likelihood objective, so a prior fit takes plain steps.
  accelerator <- if (isTRUE(accelerate_em) && is.null(prior)) {
    list(flatten = .multilpa_flatten_parameters,
         restore = .multilpa_restore_parameters,
         valid = .multilpa_valid_parameters)
  }
  fit <- .latents_em(
    parameters,
    evaluate = function(point) {
      .multilpa_expectation(x, group_index, point, codes, sampling_weights, extra)
    },
    # `point` warm-starts the covariance structures that iterate.
    maximize = function(point, expectation) {
      .multilpa_maximization(x, expectation, variance_model, min_variance,
                             covariance_model, codes, n_categories,
                             min_probability, held, structure, point, prior, extra,
                             covariance_pattern = covariance_pattern)
    },
    max_iter = max_iter, tol = tol,
    settings = .latents_em_settings(guard_decrease = is.null(prior),
                                    accelerate = accelerator),
    pause = pause, resume = resume)
  result <- list(parameters = fit$state, expectation = fit$expectation,
                 converged = fit$converged, iterations = fit$iterations,
                 history = fit$history)
  if (!is.null(fit$checkpoint)) result$checkpoint <- fit$checkpoint
  result
}

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_single_level <- function(data, n_group_classes,
                                   latent_class = FALSE) {
  stopifnot("`data` must be a data frame" = is.data.frame(data))
  name <- ".observation"
  if (name %in% names(data)) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "`id = NULL` gives every observation its own unit and names that unit",
      "`%s`, which these data already have as a column. Rename it, or pass it",
      "as `id` if it is the nesting unit."), name),
      class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  # Exactly one: `as.integer()` would let 1.5 or "1" through as a request for
  # one group class, which a fit with `id` refuses as not a positive integer.
  if (!is.null(n_group_classes) &&
      !(is.numeric(n_group_classes) && length(n_group_classes) == 1L &&
        identical(as.numeric(n_group_classes), 1))) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "`id = NULL` puts one observation in each unit, so there is no",
      "composition for a second-level class to differ in and",
      "`n_group_classes = %s` has nothing to estimate. Pass `id` to fit group",
      "classes, or leave `n_group_classes` alone for a single-level fit."),
      paste(deparse(n_group_classes), collapse = "")),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  .multilpa_single_level_notice(latent_class)
  data[[name]] <- seq_len(nrow(data))
  list(data = data, id = name, n_group_classes = 1L)
}

review_record.name: multilpa
review_record.purpose: Fit a two-level latent profile model  Fits a latent profile model for observations nested in groups and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. Each observation belongs to a Gaussian profile, and each group belongs to a latent group class that determines the profile proportions. Profile means and variances are shared across group classes (measurement invariance). By default indicators are independent within a profile; full residual covariances and observed-data maximum likelihood for missing indicators are available.

documented_parameters.data: A data frame containing the indicators and the group identifier.
documented_parameters.vars: Unique character vector of indicator column names. Columns not   named in `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count` are continuous indicators.
documented_parameters.id: Name of the group identifier column. Character, factor and   numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not. `id` has   no default: omitting it raises `latents_bad_argument`.    `id = NULL` fits a **single-level** model: each row is its own unit, the   observations are independent, and `n_group_classes` is one. The fit raises   a `latents_single_level` message. Every verb of the package works on the   result. The internal unit column is named `.observation`; it is not   returned by `get_results(x, "data")`, and a `data` that already has a   column of that name raises `latents_bad_data`. Requesting more than one   group class with `id = NULL` raises `latents_bad_argument`.
documented_parameters.n_profiles: Positive integer number of individual profiles.
documented_parameters.n_group_classes: Positive integer number of latent group classes   (default 2). With `id = NULL` it is one, and any other value is an error.
documented_parameters.profile_covariates: Names of numeric columns of   `data` that predict individual-profile and group-class membership through   multinomial logits, with the last class as reference. Naming either fits   the one-step maximum-likelihood covariate model and returns a   `multilpa_covariates` object. Profile intercepts differ by group class;   profile slopes are shared across group classes unless   `profile_slopes = "group_class"`. A group covariate must be constant   within each group. Covariates enter in their supplied units, without   centring or scaling. The covariate model refuses `start` and `fixed`; it   accepts `missing = "fiml"` for the indicators, but the covariates must be   complete. [three_step()] and [r3step()] are the staged alternatives.
documented_parameters.group_covariates: Names of numeric columns of   `data` that predict individual-profile and group-class membership through   multinomial logits, with the last class as reference. Naming either fits   the one-step maximum-likelihood covariate model and returns a   `multilpa_covariates` object. Profile intercepts differ by group class;   profile slopes are shared across group classes unless   `profile_slopes = "group_class"`. A group covariate must be constant   within each group. Covariates enter in their supplied units, without   centring or scaling. The covariate model refuses `start` and `fixed`; it   accepts `missing = "fiml"` for the indicators, but the covariates must be   complete. [three_step()] and [r3step()] are the staged alternatives.
documented_parameters.profile_slopes: `"shared"` (the default) gives each profile   covariate one slope per profile logit, common to every group class.   `"group_class"` estimates separate slopes in each group class (a   cross-level interaction), reported with terms such as `z:group_class_1`;   it multiplies the number of slope parameters by `n_group_classes`, each   set estimated from the groups in its class. Naming it without   `profile_covariates` raises `latents_bad_argument`.
documented_parameters.variance_model: `"varying"` (the default; profile-specific variances   or covariance matrices) or `"equal"` (shared across profiles).
documented_parameters.n_starts: Positive integer number of EM starts (default 10). The   first start is deterministic: Ward's hierarchical clustering of the   standardized indicators (on at most 2000 evenly spaced rows), each cluster   described by its own means and spread. The   remaining starts are k-means from random centres. A supplied `start`   replaces the first start, and the remaining starts are random. With   `start` and `max_iter = 0`, exactly one start is run whatever `n_starts`   is. Rows from zero-weight units do not supply initial clustering or   measurement parameters. For `search = "emEM"`, this is the finalist   budget, including the protected first start (see `search`).
documented_parameters.max_iter: Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start   (default 1000). `max_iter = 0` performs no update: with `start`, the model   is evaluated at exactly those values, for example to score them with   `logLik()`; without `start`, the random initializations are evaluated and   the one with the highest log likelihood is returned.
documented_parameters.tol: Positive relative log-likelihood tolerance (default `1e-8`).   Convergence requires an absolute change no greater than   `tol * (1 + abs(previous log likelihood))`.
documented_parameters.min_variance: Positive lower bound on each variance, or on each   covariance eigenvalue under full covariance, in squared input units   (default `1e-6`); the fit is then constrained maximum likelihood.   Estimates at the bound are reported and raise a warning.
documented_parameters.seed: Optional random seed: any whole number `set.seed()` accepts,   including negative ones. When supplied, the caller's random-number state   is restored on exit.
documented_parameters.start: Optional list of `means` and `variances` (profiles by   indicators), `profile_probabilities` (group classes by profiles), and   `group_probabilities` (vector). Starting probabilities must be positive.   For full covariance, supply `covariances` (indicators by indicators by   profiles); `variances` may then be omitted, or must match their diagonals.   A categorical model also takes `response_probabilities`, a list of one   profiles-by-categories matrix per indicator named in `categorical`. The   list is matched by position unless it is labelled: when its elements are   named after the indicators, or its columns after the categories, each   block is matched to the indicator and category its labels name. A label   naming an indicator or category the fit does not have raises   `latents_bad_start`.
documented_parameters.categorical: Character vector naming indicators to treat as   categorical. Each is modelled by unrestricted, profile-specific response   probabilities over its observed categories (the latent class measurement   model); binary, ordinal and unordered indicators are handled by the same   parameterization. Numeric, integer, logical, character and factor columns   are accepted. Indicators not named here stay Gaussian, so naming a subset   fits a mixed-mode model.
documented_parameters.model: The covariance structure as an mclust code, one of   `"EII"`, `"VII"`, `"EEI"`, `"VEI"`, `"EVI"`, `"VVI"`, `"EEE"`, `"VEE"`,   `"EVE"`, `"VVE"`, `"EEV"`, `"VEV"`, `"EVV"`, `"VVV"`. The letters give the   volume, shape and orientation, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across   profiles, with `I` for axis-aligned (no covariances). These are the codes   [enumerate_classes()] takes. Use it instead of   `variance_model`/`covariance_model` or `volume`/`shape`/`orientation`, not   together with them.
documented_parameters.volume: The covariance structure in its three   components. Each profile's covariance decomposes as   `Sigma_k = lambda_k * D_k * A_k * D_k'`, with *volume*   `lambda_k = |Sigma_k|^(1/d)`, *orientation* `D_k` (eigenvectors) and   *shape* `A_k` (diagonal, determinant one). Constraining the three across   profiles gives the fourteen models mclust names with three letters, all   of which are available.    `volume` is `"equal"` or `"varying"`. `shape` is `"equal"`, `"varying"`   or `"spherical"`; `"spherical"` makes every indicator's spread equal   within a profile and leaves no orientation to constrain. `orientation` is   `"axis"` (a diagonal covariance), `"equal"` (one orientation shared by   every profile) or `"varying"`. documented_parameters.select_start: Which start the fit reports. `"likelihood"` (the   default) takes the highest log likelihood across starts, preferring a   converged start only among those within a relative `1e-10` of it.   `"converged"` takes the highest log likelihood among the converged starts   when at least one converged, and among all starts otherwise. The two   differ when an unconverged start exceeds a converged one by a negligible   amount, as happens when a membership logit drifts along a flat ridge of   the likelihood; only the converged start is a maximum on which   [parameter_inference()] can be based. `summary()` and   `get_results(fit, "starts")` show every start.
documented_parameters.boundary: Whether a start with a variance at `min_variance` (a   covariance eigenvalue, under full covariance) may be reported. `"allow"`   (the default) permits it, as Mplus does, with a `latents_boundary`   warning. `"exclude"` sets such starts aside and applies `select_start` to   the rest; for models without covariates, the `boundary` column of the   starts table identifies them. When every start is at the bound, the best   is reported with a `latents_all_starts_boundary` warning. A Gaussian   profile can increase the likelihood without limit by shrinking around one   observation, so the size of that gain is set by `min_variance` rather than   by the data, and more starts make such a solution more likely to be found.   Categorical indicators have no variances and are unaffected.
documented_parameters.prior: `NULL` (the default) for maximum likelihood, or a   [prior_control()] object for maximum a posteriori estimation of the   Gaussian means and covariances under the conjugate prior of Fraley and   Raftery (2007), mclust's `priorControl()`. The hyperparameters default to   mclust's `defaultPrior()` computed from the indicators, and each M-step is   mclust's, so a fit from the same start reproduces   `mclust::Mclust(..., prior = priorControl())`. Available for EII, VII,   EEI, VEI, EVI, VVI, EEE, EEV, VEV and VVV (mclust has no prior for VEE,   EVE, VVE and EVV), with complete continuous indicators and without `fixed`   or membership covariates; otherwise `latents_unsupported_prior` is raised.   The mixing proportions have no prior. As in mclust, the fit's   `log_likelihood` is the *unpenalized* log likelihood at the posterior   mode, and `aic`, `bic` and their variants are computed from it with the   usual parameter count. EM convergence is judged on its relative change;   because a MAP step can lower that likelihood, the decrease check made   under maximum likelihood is not applied. `parameter_inference(method =   "wald")` raises `latents_unsupported_inference` for such a fit, because   the score is not zero at a posterior mode; `method = "bootstrap"` refits   every resample with the same prior. The fit stores the request as `prior`   and the resolved hyperparameters, in the indicators' units (centred,   under `centering`), as `prior_parameters`.
documented_parameters.noise: `FALSE` (the default), or `TRUE` to add a noise component: a   mixture component with constant density `1 / V` over the hypervolume `V`   of the data, which absorbs outliers and scatter that no Gaussian profile   explains (Banfield & Raftery, 1993; mclust's   `initialization = list(noise = )` and `Vinv`). `V` is mclust's   `hypvol()`: the smaller of the volumes of the data's axis-aligned and   principal-component-aligned bounding boxes. The component has no   measurement parameters; its mixing proportion is estimated with the   others, and, as in mclust, it adds two parameters (the proportion and the   hypervolume), so the criteria equal mclust's. A random start puts a tenth   of the mass on the noise; a `start` supplies `noise_probability` alongside   `profile_probabilities`, the two summing to one. Available for complete   continuous indicators with one group class (`id = NULL` or   `n_group_classes = 1`), under any of the fourteen covariance structures,   with or without `prior`; otherwise `latents_unsupported_noise` is raised.   In the fit the noise component is profile `0`, as in mclust's   classification: `subject_profiles` is `0` for an observation assigned to   it, `get_results(fit, "assignments")` adds a `posterior_noise` column,   `get_results(fit, "posteriors")` and   `get_results(fit, "profile_probabilities")` have profile-`0` rows, and the   classification diagnostics count it as a class. `means`, `variances`,   `covariances`, `profile_probabilities` and `subject_posteriors` describe   the Gaussian profiles only, so the last two sum to one minus the noise   share; the fit adds `noise_probability`, `noise_posteriors`, `n_noise` and   `hypervolume`. [parameter_inference()], [three_step()], [r3step()],   [bootstrap_lrt()], [starting_values()], bivariate residuals,   [fit_staged()] and the posterior plots raise `latents_unsupported_noise`   for such a fit.
documented_parameters.acceleration: `"squarem"` (the default) accelerates EM with SQUAREM   (Varadhan & Roland, 2008): each cycle extrapolates along the last two EM   steps and ends with an ordinary EM step, and falls back to plain EM when   the extrapolated point would lower the likelihood, so the iteration stays   monotone. Convergence is assessed over a whole cycle, so it is never   looser than plain EM's. `"none"` runs plain EM, which follows the same   path as mclust's `me()` from the same start. `iterations` and `max_iter`   count EM steps under either setting. Fits with `prior`, and models with   membership covariates, always use plain EM. For EVE and VVE, whose shared   orientation has no closed form, each EM iteration takes a fixed number of   warm-started orientation steps (a generalized EM step) under either   setting, which keeps every iteration monotone and the EM map a fixed   function, as SQUAREM requires.
documented_parameters.centering: How to centre the continuous indicators before fitting.   `"none"` (the default) fits them as supplied. `"person"` subtracts each   group's own mean from its rows, so values are deviations from the unit's   average, the profiles describe within-unit change rather than level, and   the group classes are types of change pattern rather than types of unit   (the person-mean-centred within-person design; Quintana, 2021; Voelkle,   Brose, Schmiedek, & Lindenberger, 2014). `"grand"` subtracts one mean per   indicator, which moves the origin without changing the within-group   structure. The offsets are stored on the fit, so   `get_results(x, "data")` returns the supplied columns and row-alignment   checks still apply. `"person"` raises `latents_bad_data` when it leaves an   indicator constant, as happens when a unit has one observation of it.
documented_parameters.scaling: How to scale the continuous indicators before fitting, at   the same levels as `centering`. `"none"` (the default) fits them as   supplied. `"grand"` divides each indicator by its standard deviation over   all observations; `"person"` divides each group's values by that group's   own standard deviation. With the matching centring these are z-scores:   `centering = "grand", scaling = "grand"` standardizes each indicator over   the sample, and `centering = "person", scaling = "person"` standardizes it   within each unit. Standard deviations use the observed values with   denominator `n - 1`. The scales are stored on the fit with the centring   offsets, so `get_results(x, "data")` returns the supplied columns, and   `predict()` scales new units by their own spread under `"person"` and by   the fitted spread under `"grand"`. Means, variances and covariances are   reported in standard-deviation units. The log likelihood and every   information criterion are those of the scaled values, so only fits with   the same centring and scaling are comparable. A standard deviation that is   zero or undefined (under `"person"`, a unit observed once on an indicator   or always giving the same value) raises `latents_bad_data`. Under   structures that give each indicator its own variance (`EEI`, `VVI`,   `EEE`, `VVV`, `EVI`, `VEI`), grand scaling changes only the units of the   estimates; under the spherical `EII` and `VII`, which impose one variance   on every indicator, it changes the solution.
documented_parameters.drop_empty: `TRUE` (the default) or `FALSE`: how the reported   statistics treat rows whose every indicator is missing, and groups   consisting only of such rows. These contribute nothing to the likelihood,   so the estimates are the same either way, and their posterior is the   prior. With `TRUE` they are excluded, as in Mplus, from the individual and   group sample sizes of the information criteria, from relative entropy,   AvePP and the entropy term of ICL, AWE and CLC, from the classification   tables and diagnostic plots, and from the effective class counts. With   `FALSE` every row and group is counted in those statistics (the results   of latents 0.9.37 and earlier), except in the individual sample size of a   `multilpa()` fit, which excludes such rows either way. [compare_models()]   and [bootstrap_lrt()] do not compare fits made with different   `drop_empty`. The setting is stored on the fit and passed on by   enumerations and refits; it has no effect on data without such rows.
documented_parameters.cores: Number of processor cores for the random starts (default 1).   The starting values are drawn in order in the current process and only   the EM iterations are distributed, so the result is identical to   `cores = 1`. Under `search = "emEM"` both the screening of the pool and   the final runs are distributed; the screening is most of the time of an   emEM fit, so a large model or data set gains most. Workers are forked   processes on macOS and Linux, and a socket cluster on Windows and on   macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, as in [enumerate_classes()]. Lost   worker results are retried once with half as many workers (rounded up).   One `latents_worker_lost` warning reports losses and recovery; starts still   lost are recorded as failed. Socket workers retain completed chunks, but   tasks within a failed chunk may also be retried. Models with   membership covariates run their starts on one core. To fit many models,   give `cores` to [enumerate_classes()], which shares its worker pool   across candidates and their starts for models without membership   covariates or joined categorical `local_dependence` pairs. Other fitting   engines use one task per candidate.
documented_parameters.local_dependence: Pairs of indicators that stay associated within   each class, written `"item1:item2"` (several as a character vector).   A pair of continuous indicators gets its own covariance in each class   (one shared covariance with `variance_model = "equal"`), every other   covariance staying zero: the covariance Latent GOLD fits with   `item1 <-> item2 | Cluster`. It is not combined with `covariance_model`,   `model` or the structure arguments, covariates, `time`, `prior`, `noise`   or held variances. A pair of categorical indicators is modelled jointly   within each class. Each such pair becomes one categorical indicator, named   `"item1:item2"`, whose categories are the observed combinations of the   two items' categories, so every class has its own joint distribution of   the pair: the class-specific association Latent GOLD fits with   `item1 <-> item2 | Cluster`. The other indicators stay independent given   the class. `get_results(fit, "local_dependence")` reports each class's   joint probabilities beside their values under independence; `predict()`,   `parameter_inference(data = )` and the other functions that take `data`   join the pair in the caller's data. A row observing one item of a pair   and not the other treats the pair as missing, with a   `latents_partial_pair` warning. A pair of indicators that are not both   categorical, that names an indicator twice or that shares an indicator   with another pair raises `latents_bad_argument`; a categorical item of a   pair whose categories contain `":"` raises `latents_bad_data`. Default:   none.
documented_parameters.direct_effects: Direct effects of covariates on continuous   indicators, written `"indicator ~ covariate"` (several covariates joined   with `+`, several indicators as a character vector). The covariate moves   the indicator's mean by the same amount in every profile,   `y = mean_k + b z + e` (Bandeen-Roche et al., 1997), so a difference in   the indicator that the covariate explains is not read as a difference   between profiles: the direct effect Latent GOLD fits with   `y <- 1 + Cluster + z`. Covariates are numeric columns of `data`,   observed in every row (code a categorical covariate as indicator   columns), and enter with their values as given, so `means` are the   profile means at a covariate value of zero; centre a covariate first to   read them at its mean. The effects are estimated with the profiles (a   conditional maximization step in EM; Meng & Rubin, 1993), have standard   errors in [parameter_inference()] (parameter `direct_effect`, term   `"indicator:covariate"`), and are reported by   `get_results(fit, "direct_effects")`. [predict()] and the functions that   take `data` read the covariates from it. Direct effects need a diagonal   covariance (EEI or VVI) and are not combined with `local_dependence`   between continuous indicators, `profile_covariates`, `group_covariates`,   `time`, `prior`, `noise`, `fixed`, `start`, `centering` or `scaling`;   those, a term that is not `"indicator ~ covariate"`, and an indicator   that is not continuous raise `latents_bad_argument`, and a covariate   that is absent, not numeric, missing or constant raises   `latents_bad_data`. Default: none.
documented_parameters.time: Optional name of a column giving each observation's position   within its group, such as a wave, occasion or course number. It is not   used in estimation; it is stored for `get_results(x, "sequences")`,   `get_results(x, "sequence_summary")` and `plot(what = "sequences")`.   Values must be complete and unique within each group, and are ordered as   [sort()] orders them. Numbers stored as text whose alphabetical order is   not their numeric order (`"2"`, `"10"`) raise `latents_bad_time`;   zero-padded numbers and ISO dates are accepted.
documented_parameters.fixed: Character vector naming measurement blocks to hold at the   values in `start` instead of estimating them: any of `"means"`,   `"variances"` and `"response_probabilities"`, or `"measurement"` for every   block the model has. Under `covariance_model = "full"`, `"variances"`   holds the residual covariance matrices. A held block stays as supplied in   every start and is not counted in `n_parameters`, so the result is a   different model, not a different starting point. `start` must contain the   named blocks; `starting_values(fit, what = "measurement")` produces them,   and [fit_staged()] performs the two-stage workflow in one call. The mixing   parameters cannot be held.
documented_parameters.min_probability: Positive lower bound on every categorical response   probability (default `1e-10`), constraining the maximum-likelihood problem   as `min_variance` does for Gaussian indicators.
documented_parameters.missing: `"error"` (the default) rejects missing indicators; `"fiml"`   maximizes the observed-data likelihood under an ignorable missingness   mechanism (MAR), integrating missing indicators out rather than filling   them in. This also holds with membership covariates; the covariates   themselves must be complete (`latents_bad_data`).
documented_parameters.covariance_model: `"diagonal"` (the default) assumes conditional   independence; `"full"` estimates within-profile residual covariances.
documented_parameters.family: The model family. `"profiles"` (the default) is the model   described above: individual profiles whose prevalences differ across   group classes. Three group-class-only families have no individual   profiles (Houle, Morin & Harvey, 2026): each group has a Gaussian   intercept per indicator, drawn from its group class's distribution, and   its members vary around it.   * `"additive"`: group classes differ in their means (and, optionally, in     between-group variances); one within-group variance per indicator is     shared by every class.   * `"dispersion"`: group classes differ in their within-group variances;     means and between-group variances are shared.   * `"additive_dispersion"`: group classes differ in means and in     within-group variances.    These families take only `data`, `vars`, `id`, `n_group_classes`,   `between_variance`, `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol`, `min_variance`,   `seed` and `weights`; any other argument raises `latents_bad_argument`.   Indicators must be complete and continuous, and at least one group must   have more than one row (`latents_unidentified` otherwise). Between   variances estimated at zero are reached by a boundary maximization with a   Karush-Kuhn-Tucker check and flagged (`latents_boundary`); interior fits   are finished by Newton steps. The result has class `multilpa_additive`;   `bic` uses the number of groups and `bic_individual` the number of rows.   It is read with [get_results()]; `summary()`, `plot()`, `coef()`,   `vcov()`, `confint()` and [parameter_inference()] work on it,   [enumerate_classes()] compares families through its `family` argument,   and [bootstrap_lrt()] tests one number of group classes against another.   These families are experimental: `parameter_inference(method =   "bootstrap")` raises `latents_unsupported_inference`, and missing   indicators (`latents_bad_data`), `missing`, membership covariates and   ordinal or count indicators (`latents_bad_argument`) are not available.   See the [group-class and cross-level models   article](https://pak.dynasite.org/latents/articles/additive.html).    Two cross-level families estimate individual profiles and group classes   from the same indicators, following the manifest-aggregation   specification of Houle et al. (2026, supplement): each group's means of   the indicators are between-level indicators of its group class, with   class-specific means and variances.   * `"restricted_cross_level"`: profile prevalences are the same in every     group class, so profiles and group classes are estimated separately;     the profile composition of each class is reported descriptively.   * `"full_cross_level"`: profile prevalences differ across group classes     (as in `"profiles"`), and the group means also inform the classes.    These take `data`, `vars`, `id`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`,   `variance_model` (individual profiles), `between_variance` (group   classes), `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol`, `min_variance`, `seed` and   `weights`. The group means are computed from the same ratings, so the   likelihood is the specification's working likelihood: comparable between   cross-level fits of the same data, not with the other families. Standard   errors are not available (`latents_unsupported_inference`). The result   has class `multilpa_cross_level`, read with [get_results()]. Its   `get_results(fit, "profiles")` table ends with a `prevalence` column:   each individual profile's prevalence (estimated and shared for the   restricted family, the class-weighted marginal for the full family) and,   on the group-class rows, the class weight.
documented_parameters.between_variance: For the additive and additive-dispersion families:   `"varying"` (the default) estimates between-group variances per group   class, `"equal"` one set shared by all classes. The dispersion family   holds them equal and refuses `"varying"`. For the cross-level families,   the variances of the group means within each group class.
documented_parameters.weights: `NULL`, or the name of a numeric column of `data` holding a   sampling weight for each independent unit: each `id` group of a two-level   fit, each row of a single-level one. A two-level weight must be constant   within its group (`latents_bad_weights` otherwise); within-unit weights   are not supported. The fit maximizes the pseudo log likelihood   `sum_j w_j log L_j` (Skinner, 1989) with the weights scaled to sum to the   number of units, as Mplus does, so integer weights give the fit to the   data with each unit repeated that many times and the criteria stay on the   sample's scale. Standard errors are sandwich estimates:   `parameter_inference()` defaults to `vcov_type = "robust"` and refuses   `"observed"` and `"opg"` (`latents_unsupported_weights`), and   `method = "bootstrap"` resamples the units with their weights.   Classification tables report each unit's own posterior; effective counts   and proportions are weighted. [bootstrap_lrt()], [three_step()],   [r3step()], `prior` and `noise` refuse a weighted fit. Weights work with   every `family`, membership covariates, categorical indicators and   `missing = "fiml"`.
documented_parameters.ordinal: Names of indicators in `vars` to model as ordinal: an   (ordered) factor, or whole numbers, whose categories are ordered by factor   level or by value. Each follows an adjacent-category logit with category   intercepts shared by every profile and one location per profile,   `log P(k | c) / P(k - 1 | c) = a_k - a_(k-1) + eta_c`, with the last   profile's location fixed at zero: `(K - 1) + (C - 1)` parameters per   indicator, against `C (K - 1)` for a `categorical` one. This is Latent   GOLD's default ordinal model, against which it is checked. The category   probabilities and locations are returned by   `get_results(fit, "ordinal")`. A factor level never observed in the data   raises the `latents_unused_category` warning; `droplevels()` removes it.
documented_parameters.count: Names of indicators in `vars` holding non-negative whole   numbers, modelled as Poisson with one mean per profile (or negative   binomial, see `count_model`); the means are returned by   `get_results(fit, "count_means")`. Ordinal and count indicators work with   `missing = "fiml"`, `weights`, two-level fits, membership covariates,   Wald and bootstrap inference, [bootstrap_lrt()], [predict()] and [lta()].   `start`, `fixed`, `prior` and `noise` do not accept them   (`latents_unsupported_indicator`), and the group-class and cross-level   families refuse them as arguments they do not take   (`latents_bad_argument`).
documented_parameters.count_model: `"poisson"` (the default) or `"negative_binomial"`: NB2,   with mean `mu` and variance `mu + alpha mu^2`, for counts more variable   than a Poisson within a profile (Latent GOLD's `poisson overdispersed`).   A dispersion estimated at zero is the Poisson limit, a boundary fit   (`latents_boundary` warning; Wald inference is refused there).
documented_parameters.count_dispersion: For `count_model = "negative_binomial"`: one   dispersion per profile (`"varying"`, the default) or one shared by every   profile (`"equal"`).
documented_parameters.search: How the starts are found: `NULL` (the default), `"kmeans"`   or `"emEM"`. `NULL` uses `"emEM"` when every profile shares one   covariance matrix (EII, EEI, EEE with continuous indicators), where the   likelihood is bounded and a higher maximum cannot be a collapsed profile,   and `"kmeans"` otherwise, including categorical-only models and the   group-class families. The search used is recorded on the fit, and   `search = "kmeans"` reproduces the fits of latents 0.96.2 for every   model. `"kmeans"` runs   `n_starts` starts to convergence: Ward's clustering first, then k-means   from random centres. `"emEM"` screens a pool of `n_screen` starts by a   short EM run each and runs `n_starts` finalists to convergence   (Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert, 2003). The first start (Ward's clustering,   or supplied starting values) reserves one finalist slot if its screening   succeeds; the remaining slots take the highest screening likelihoods.   Thus `n_starts = 1` finalizes Ward's start whenever it screens   successfully, even if another screened start has a higher likelihood.   With a supplied start and `n_starts = 1`, screening is skipped entirely.   The pool begins with the kmeans search's own   starts, drawn in the same order, followed by random partitions of the   rows and random rows as class centres, and `get_results(fit, "starts")`   gives every start of the pool with its `kind`, its `stage` and its   likelihood after screening. Either search reports the start with the   highest likelihood among those run to convergence (subject to   `select_start` and `boundary`). With profile-specific variances that   maximum can be spurious, a profile on a few nearly coincident points   with a variance near zero (McLachlan & Peel, 2000, section 3.10), and a   harder search finds such maxima more often. They are reported, not set   aside: a variance at `min_variance` as a boundary fit   (`latents_boundary`; `boundary = "exclude"` sets those starts aside),   and low Gaussian membership mass by a `latents_thin_profiles` heuristic   warning. `get_results(fit, "gaussian_diagnostics")` reports continuous   covariance and support measures without an automatic spike cutoff or   changing the selected start. Neither a warning's absence nor a repeated   likelihood establishes a regular or globally optimal solution.
documented_parameters.n_screen: For `search = "emEM"`, the number of starts screened, at   least `n_starts`. `NULL` (the default) screens five times `n_starts`.   The protected first start counts toward the `n_starts` finalist budget;   increasing `n_screen` does not add finalist slots. A single supplied   start with `n_starts = 1` disables screening.   A value with `search = "kmeans"`, or one below `n_starts`, raises   `latents_bad_argument`.

outputs.documented_return: A `multilpa` object containing `means`, `variances`, optional   `covariances` (indicators by indicators by profiles),   `profile_probabilities`, `group_probabilities`, posterior matrices,   classifications, log likelihood, information criteria, restart   diagnostics and convergence history. Individual rows keep their input   order; groups keep first-occurrence order. `bic` and `bic_groups` use the   observed group count; `bic_individual` uses `n_informative`, the number of   rows with at least one observed indicator. These are alternative   conventions, not interchangeable criteria. `boundary` identifies variance   bounds; `small_classes` flags a profile or group class whose effective   membership (`effective_profile_counts`, `effective_group_counts`, weighted   for a fit with `weights`) is below one, in which case the fit warns with   `latents_small_classes`. The fit carries no standard errors:   [parameter_inference()] computes them, and [bootstrap_lrt()] tests nested   models. Global optimality is not guaranteed for any `n_starts`.   `as.data.frame()` returns the tidy tables, selected by `what`.

mathematical_conventions.file_context: The public profile estimator routes families, validates indicator/group contracts, constructs numerically centered measurements, prepares starts, and delegates iteration. Gaussian MLE variances use posterior mass divisors rather than unbiased sample divisors; native groups use integer indices.
mathematical_conventions.function_contract: Fit a two-level latent profile model  Fits a latent profile model for observations nested in groups and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. Each observation belongs to a Gaussian profile, and each group belongs to a latent group class that determines the profile proportions. Profile means and variances are shared across group classes (measurement invariance). By default indicators are independent within a profile; full residual covariances and observed-data maximum likelihood for missing indicators are available.
mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
multilpa <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles,
                       n_group_classes = 2L,
                       profile_covariates = character(),
                       group_covariates = character(),
                       variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
                       n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 1000L, tol = 1e-8,
                       min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL, start = NULL,
                       missing = c("error", "fiml"),
                       profile_slopes = c("shared", "group_class"),
                       covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
                       categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10,
                       time = NULL, fixed = character(),
                       centering = c("none", "person", "grand"),
                       volume = NULL, shape = NULL, orientation = NULL,
                       model = NULL,
                       select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                       prior = NULL, noise = FALSE,
                       acceleration = c("squarem", "none"),
                       family = c("profiles", "additive", "dispersion",
                                  "additive_dispersion", "restricted_cross_level",
                                  "full_cross_level"),
                       between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
                       weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                       count = character(),
                       count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
                       count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
                       scaling = c("none", "person", "grand"),
                       drop_empty = TRUE, cores = 1L,
                       local_dependence = character(),
                       direct_effects = character(),
                       search = NULL, n_screen = NULL,
                       boundary = c("allow", "exclude")) {
  # Forward only supplied arguments so setup retains every missing() check.
  fitting_call <- match.call()
  setup_call <- fitting_call
  setup_call[[1L]] <- .multilpa_setup
  setup_call$.call <- substitute(quote(value), list(value = fitting_call))
  plan <- eval(setup_call, parent.frame())
  if (!inherits(plan, "latents_multilpa_plan")) return(plan)
  .multilpa_run_plan(plan, plan$cores)
}

review_record.documentation_contract: Fit a two-level latent profile model  Fits a latent profile model for observations nested in groups and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. Each observation belongs to a Gaussian profile, and each group belongs to a latent group class that determines the profile proportions. Profile means and variances are shared across group classes (measurement invariance). By default indicators are independent within a profile; full residual covariances and observed-data maximum likelihood for missing indicators are available.  @param data A data frame containing the indicators and the group identifier. @param vars Unique character vector of indicator column names. Columns not   named in `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count` are continuous indicators. @param id Name of the group identifier column. Character, factor and   numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not. `id` has   no default: omitting it raises `latents_bad_argument`.    `id = NULL` fits a **single-level** model: each row is its own unit, the   observations are independent, and `n_group_classes` is one. The fit raises   a `latents_single_level` message. Every verb of the package works on the   result. The internal unit column is named `.observation`; it is not   returned by `get_results(x, "data")`, and a `data` that already has a   column of that name raises `latents_bad_data`. Requesting more than one   group class with `id = NULL` raises `latents_bad_argument`. @param n_profiles Positive integer number of individual profiles. @param n_group_classes Positive integer number of latent group classes   (default 2). With `id = NULL` it is one, and any other value is an error. @param profile_covariates,group_covariates Names of numeric columns of   `data` that predict individual-profile and group-class membership through   multinomial logits, with the last class as reference. Naming either fits   the one-step maximum-likelihood covariate model and returns a   `multilpa_covariates` object. Profile intercepts differ by group class;   profile slopes are shared across group classes unless   `profile_slopes = "group_class"`. A group covariate must be constant   within each group. Covariates enter in their supplied units, without   centring or scaling. They are reported, not set   aside: a variance at `min_variance` as a boundary fit   (`latents_boundary`; `boundary = "exclude"` sets those starts aside),   and low Gaussian membership mass by a `latents_thin_profiles` heuristic   warning. `get_results(fit, "gaussian_diagnostics")` reports continuous   covariance and support measures without an automatic spike cutoff or   changing the selected start. Neither a warning's absence nor a repeated   likelihood establishes a regular or globally optimal solution. @param n_screen For `search = "emEM"`, the number of starts screened, at   least `n_starts`. `NULL` (the default) screens five times `n_starts`.   The protected first start counts toward the `n_starts` finalist budget;   increasing `n_screen` does not add finalist slots. A single supplied   start with `n_starts = 1` disables screening.   A value with `search = "kmeans"`, or one below `n_starts`, raises   `latents_bad_argument`. @return A `multilpa` object containing `means`, `variances`, optional   `covariances` (indicators by indicators by profiles),   `profile_probabilities`, `group_probabilities`, posterior matrices,   classifications, log likelihood, information criteria, restart   diagnostics and convergence history. Individual rows keep their input   order; groups keep first-occurrence order. `bic` and `bic_groups` use the   observed group count; `bic_individual` uses `n_informative`, the number of   rows with at least one observed indicator. These are alternative   conventions, not interchangeable criteria. `boundary` identifies variance   bounds; `small_classes` flags a profile or group class whose effective   membership (`effective_profile_counts`, `effective_group_counts`, weighted   for a fit with `weights`) is below one, in which case the fit warns with   `latents_small_classes`. The fit carries no standard errors:   [parameter_inference()] computes them, and [bootstrap_lrt()] tests nested   models. Global optimality is not guaranteed for any `n_starts`.   `as.data.frame()` returns the tidy tables, selected by `what`. @details Infinite and constant observed indicators are rejected; each   indicator must have at least two distinct observed values. No rows are   silently dropped. Under FIML, fully missing individuals contribute no   direct measurement likelihood but receive posterior probabilities from   their group's information. Observation counts include these individuals;   the individual-level BIC excludes them through `n_informative`, while the   group-level BIC uses all observed groups. Missing patterns can prevent   parameter identification; no general identification guarantee is made.   Only initialization fills missing values with indicator means; EM uses   conditional Gaussian sufficient statistics and observed marginal   densities. More than one group class requires more than one profile and at   least one group with more than one individual; these checks are necessary   but do not establish identification. By default the highest finite   likelihood across starts is returned, even if that start did not converge;   `select_start = "converged"` prefers a converged start, and `converged`   and `starts` show which was chosen. Profile and group-class labels are   arbitrary. @references Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models.   Sociological Methodology, 33, 213--239.   doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x.    Banfield, J. D., & Raftery, A. E. (1993). Model-based Gaussian and   non-Gaussian clustering. Biometrics, 49, 803--821. doi:10.2307/2532201.    Bandeen-Roche, K., Miglioretti, D. L., Zeger, S. L., & Rathouz, P. J.   (1997). Latent variable regression for multiple discrete outcomes.   Journal of the American Statistical Association, 92(440), 1375--1386.    Meng, X.-L., & Rubin, D. B. (1993). Maximum likelihood estimation via the   ECM algorithm: A general framework. Biometrika, 80(2), 267--278.   doi:10.1093/biomet/80.2.267.    Houle, S. A., Morin, A. J. S., & Harvey, J.-F. (2026). Multilevel latent   profile analyses: A comprehensive guide. Organizational Research Methods.   doi:10.1177/10944281261469432.    Skinner, C. J. (1989). Domain means, regression and multivariate   analysis. In C. J. Skinner, D. Holt, & T. M. F. Smith (Eds.), Analysis   of complex surveys (pp. 59--87). Wiley.    Asparouhov, T. (2005). Sampling weights in latent variable modeling.   Structural Equation Modeling, 12, 411--434.   doi:10.1207/s15328007sem1203_4.    Fraley, C., & Raftery, A. E. (2007). Bayesian regularization for normal   mixture estimation and model-based clustering. Journal of   Classification, 24, 155--181. doi:10.1007/s00357-007-0004-5. @examples # Course sessions nested in students: engagement profiles of sessions, and # classes of students that differ in how often they are engaged. activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance") fit <- multilpa(course_engagement, activity, "student",                 n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,                 seed = 42) summary(fit) as.data.frame(fit) get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities") @seealso [multilca()] for a model in which every indicator is categorical. @export @importFrom stats setNames
