mathematical_conventions.file_context: The public profile estimator routes families, validates indicator/group contracts, constructs numerically centered measurements, prepares starts, and delegates iteration. Gaussian MLE variances use posterior mass divisors rather than unbiased sample divisors; native groups use integer indices.
mathematical_conventions.function_contract: Prepare a profile-model fit without running its starts
mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_setup <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles,
                       n_group_classes = 2L,
                       profile_covariates = character(),
                       group_covariates = character(),
                       variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
                       n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 1000L, tol = 1e-8,
                       min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL, start = NULL,
                       missing = c("error", "fiml"),
                       profile_slopes = c("shared", "group_class"),
                       covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
                       categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10,
                       time = NULL, fixed = character(),
                       centering = c("none", "person", "grand"),
                       volume = NULL, shape = NULL, orientation = NULL,
                       model = NULL,
                       select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                       boundary = c("allow", "exclude"),
                       prior = NULL, noise = FALSE,
                       acceleration = c("squarem", "none"),
                       family = c("profiles", "additive", "dispersion",
                                  "additive_dispersion", "restricted_cross_level",
                                  "full_cross_level"),
                       between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
                       weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                       count = character(),
                       count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
                       count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
                       scaling = c("none", "person", "grand"),
                       drop_empty = TRUE, cores = 1L,
                       local_dependence = character(),
                       direct_effects = character(),
                       search = NULL, n_screen = NULL, .call = NULL) {
  .call <- .call %||% match.call()
  # Read before any argument is reassigned: missing() is FALSE afterwards.
  covariance_model_given <- !missing(covariance_model)
  # Locally dependent categorical pairs are joined into one indicator each,
  # and the model is fitted on the joint indicators with the caller's other
  # arguments; continuous pairs go on to a covariance pattern below.
  if (length(local_dependence) > 0L &&
      any(.latents_parse_pairs(local_dependence)$item_1 %in% categorical)) {
    return(.latents_fit_local_dependence(.call, environment(),
                                         local_dependence))
  }
  family <- match.arg(family)
  cores <- .latents_check_cores(cores)
  count_model <- match.arg(count_model)
  count_dispersion <- match.arg(count_dispersion)
  if (family %in% c("restricted_cross_level", "full_cross_level")) {
    supplied <- setdiff(names(.call)[-1L], .cross_level_arguments())
    if (length(supplied) > 0L || missing(id) || is.null(id) || missing(n_profiles)) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "`family = \"%s\"` needs `id` and `n_profiles`; it takes %s.%s"), family,
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", setdiff(.cross_level_arguments(), "family")),
              collapse = ", "),
        if (length(supplied) > 0L) sprintf(" Not applicable: %s.",
          paste(sprintf("`%s`", supplied), collapse = ", ")) else ""),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    return(.cross_level_fit(data, vars, id, n_profiles, n_group_classes, family,
                            match.arg(variance_model),
                            if (missing(between_variance)) "varying" else
                              match.arg(between_variance),
                            n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance, seed,
                            .call, weights = weights,
                            search = .latents_check_search(search) %||% "kmeans",
                            n_screen = n_screen))
  }
  if (!identical(family, "profiles")) {
    # Group-class families have no individual profiles, so most arguments
    # have no meaning for them; refuse those rather than ignore them.
    supplied <- setdiff(names(.call)[-1L], .additive_arguments())
    if (length(supplied) > 0L || missing(id) || is.null(id)) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "`family = \"%s\"` has group classes only and needs `id`; it takes",
        "%s.%s"), family,
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", setdiff(.additive_arguments(), "family")),
              collapse = ", "),
        if (length(supplied) > 0L) sprintf(" Not applicable: %s.",
          paste(sprintf("`%s`", supplied), collapse = ", ")) else ""),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    return(.additive_fit(data, vars, id, n_group_classes,
                         if (missing(between_variance)) NULL else
                           match.arg(between_variance),
                         n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance, seed,
                         .call, family = family, weights = weights,
                         search = .latents_check_search(search) %||% "kmeans",
                         n_screen = n_screen))
  }
  if (!missing(between_variance)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "`between_variance` belongs to the group-class families",
      "(`family = \"additive\"`); the profile model does not have it."),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  select_start <- match.arg(select_start)
  boundary <- match.arg(boundary)
  # Read once here: `boundary` is reused below for the selected fit's flag.
  exclude_boundary <- identical(boundary, "exclude")
  acceleration <- match.arg(acceleration)
  search <- .latents_check_search(search)
  ## Before `stopifnot()`, which reads `id` and would otherwise force the
  ## missing argument into R's own bare "argument \"id\" is missing" error.
  if (missing(id)) .multilpa_missing_id("multilpa", "`lpa()`")
  stopifnot(
    "`data` must be a data frame" = is.data.frame(data),
    "`vars` must be a character vector of column names" =
      is.character(vars),
    "`id` must be a single column name, or NULL for a single-level fit" =
      is.null(id) || (is.character(id) && length(id) == 1L),
    "`profile_covariates` must be a character vector of column names" =
      is.character(profile_covariates) && !anyNA(profile_covariates),
    "`group_covariates` must be a character vector of column names" =
      is.character(group_covariates) && !anyNA(group_covariates),
    "`categorical` must be a character vector of indicator names" =
      is.character(categorical) && !anyNA(categorical),
    "`min_probability` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
      is.numeric(min_probability) && length(min_probability) == 1L &&
      is.finite(min_probability) && min_probability > 0 &&
      min_probability < 1)
  # Every later reader of `start` indexes it as a list, so anything else would
  # surface as an unclassed `$` error from deep inside the fit.
  if (!is.null(start) && !is.list(start)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`start` must be NULL or a list of parameter blocks, such as starting_values(fit).",
      class = "latents_bad_start", call = NULL))
  }
  call <- .call
  single_level <- is.null(id)
  if (single_level) {
    resolved <- .multilpa_single_level(
      data, if (missing(n_group_classes)) NULL else n_group_classes,
      latent_class = length(vars) > 0L && all(vars %in% categorical))
    data <- resolved$data
    id <- resolved$id
    n_group_classes <- resolved$n_group_classes
  }
  # `model` names the whole covariance structure in mclust's three letters,
  # the same codes enumerate_classes() takes; it replaces the switches and the
  # pieces rather than combining with them.
  if (!is.null(model)) {
    if (!is.character(model) || length(model) != 1L ||
        !model %in% .multilpa_structures()) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
        "`model` must be one of the covariance structures %s.",
        paste(sprintf("\"%s\"", .multilpa_structures()), collapse = ", ")),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    if (!missing(variance_model) || !missing(covariance_model) ||
        !is.null(volume) || !is.null(shape) || !is.null(orientation)) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "Give the covariance structure either as `model` or through",
        "`variance_model`/`covariance_model` or `volume`/`shape`/`orientation`,",
        "not both."), class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    pieces <- .multilpa_structure_arguments(model)
    volume <- pieces$volume
    shape <- pieces$shape
    orientation <- pieces$orientation
  }
  variance_model <- match.arg(variance_model)
  covariance_model <- match.arg(covariance_model)
  missing <- match.arg(missing)
  centering <- match.arg(centering)
  scaling <- match.arg(scaling)
  .multilpa_check_drop_empty(drop_empty)
  profile_slopes <- match.arg(profile_slopes)
  if (identical(profile_slopes, "group_class") && length(profile_covariates) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "`profile_slopes = \"group_class\"` lets profile-covariate slopes differ",
      "across group classes, so it needs `profile_covariates`."),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  # Continuous local dependence: a covariance for each named pair within every
  # class, every other covariance zero, fitted as a patterned full covariance.
  covariance_pattern <- NULL
  if (length(local_dependence) > 0L) {
    covariance_pattern <- .latents_covariance_pattern(
      .latents_parse_pairs(local_dependence), vars, categorical, ordinal, count,
      conflicts = c(
        "covariance_model" = covariance_model_given, "model" = !is.null(model),
        "volume, shape or orientation" =
          !is.null(volume) || !is.null(shape) || !is.null(orientation),
        "profile_covariates or group_covariates" =
          length(profile_covariates) > 0L || length(group_covariates) > 0L,
        "time" = !is.null(time), "prior" = !is.null(prior),
        "fixed variances" = any(c("variances", "measurement") %in% fixed),
        "noise" = isTRUE(noise)))
    covariance_model <- "full"
  }
  structure <- .multilpa_resolve_structure(variance_model, covariance_model,
                                           volume, shape, orientation)
  # An ellipsoidal structure has an orientation, which a diagonal parameter
  # block cannot carry, so the fit keeps a full covariance array whatever
  # `covariance_model` said.
  if (.multilpa_is_ellipsoidal(structure)) covariance_model <- "full"
  # The four structures the package has always fitted are maximized by the
  # `variance_model` branch of the M-step rather than by a constrained solver,
  # so reaching one of them through `volume`/`shape`/`orientation` has to set
  # it. Without this, asking for EEI by its pieces reported EEI and counted its
  # parameters while fitting free per-profile variances.
  if (structure %in% c("EEI", "EEE")) variance_model <- "equal"
  if (structure %in% c("VVI", "VVV")) variance_model <- "varying"
  search <- search %||%
    .latents_default_search(structure, setdiff(vars, c(categorical, ordinal, count)))
  # Direct effects are checked here, before the covariate and transition
  # engines take over: those engines do not fit them.
  direct_terms <- NULL
  if (length(direct_effects) > 0L) {
    direct_terms <- .latents_parse_direct_effects(direct_effects)
    .latents_check_direct_conflicts(c(
      "a covariance structure other than EEI or VVI" = !structure %in% c("EEI", "VVI"),
      "`local_dependence` between continuous indicators" = length(local_dependence) > 0L,
      "`profile_covariates` or `group_covariates`" =
        length(profile_covariates) > 0L || length(group_covariates) > 0L,
      "`time`" = !is.null(time), "`prior`" = !is.null(prior),
      "`noise`" = isTRUE(noise),
      "`fixed` or `start`" = length(fixed) > 0L || !is.null(start),
      "`centering` or `scaling`" = !identical(centering[[1L]], "none") ||
        !identical(scaling[[1L]], "none")))
  }
  # Counted across every M-step of every start, and reported once at the end.
  .multilpa_reset_structure_log()
  report_structure <- TRUE
  on.exit(if (report_structure) .multilpa_report_structure_log(), add = TRUE)
  if (!structure %in% .multilpa_separable_structures() &&
      any(c("variances", "measurement") %in% fixed)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "A constrained covariance structure is maximized across every profile at",
      "once, so holding one profile's variances would not leave the others at",
      "their maximum. Use `fixed = \"means\"`, or the unconstrained structure."),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  .multilpa_check_prior(prior, structure, categorical, fixed,
                        length(profile_covariates) + length(group_covariates))
  .multilpa_check_noise(noise, n_group_classes, categorical, fixed,
                        length(profile_covariates) + length(group_covariates))
  if (!is.null(weights)) {
    if (!is.null(prior)) .latents_refuse_weights("`prior`")
    if (isTRUE(noise)) .latents_refuse_weights("`noise = TRUE`")
  }
  .latents_check_extra_arguments(vars, categorical, ordinal, count, list(
    "`prior`" = !is.null(prior), "`noise = TRUE`" = isTRUE(noise),
    "`fixed`" = length(fixed) > 0L, "`start`" = !is.null(start)))
  if (length(profile_covariates) > 0L || length(group_covariates) > 0L) {
    # The covariate model is fitted through `variance_model` and
    # `covariance_model` alone, which reach these four structures only; any
    # other used to be fitted silently as the nearest of them.
    if (!structure %in% c("EEI", "VVI", "EEE", "VVV")) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "The covariance structure \"%s\" is not available with",
        "`profile_covariates` or `group_covariates`, which fit EEI, VVI, EEE",
        "and VVV only. Fit the covariate-free model with this structure and use",
        "three_step() or r3step(), or choose one of the four."), structure),
        class = "latents_unsupported_structure", call = NULL))
    }
    result <- .multilpa_covariate_model(
      data = data, vars = vars, id = id, n_profiles = n_profiles,
      n_group_classes = n_group_classes,
      profile_covariates = profile_covariates,
      group_covariates = group_covariates, variance_model = variance_model,
      n_starts = n_starts, max_iter = max_iter, tol = tol,
      min_variance = min_variance, seed = seed, start = start,
      missing = missing, profile_slopes = profile_slopes,
      covariance_model = covariance_model,
      categorical = categorical, min_probability = min_probability,
      time = time, fixed = fixed, select_start = select_start, boundary = boundary,
      call = call,
      weights = weights, ordinal = ordinal, count = count,
      count_model = count_model, count_dispersion = count_dispersion,
      centering = centering, scaling = scaling, drop_empty = drop_empty,
      search = search, n_screen = n_screen)
    result$single_level <- single_level
    return(result)
  }
  # The data contract comes first: `time` is checked against the `id` column,
  # so an `id` that does not name a column of `data` must be reported as
  # that, not as an opaque failure inside the time check.
  .multilpa_check_arguments(data, vars, id, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                          n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance, min_probability,
                          seed, categorical)
  time_values <- .multilpa_time_values(data, time, id, vars)
  measurement <- .multilpa_prepare_indicators(data, vars, categorical,
                                            missing, min_probability,
                                            other = c(ordinal, count))
  extra <- .latents_set_count_model(
    .latents_prepare_extra(data, ordinal, count, missing), count_model, count_dispersion)
  if (!is.null(direct_terms)) {
    extra <- .latents_add_direct(extra, .latents_prepare_direct(
      data, direct_terms, vars, measurement$continuous))
  }
  continuous <- measurement$continuous
  indicator_frame <- measurement$frame
  encoded <- measurement$encoded
  codes <- measurement$codes
  n_categories <- measurement$n_categories
  x <- measurement$x
  groups <- .multilpa_prepare_groups(data[[id]])
  group_values <- groups$values
  group_index <- groups$index
  group_ids <- groups$ids
  n_groups <- groups$n
  sampling_weights <- .latents_sampling_weights(data, weights, group_index, n_groups)
  # Centring happens here, between validating the indicators and fitting them,
  # so the measurement model sees deviations and every verb downstream can put
  # a supplied frame on the same scale from the offsets kept on the fit.
  centred <- .multilpa_center_indicators(x, group_index, n_groups, centering,
                                         scaling)
  if ((!identical(centering, "none") || !identical(scaling, "none")) &&
      ncol(x) > 0L) {
    .multilpa_check_centered(centred$x, centering, raw = x,
                             group_index = group_index)
    x <- centred$x
    indicator_frame <- as.data.frame(x)
  }
  group_sizes <- groups$sizes
  distinct_rows <- nrow(unique(cbind(x, codes, .latents_extra_matrix(extra))))
  if (n_profiles > distinct_rows) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "n_profiles cannot exceed the number of distinct observed indicator rows.",
      class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (n_group_classes > n_groups) {
    stop(errorCondition("n_group_classes cannot exceed the number of groups.",
                        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (n_group_classes > 1L && (n_profiles == 1L || all(group_sizes == 1L))) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "Multiple group classes are not identifiable with one profile or only singleton groups.",
      class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (length(fixed) > 0L) {
    start <- .multilpa_complete_start(start, n_profiles, n_group_classes)
  }
  # `fixed` is checked against the start before the start's own shape is, so
  # that a request to hold a block the start does not carry is reported as
  # that, rather than as a generic complaint about the start's contents.
  fixed <- .multilpa_validate_fixed(fixed, start, covariance_model, ncol(x),
                                    n_categories)
  # A noise start carries its proportion beside the profile probabilities;
  # it is taken out here so the ordinary validation sees the ordinary shape.
  noise_start <- NULL
  if (isTRUE(noise) && !is.null(start)) {
    split_start <- .multilpa_noise_start(start)
    start <- split_start$start
    noise_start <- split_start$noise_probability
  }
  if (!is.null(start)) {
    start <- .multilpa_validate_start(start, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                                    ncol(x), variance_model, min_variance,
                                    covariance_model, n_categories, min_probability,
                                    categorical, encoded$levels)
  }
  .latents_local_seed(seed)
  # Center to reduce cancellation in weighted means when indicators have large
  # offsets. This is a translation, with no density Jacobian or scale change.
  centers <- .multilpa_initialization_center(x, sampling_weights[group_index])
  x <- sweep(x, 2L, centers, "-")
  # Direct effects are fitted on centred covariates too: an intercept and the
  # effect of a covariate far from zero are nearly collinear, which makes the
  # conditional M-steps crawl (4911 EM iterations for a covariate centred at
  # 41, against 21 at 1). The model is the same; the means are moved back to
  # a covariate value of zero after EM.
  fitting_extra <- .latents_center_direct(extra, x, sampling_weights[group_index])
  if (any(!is.finite(x[!is.na(x)]^2))) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "Indicator scales overflow squared residuals; rescale the data.",
      class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  if (!is.null(start)) start$means <- sweep(start$means, 2L, centers, "-")
  held <- .multilpa_held_parameters(start, fixed, covariance_model)
  # The prior is resolved on the indicators the EM sees, so its default mean is
  # their (centred) column means and a supplied mean moves with the centring.
  prior_parameters <- if (is.null(prior)) NULL else {
    if (anyNA(x)) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "`prior` is defined for complete indicators, as in mclust; these have",
        "missing values. Drop `prior`, or use complete rows."),
        class = "latents_unsupported_prior", call = NULL))
    }
    .multilpa_prior_parameters(prior, x, n_profiles, structure, offset = centers)
  }
  # The noise component's density is the reciprocal of mclust's hypervolume of
  # the data, which a translation does not change.
  noise_log_density <- if (isTRUE(noise)) {
    if (anyNA(x)) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "A noise component is a uniform density over the complete indicator",
        "space, as in mclust; these indicators have missing values."),
        class = "latents_unsupported_noise", call = NULL))
    }
    -.multilpa_log_hypervolume(x)
  } else NULL
  # `max_iter = 0` performs no update, so a restart cannot improve on anything:
  # scoring extra random initializations and keeping the highest would return a
  # parameter set nobody supplied in place of the one the caller asked to have
  # evaluated. Evaluate-only with a `start` therefore uses that start alone, and
  # `get_results(fit, "starts")` shows the single start that was run.
  if (max_iter == 0L && !is.null(start)) n_starts <- 1L
  # Under emEM a pool is screened and the best `n_starts` are run to the end;
  # the pool's first `n_starts` starts are the kmeans search's own, drawn in
  # the same order, so emEM considers every start that search would run.
  screen <- .latents_search_screen(search, n_starts, n_screen, max_iter,
                                   supplied = !is.null(start))
  start_kind <- function(start_index) .latents_start_kind(start_index, n_starts)
  # Each start runs to completion or is recorded as failed; the best is
  # chosen by the shared rule (see .latents_run_starts()).
  prepare <- function(start_index) {
    initial <- if (start_index == 1L && !is.null(start)) start else {
      # The first start is Ward's hierarchical clustering, deterministic
      # and good at profiles that differ in shape; the rest are k-means
      # from random centres, and in an emEM pool random partitions and
      # random centres after those.
      .multilpa_initialize(x, group_index, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                         variance_model, min_variance, start_index,
                         covariance_model, codes, n_categories, min_probability,
                         hierarchical = start_index == 1L, extra = fitting_extra,
                         kind = start_kind(start_index),
                         row_weights = sampling_weights[group_index])
    }
    # Every restart begins from the held values, so a random start cannot
    # report a measurement solution that was neither estimated nor supplied.
    initial <- .multilpa_apply_held(initial, held)
    initial <- .multilpa_project_start(initial, structure, nrow(x), min_variance)
    # A random start begins with a tenth of the mass on the noise component;
    # a supplied start with the proportion it supplied.
    if (!is.null(noise_log_density)) {
      initial <- .multilpa_add_noise(
        initial,
        if (start_index == 1L && !is.null(noise_start)) noise_start else 0.1,
        noise_log_density)
    }
    initial
  }
  initial <- .latents_prepare_starts(
    if (is.null(screen)) n_starts else screen$n_pool, prepare)
  context <- as.list(environment())
  context[c("prepare", "start_kind", "initial")] <- NULL
  plan <- .lta_plan(context, initial, .multilpa_run_start, .multilpa_finalise,
    c("x", "group_index", "variance_model", "min_variance", "max_iter", "tol",
      "covariance_model", "codes", "n_categories", "min_probability", "held",
      "structure", "prior_parameters", "acceleration", "sampling_weights",
      "fitting_extra", "covariance_pattern"))
  plan$interior <- if (exclude_boundary) .lta_bind_context(
    .multilpa_start_interior, list(min_variance = min_variance))
  plan$cores <- cores
  class(plan) <- "latents_multilpa_plan"
  report_structure <- FALSE
  plan
}

review_record.name: .latents_warn_thin_profiles
review_record.purpose: Warn when a profile has fewer members than its own parameters  This is a conservative membership-versus-parameter heuristic for profiles with class-specific spread. It is not a rank or identification test: positive soft memberships can yield full-rank covariance at arbitrarily small total mass, and a larger profile can be nearly flat. Under sampling weights the membership is normalized mass, not an independent sample count. The estimate is unchanged; continuous covariance diagnostics are reported separately without using a rejection threshold.

review_record.name: .multilpa_covariate_model
review_record.purpose: Hand a covariate request to the covariate estimator  `multilpa()` is one verb over one model, and membership covariates are part of that model rather than a different one, so they are arguments and not a separate entry point. Two of `multilpa()`'s own arguments have no meaning on this path: the covariate likelihood has no starting-value contract of the shape the covariate-free EM uses, and no held-measurement machinery. Each is refused by name instead of being accepted and ignored, which would return a fit that is not the one asked for. `missing = "fiml"` is supported: the measurement density is the covariate-free model's observed-data one.

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_covariate_model <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles,
                                      n_group_classes, profile_covariates,
                                      group_covariates, variance_model,
                                      n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance,
                                      seed, start, missing,
                                      profile_slopes = "shared", covariance_model,
                                      categorical, min_probability, time,
                                      fixed, select_start = "likelihood",
                                      boundary = "allow",
                                      call, weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                                      count = character(), count_model = "poisson",
                                      count_dispersion = "varying",
                                      centering = "none", scaling = "none",
                                      drop_empty = TRUE, search = "kmeans",
                                      n_screen = NULL) {
  unsupported <- c(
    start = !is.null(start),
    fixed = length(fixed) > 0L)
  if (any(unsupported)) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "%s cannot be combined with `profile_covariates` or",
      "`group_covariates`. Fit the covariate model without %s, or fit the",
      "covariate-free model and use three_step() or r3step()."),
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", names(unsupported)[unsupported]), collapse = ", "),
      if (sum(unsupported) > 1L) "them" else "it"),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  .multilpa_fit_covariates(
    data = data, vars = vars, id = id, n_profiles = n_profiles,
    n_group_classes = n_group_classes,
    profile_covariates = profile_covariates,
    group_covariates = group_covariates, variance_model = variance_model,
    n_starts = n_starts, max_iter = max_iter, tol = tol,
    min_variance = min_variance, seed = seed, time = time,
    covariance_model = covariance_model, categorical = categorical,
    min_probability = min_probability, missing = missing,
    profile_slopes = profile_slopes, select_start = select_start,
    boundary = boundary, call = call,
    weights = weights, ordinal = ordinal, count = count,
    count_model = count_model, count_dispersion = count_dispersion,
    centering = centering, scaling = scaling, drop_empty = drop_empty,
    search = search, n_screen = n_screen)
}

.multilpa_split_noise <- function(parameters, posteriors) {
  last <- ncol(posteriors)
  gaussian <- seq_len(last - 1L)
  noise_probability <- parameters$profile_probabilities[1L, last]
  parameters$profile_probabilities <-
    parameters$profile_probabilities[, gaussian, drop = FALSE]
  parameters$noise_log_density <- NULL
  list(parameters = parameters,
       posteriors = posteriors[, gaussian, drop = FALSE],
       noise_probability = unname(noise_probability),
       noise_posteriors = unname(posteriors[, last]),
       classes = {
         modal <- max.col(posteriors, ties.method = "first")
         modal[modal == last] <- 0L
         modal
       })
}

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.latents_windows_alive <- function(pids) {
  stopifnot("pids are numeric" = is.numeric(pids))
  unknown <- rep(NA, length(pids))
  # Nonzero exit status and malformed PIDs are diagnosed as unknown below.
  listing <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch( # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.
    system2("tasklist", c("/FO", "CSV", "/NH"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE),
    error = function(condition) NULL))
  if (!length(listing) || !is.null(attr(listing, "status")) &&
      attr(listing, "status") != 0L) return(unknown)
  processes <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(text = listing, header = FALSE,
    colClasses = "character", stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    error = function(condition) NULL)
  if (is.null(processes) || ncol(processes) < 2L) return(unknown)
  running <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(processes[[2L]])) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.
  if (anyNA(running) || !length(running)) return(unknown)
  pids %in% running
}

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.latents_make_cluster <- function(cores) {
  cluster <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(cores)
  registered <- FALSE
  on.exit(if (!registered) .latents_stop_cluster(cluster), add = TRUE)
  pids <- unlist(parallel::clusterCall(cluster, Sys.getpid), use.names = FALSE)
  if (is.null(pids)) pids <- integer()
  stopifnot("one positive worker PID per socket node" =
              is.numeric(pids) && length(pids) == length(cluster) &&
              all(is.finite(pids) & pids > 0 & pids == as.integer(pids)))
  attr(cluster, "latents_pids") <- as.integer(pids[pids != Sys.getpid()])
  registered <- TRUE
  cluster
}

review_record.name: .latents_socket_pass
review_record.purpose: Run bounded socket chunks while retaining completed chunks  The exported parallel API returns no partial results when parLapplyLB loses a connection. review_record.name: .latents_map_candidates
review_record.purpose: Apply `fun` to candidates or starts in a shared worker pool  With several cores, tasks use dynamically assigned forked processes where the platform allows them, or a load-balanced socket cluster on Windows and on macOS with Accelerate's BLAS (`.latents_fork_safe()`). Optional costs send the longest estimated tasks first. Results and conditions retain the order of `indices`, independently of dispatch or completion order. Conditions retain their classes and can instead be returned for later signalling.  Missing worker results are retried once using half as many fork workers, rounded up, or one socket worker to isolate repeated losses. A classed warning reports process losses and recovery. Socket calls use bounded chunks because the exported parallel API cannot retain results from within a call whose connection breaks; previously completed chunks survive.

review_record.name: prior_control
review_record.purpose: Specify a conjugate prior for Gaussian mixture estimation  Returns a `latents_prior` object requesting maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation of the Gaussian profile means and covariances under the conjugate prior of Fraley and Raftery (2007), as `mclust::priorControl()` does for `mclust::Mclust()`. Pass the result as `multilpa(prior = )`. The prior keeps the covariance estimates away from singularity.  Every argument left `NULL` takes `mclust::defaultPrior()`'s value, computed from the indicators being fitted: the prior mean is their column means, the degrees of freedom are `d + 2` for `d` indicators, and the scale is `(1/G)^(2/d)` times the sample covariance (ellipsoidal structures) or times the average sample variance (axis-parallel and spherical structures), for `G` profiles.  The updates follow mclust's fitted-model convention, including its structure-specific departures from a textbook conjugate update, so the controls have different effects across covariance structures. For `EII`, `scale` does not enter the variance update. For `EEI`, `shrinkage` and `mean` enter the variance calculation but do not shrink the fitted means. For `VEV`, `dof` does not enter the update. `EEI`, `EVI` and `EEV` count the mean-prior contribution once rather than once per profile.

inputs.defaults_source: pairlist(shrinkage = 0.01, mean = NULL, dof = NULL, scale = NULL)

documented_parameters.shrinkage: Non-negative prior precision factor for the means, `kappa`   (default `0.01`, as in mclust). Zero leaves the means unshrunk.
documented_parameters.mean: Optional prior mean, one value per continuous indicator, on the   scale the profile means are estimated on: the indicators' own units, or   their centred values under [multilpa()]'s `centering`. Requires a positive   `shrinkage`.
documented_parameters.dof: Optional prior degrees of freedom, a single positive number.
documented_parameters.scale: Optional prior scale: a single positive number for an   axis-parallel or spherical structure, or a positive-definite `d` by `d`   matrix for an ellipsoidal one.

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_group_scores <- function(theta, x, object, codes = NULL) {
  stopifnot("`theta` must be numeric" = is.numeric(theta),
            "`x` must be a numeric matrix" = is.matrix(x) && is.numeric(x),
            "`object` must be an `multilpa` fit" = inherits(object, "multilpa"))
  parameters <- .multilpa_decode(theta, object)
  group_index <- object$group_index
  expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(x, group_index, parameters, codes,
                                       unname(object$sampling_weights),
                                       object$extra_data)
  n_profiles <- object$n_profiles
  n_types <- object$n_group_classes
  measurement <- if (.multilpa_uses_chart(object)) {
    .multilpa_chart_scores(
      parameters, expectation, x, object,
      theta[length(parameters$means) +
              seq_len(.multilpa_coordinate_widths(object, "unconstrained")[["variances"]])],
      group_index)
  } else if (identical(object$covariance_model, "full")) {
    .multilpa_full_measurement_group_score(parameters, expectation, object)
  } else {
    shifted <- .latents_direct_shift(x, object$extra_data, parameters)
    observed <- !is.na(x)
    blocks <- lapply(seq_len(n_profiles), function(profile) {
      residuals <- sweep(shifted, 2L, parameters$means[profile, ], "-")
      residuals[!observed] <- 0
      weights <- expectation$subject_posteriors[, profile]
      list(
        means = rowsum(sweep(residuals, 2L, parameters$variances[profile, ], "/") *
                         weights, group_index, reorder = FALSE),
        variances = rowsum(0.5 * (sweep(residuals^2, 2L,
          parameters$variances[profile, ], "/") - observed) * weights,
          group_index, reorder = FALSE))
    })
    variances <- if (object$variance_model == "equal") {
      Reduce(`+`, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "variances"))
    } else do.call(cbind, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "variances"))
    list(means = do.call(cbind, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "means")),
         covariances = variances)
  }
  # Each group class contributes its own multinomial score for the profile
  # proportions, with the final profile as the omitted reference category.
  profile_scores <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(group_type) {
    counts <- rowsum(expectation$joint[[group_type]], group_index, reorder = FALSE)
    expected <- outer(rowSums(counts), parameters$profile_probabilities[group_type, ])
    (counts - expected)[, seq_len(n_profiles - 1L), drop = FALSE]
  }))
  # A weighted posterior row sums to its unit's weight, so the expected count
  # is that weight times the class probabilities; unweighted, it is one.
  group_scores <- (expectation$group_posteriors -
    outer(rowSums(expectation$group_posteriors),
          parameters$group_probabilities))[, seq_len(n_types - 1L), drop = FALSE]
  response_scores <- .multilpa_response_scores(
    codes, expectation$subject_posteriors, parameters$response_probabilities,
    group_index)
  extra_scores <- .latents_extra_scores(object$extra_data,
                                        expectation$subject_posteriors,
                                        parameters, group_index, x = x)
  scores <- cbind(measurement$means, measurement$covariances, response_scores,
                  extra_scores, profile_scores, group_scores)
  dimnames(scores) <- list(object$group_ids, names(theta))
  scores
}

review_record.name: .multilpa_design_scale
review_record.purpose: Column scales that make an optimization coordinate unit-free  A multinomial logit is a parameterization of the same model under any linear rescaling of a predictor: multiplying a covariate by `c` and its coefficient by `1/c` leaves every fitted probability alone. A quasi-Newton search is not invariant in that way, because it stops on a relative tolerance measured in the coordinates it was handed. A column whose units are `1e-7` times those of the rest therefore stalls the search while the score is still large, and the optimizer still reports success.  The root-mean-square of a column is exactly proportional to that column's units, so dividing each column by it gives a design matrix that does not change when a predictor is rescaled. Fitting in those coordinates and dividing the coefficients back by the same scales returns estimates in the user's units while making the search itself unit-free.

mathematical_conventions.formula_or_effect_source:
.multilpa_design_scale <- function(design) {
  stopifnot(
    "`design` must be a numeric matrix" =
      is.matrix(design) && is.numeric(design),
    "`design` must be finite" = all(is.finite(design)))
  if (ncol(design) == 0L) return(numeric(0))
  ## The peak comes out first so that squaring a column held in very large
  ## units cannot overflow to `Inf` before the mean is taken.
  peak <- apply(abs(design), 2L, max)
  safe <- ifelse(is.finite(peak) & peak > 0, peak, 1)
  scale <- safe * sqrt(colMeans(sweep(design, 2L, safe, "/")^2))
  unname(ifelse(is.finite(scale) & scale > 0, scale, 1))
}

review_record.name: .multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale
review_record.purpose: Scales for the log-Cholesky coordinates of a residual covariance  The unrestricted residual covariance is estimated through the lower triangle of its Cholesky factor, with the diagonal logged. Those coordinates do not share one unit: a logged diagonal entry is dimensionless, while an off-diagonal entry `L[i, j]` carries the units of indicator `i`. Handing them to a finite-difference Hessian unscaled makes the information matrix's condition number grow with the square of the indicator units, and it is then declared singular for no reason but the units the data arrived in.  This is the general form of the scaling [parameter_inference()] already applies to a covariate-free `multilpa` fit (R/inference.R), written so that the covariate path can share it instead of rediscovering it.

documented_parameters.rows: Integer indices of the rows of `variances` whose spread block is   estimated separately: every profile under a varying spread, `1L` when one   block is shared.

.multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale <- function(variances, dimension, rows) {
  stopifnot(
    "`variances` must be a numeric matrix" =
      is.matrix(variances) && is.numeric(variances),
    "`dimension` must be a single non-negative whole number" =
      is.numeric(dimension) && length(dimension) == 1L && is.finite(dimension) &&
      dimension >= 0 && dimension == as.integer(dimension),
    "`variances` must have at least `dimension` columns" =
      ncol(variances) >= dimension,
    "`rows` must index rows of `variances`" =
      is.numeric(rows) && length(rows) >= 1L && all(is.finite(rows)) &&
      all(rows >= 1L) && all(rows <= nrow(variances)),
    "`variances` must be positive" = all(variances > 0))
  if (dimension == 0L) return(numeric(0))
  positions <- which(lower.tri(matrix(0, dimension, dimension), diag = TRUE),
                     arr.ind = TRUE)
  unlist(lapply(rows, function(profile) {
    ifelse(positions[, 1L] == positions[, 2L], 1,
           sqrt(variances[profile, positions[, 1L]]))
  }), use.names = FALSE)
}

review_record.name: .latents_default_search
review_record.purpose: The default start search of a profile model  When every profile shares one covariance matrix (EII, EEI, EEE), the likelihood is bounded: no profile can collapse onto a point without lowering the density of every other (McLachlan & Peel, 2000, section 3.8). A higher maximum is then a better estimate, never a degenerate one, so the screened emEM search, which reaches more of them, is the default. With profile-specific covariances a higher maximum can be such a collapse, and the kmeans search stays the default.

review_record.documentation_contract: The default start search of a profile model  When every profile shares one covariance matrix (EII, EEI, EEE), the likelihood is bounded: no profile can collapse onto a point without lowering the density of every other (McLachlan & Peel, 2000, section 3.8). A higher maximum is then a better estimate, never a degenerate one, so the screened emEM search, which reaches more of them, is the default. With profile-specific covariances a higher maximum can be such a collapse, and the kmeans search stays the default.  @param structure The resolved covariance structure code. @param continuous The continuous indicators. @return `"emEM"` or `"kmeans"`. @noRd

.latents_refit_controls <- function(model, n_starts = NULL, max_iter = NULL,
                                    tol = NULL) {
  recorded <- !is.null(model$search)
  starts <- as.integer(n_starts %||% (if (recorded) model$n_starts) %||% 10L)
  search <- model$search %||% "kmeans"
  # A changed number of starts takes the default pool for that number.
  n_screen <- if (identical(search, "emEM") &&
                  identical(starts, as.integer(model$n_starts))) model$n_screen
  list(search = search, n_starts = starts, n_screen = n_screen,
       max_iter = as.integer(max_iter %||% (if (recorded) model$max_iter) %||% 1000L),
       tol = tol %||% (if (recorded) model$tol) %||% 1e-8,
       acceleration = model$acceleration %||% "squarem",
       select_start = model$select_start %||% "likelihood",
       boundary = model$boundary_policy %||% "allow")
}

.latents_pool_phase <- function(tasks, costs, cores, n_candidates,
                                  execute, on_lost = NULL) {
  candidate <- vapply(tasks, `[[`, integer(1), "candidate")
  results <- if (length(tasks)) .latents_map_candidates(
    tasks, execute, cores, costs = costs[candidate], signal = FALSE,
    on_lost = on_lost) else list()
  lapply(seq_len(n_candidates), function(i) results[candidate == i])
}

review_record.name: .multilpa_select_start
review_record.purpose: Choose the start a fit reports  Restarts of a mixture routinely reach the same optimum under different label permutations, and then differ only in the last bits of the likelihood. Picking by `which.max()` alone makes the reported labelling turn on floating-point noise, so the maximum is taken up to a relative tolerance far below any difference that could matter, a converged start is preferred among those tied, and then the earliest.

inputs.defaults_source: as.pairlist(alist(log_likelihood = , converged = , rule = c("likelihood", "converged"), interior = NULL))

documented_parameters.log_likelihood: Numeric vector, one entry per start; `-Inf` for a   start that failed.
documented_parameters.converged: Logical vector of the same length.
documented_parameters.rule: `"likelihood"` takes the highest likelihood whether or not that   start converged. `"converged"` takes the highest likelihood among the   converged starts, falling back to every start when none converged.
documented_parameters.interior: `NULL`, or a logical vector of the same length flagging   the starts with no variance at its lower bound. When supplied, only those   starts are candidates, and the rule chooses among them; when none is   flagged, every start is, with a `latents_all_starts_boundary` warning.

guard_expressions:
stopifnot(`\`log_likelihood\` must be numeric` = is.numeric(log_likelihood), `\`converged\` must be logical and match \`log_likelihood\`` = is.logical(converged) && 
    length(converged) == length(log_likelihood), `at least one start must have a finite likelihood` = any(is.finite(log_likelihood)), 
    `\`interior\` must be NULL or logical and match \`log_likelihood\`` = is.null(interior) || (is.logical(interior) && length(interior) == 
        length(log_likelihood) && !anyNA(interior)))
inputs.interpretation: Formal/default and guard syntax are read from the current parsed body. Documentation describes the intended contract; implicit callee requirements are not claimed exhaustively validated.

outputs.documented_return: A single integer index.

review_record.name: mixture_regression
review_record.purpose: Fit a finite mixture of regressions  Fits a regression whose coefficients differ across `n_classes` latent classes and returns the fitted model: the class-specific regressions, the class sizes and every row's posterior class membership, estimated jointly by maximum likelihood.

input_contract.signature_source:
mixture_regression <- function(formula, data, n_classes,
                   family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial",
                              "ordinal"),
                   id = NULL, class_level = c("observation", "group"),
                   n_group_classes = 1L, common = NULL, membership = ~1,
                   group_membership = ~1, variance = c("varying", "equal"),
                   n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 1000L, tol = 1e-8,
                   min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL,
                   missing = c("error", "omit"),
                   select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                   vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg", "none"),
                   weights = NULL, random = NULL,
                   random_covariance = c("varying", "equal", "proportional"),
                   random_diagonal = FALSE, cluster = NULL,
                   residual_correlation = c("none", "ar", "brownian"),
                   residual_time = NULL)

parameter_descriptions.declared_description: A model formula `outcome ~ predictors`. Factors, interactions   and `offset()` are supported.
`NULL` (default), or the name of the column identifying groups   (persons, schools, ...).
`"observation"` (default; each row has its own class) or   `"group"` (all rows of a group share a class; requires `id`).
Number of second-level group classes (default 1,   no second level), for `class_level = "observation"` with `id`, or for the   clusters of a multilevel growth mixture (`cluster`).
`NULL`, or the predictor terms whose coefficients are   shared by every class: variable names such as `"age"`, or a one-sided   formula such as `~ age`. Each term must appear in `formula`.

Covariates predicting class membership (a multinomial   logit, the first class as the reference): variable names such as   `"age"`, or a one-sided formula (`~ 1`, the default, for none).   Row-level for `"observation"`; constant within groups for `"group"`.
Group-level covariates predicting the group class,   for the two-level model, as names or a one-sided formula. Must be   constant within groups.
`"varying"` (default; a residual standard deviation, or a   negative-binomial dispersion, per class) or `"equal"` (one shared).   Gaussian and negative-binomial families only.

Number of random starts (default 10), besides one start   built from the residuals of a pooled regression. Every start runs up to   50 EM iterations; the better half (at least two) continue to   convergence.
Relative convergence tolerance on the log likelihood (default   `1e-8`).
Floor for a Gaussian residual variance, relative to the   outcome's variance (default `1e-6`). Starts in which a class reaches the   floor (fits too few rows exactly) are set aside.
`NULL` (default) or an integer seed. The caller's random state   is restored afterwards.
`"error"` (default) refuses rows with missing values in any   variable the model uses; `"omit"` drops them with a   `latents_rows_dropped` warning stating how many.
`"likelihood"` (default) keeps the start with the   highest likelihood; `"converged"` prefers the best start that converged.

Covariance of the estimates stored with the fit:   `"observed"` (default; inverse observed information), `"robust"` (sandwich with   the CR1 factor `G / (G - 1)`, clustered on the top-level unit, or on `id` for a single-level fit given   `id`) or `"opg"` (outer product of the scores). `"none"` skips inference.

`NULL`, or the name of a numeric column of `data` with a   sampling weight per independent unit: per row without `id`, per `id`   group otherwise (constant within it). Pseudo maximum likelihood with the   weights scaled to sum to the number of units; `vcov_type` defaults to   `"robust"` and refuses `"observed"` and `"opg"`. The information   criteria use the weighted log likelihood; the entropy term of ICL sums   the units' own posteriors unweighted, as in the profile models.

`NULL` (default; no random effects), or the random effects   within classes: variable names such as `"time"` (a random intercept and   a random slope on `time`) or `"intercept"` (random intercepts only), or a   one-sided formula such as `~ 1 + time`. A slope without a random   intercept needs the formula `~ 0 + time`. See *Growth mixture models*.

How the random-effect covariance differs across   classes: `"varying"` (default; one per class), `"equal"` (one shared matrix, as   `lcmm::hlme()` with `nwg = FALSE`) or `"proportional"` (a shared matrix   times a class-specific scale, the last class's being one; `nwg = TRUE`).
`TRUE` for uncorrelated random effects (a diagonal   covariance, as `idiag = TRUE` in lcmm); default `FALSE`.

`NULL` (default), or the name of a column grouping the   persons (`id`) into clusters, such as schools, for the multilevel growth   mixture model (with `random`): each cluster belongs to one of   `n_group_classes` group classes, which sets the trajectory-class   probabilities of its persons. The clusters are the independent units of   the likelihood, the standard errors and the BIC; with   `n_group_classes = 1` the model is the single-level growth mixture with   clusters as those units, comparable by BIC with fits with more group   classes. See *Growth mixture models*.

`"none"` (default) for independent residuals   within a person; with `random`, `"ar"` adds a continuous-time   autoregressive process, covariance `sd^2 exp(-rate |t - s|)`, and   `"brownian"` Brownian motion, `sd^2 min(t, s)`, to the residual   variance, shared by the classes: `lcmm::hlme(cor = AR(time))` and   `cor = BM(time)`. The model without the process is fitted first from   every start; the process is then estimated jointly with all other   parameters. A process the data cannot separate from the residual variance or the   random effects is left on its bound and warned about   (`latents_random_boundary`); its rows then have no standard error.   Refused with `latents_bad_argument` without `random`.
The numeric column the process runs over; by default   the first numeric variable of `random`, or else of the predictors.   Brownian motion needs non-negative times (`latents_bad_data`).

review_record.name: lta
review_record.purpose: Fit a latent transition model  Fits latent profiles to repeated observations of the same group, estimates the probabilities of moving between profiles from one occasion to the next, and returns a `multilpa_transitions` (or `multilpa_lta`) object.

input_contract.signature_source:
lta <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles, time,
                            n_group_classes = 1L,
                            variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
                            n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 5000L, tol = 1e-10,
                            min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL,
                            missing = c("error", "fiml"),
                            covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
                            categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10,
                            occasions = c("observed", "grid"),
                            select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                            transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"),
                            transition_covariates = character(),
                            initial_covariates = character(),
                            measurement = c("invariant", "occasion"),
                            order = 1L, model = NULL, mover_stayer = FALSE,
                            weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                            count = character(),
                            count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
                            count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
                            drop_empty = TRUE, search = c("kmeans", "emEM"),
                            n_screen = NULL,
                            acceleration = c("squarem", "none"), cores = 1L)

parameter_descriptions.declared_description: How the starts are found: `"kmeans"` (the default) or   `"emEM"`, as described for [multilpa()]. Unlike [multilpa()], `lta()`   does not choose its default by the covariance structure.

Number of processor cores for the random starts (default 1).   The starting values are drawn in order in the current process and only   the EM runs are distributed, so with `seed` given the result is identical   to `cores = 1`. Under `search = "emEM"` both screening and the final runs   are distributed. Workers are forked processes on macOS and Linux, and a   socket cluster on Windows and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, as   in [enumerate_classes()]. Lost worker results are retried once with half   as many workers (rounded up), with one `latents_worker_lost` warning   reporting losses and recovery and suggesting fewer cores. A start still   lost is recorded as failed; the fit uses the remaining starts. If all   starts fail, the usual `latents_all_starts_failed` error is raised.   Socket workers use bounded chunks; completed tasks within a failed chunk   may also be retried. To fit many models, give `cores` to   [enumerate_classes()], which runs starts across candidates in one pool.
Name of the observed group identifier column. Character, factor   and numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not.   Required; `id = NULL` is not accepted.
Integer number of individual profiles, at least two   (`latents_bad_transition` otherwise).

Name of the column giving each observation's occasion within   its group. Required. Values must be complete and unique within each   group. They are ordered as [sort()] orders them: numbers numerically, a   factor by its levels, and character strings alphabetically. Numbers   stored as text whose alphabetical order is not their numeric order   (`"2"`, `"10"`) raise `latents_bad_time` (also `latents_bad_data`);   zero-padded numbers and ISO dates are accepted.
Positive integer number of latent group classes   (default 1). One gives an ordinary latent transition model; more than one   fits a mixture of transition models over groups.

Which start the fit reports. `"likelihood"` (the   default) takes the highest log likelihood across starts, preferring a   converged start only among those within a relative `1e-10` of it.   `"converged"` takes the highest log likelihood among the converged starts   when at least one converged, and among all starts otherwise. The two   differ when an unconverged start exceeds a converged one by a negligible   amount, as happens when a membership logit drifts along a flat ridge of   the likelihood; only the converged start is a maximum on which standard   errors can be based. `summary()` and `get_results(fit, "starts")` show   every start.

How a group's occasions are placed on the transition grid.   `"observed"` (the default) numbers each group's own observations   consecutively, so a transition always links two adjacent observations.   `"grid"` places them on the grid of every position seen in the data, so a   group that skips a position still makes a transition across the gap and   contributes no measurement information at it. The two agree when every   group is observed at every position. Under either, a group's first   observation is its first occasion: occasion-specific transitions and   measurement count occasions from each group's own start, not from the   first position in the data.
`"homogeneous"` (the default) uses one transition matrix   for every occasion; `"occasion"` estimates a separate one for each move   (occasion 1 to 2, 2 to 3, ...).

Names of columns whose values shift the   transition probabilities through a multinomial logit per origin profile:   the log odds of moving to each other profile rather than staying. A   column may change over occasions; the value at the destination occasion   is used. Factors are expanded to indicator columns. With `occasions =   "grid"`, a move into a position the group skipped has no row to read the   covariates from, and the fit raises `latents_bad_data`; use   `occasions = "observed"`, or add the skipped rows with their covariate   values (their indicators may be missing under `missing = "fiml"`).
Names of columns that shift the initial profile   distribution (a multinomial logit, reference: the last profile), read at   each group's first occasion.
`"invariant"` (the default) keeps the profiles' means,   variances and response probabilities equal across occasions;   `"occasion"` estimates them separately at each occasion.

Positive relative log-likelihood tolerance (default `1e-10`,   tighter than the `1e-8` of [multilpa()]). Convergence requires an   absolute change no greater than `tol * (1 + abs(previous log likelihood))`.   The group-class shares are re-estimated from posteriors one EM step   behind them; at `1e-8` the two differed by up to about `2e-4`, at `1e-10`   by about `2e-5`, for roughly 1.5 times the iterations.

`"squarem"` (the default) accelerates EM with SQUAREM   (Varadhan & Roland, 2008), as [multilpa()] does: each cycle extrapolates   along the last two EM steps, including the initial and transition   probabilities, and ends with an ordinary EM step. An extrapolated point   that would lower the likelihood, or that leaves a probability   non-positive or a row not summing to one, is replaced by the plain EM   point, so the iteration stays monotone. Convergence is assessed over a   whole cycle, so it is never looser than plain EM's. Under the strict   default `tol` plain EM can creep along a flat likelihood for thousands of   steps; SQUAREM usually stops in far fewer, at the same or a slightly   higher maximum. `"none"` runs plain EM, which reproduces fits from   versions before this argument existed. `iterations` and `max_iter` count   EM steps under either setting.

Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start   (default 5000, higher than the 1000 of [multilpa()] to match the tighter   `tol`). A fit that stops short warns with `latents_unconverged`.   `max_iter = 0` updates nothing and evaluates the starting values.

`1` (the default) or `2`. With `2`, the profile at each   occasion from the third on depends on the profiles at the two previous   occasions (a second-order Markov chain); the first move stays first   order.

`FALSE` (the default), or `TRUE` to add a class of   stayers: groups that never change profile (identity transitions) and have   their own initial profile distribution (Goodman's mover-stayer model).   `n_group_classes` then counts the mover classes; the stayer class is   reported as `"stayers"`.

`NULL`, or the name of a column of `data` holding one   sampling weight per `id` (constant over its occasions). As in   [multilpa()]: pseudo maximum likelihood with the weights scaled to sum to   the number of `id` units, sandwich standard errors by default, and   integer weights equal to repeating each sequence. A weighted fit uses the   general transition engine and returns a `multilpa_lta`, whose   model-implied `"transitions"` and `"initial"` tables average the groups   with their weights.

Ordinal and count   indicators, as in [multilpa()]; with `measurement = "occasion"` their   parameters are estimated per occasion. Read them with   `get_results(fit, "ordinal")` and `get_results(fit, "count_means")`. A   fit with them uses the general transition engine.

A covariance structure as `multilpa()` takes it (`"EEI"`,   `"VVI"`, `"VEI"`, ... ; mclust's codes). Standard errors are given for   every structure with the extensions (covariate, occasion-varying or   second-order transitions, occasion-specific measurement), and for EEI,   VVI, EEE and VVV in the homogeneous model, which refuses the other ten   with `latents_unsupported_inference`.

.additive_unpack <- function(theta, n_classes, n_indicators, structure) {
  theta <- unname(theta)
  sizes <- n_indicators * c(.additive_rows(structure$means, n_classes),
                            .additive_rows(structure$within, n_classes),
                            .additive_rows(structure$between, n_classes))
  at <- cumsum(c(0L, sizes))
  block <- function(k) theta[seq.int(at[k] + 1L, length.out = sizes[k])]
  logits <- c(0, theta[-seq_len(at[4L])])
  list(means = .additive_block_unpack(block(1L), structure$means, n_classes,
                                      n_indicators),
       within = exp(.additive_block_unpack(block(2L), structure$within,
                                           n_classes, n_indicators)),
       between = exp(.additive_block_unpack(block(3L), structure$between,
                                            n_classes, n_indicators)),
       weights = exp(logits - max(logits)) / sum(exp(logits - max(logits))))
}

review_record.source_function:
.additive_group_scores <- function(stats, parameters, structure, class_names,
                                   vars) {
  parameters <- .additive_check_parameters(parameters, length(vars))
  expectation <- .additive_expectation(stats, parameters)
  # A weighted group's score is its weight times its own score.
  posterior <- expectation$posterior * (stats$sampling_weights %||% 1)
  n_classes <- nrow(parameters$means)
  j_count <- stats$n_groups
  pieces <- lapply(seq_len(n_classes), function(h) {
    within <- .additive_row(parameters$within, h, j_count)
    between <- .additive_row(parameters$between, h, j_count)
    deviation <- stats$averages - .additive_row(parameters$means, h, j_count)
    denominator <- within + stats$sizes * between
    weight <- posterior[, h]
    list(
      mean = weight * stats$sizes * deviation / denominator,
      log_within = weight * -0.5 * within *
        ((stats$sizes - 1) / within + 1 / denominator - stats$scatter / within^2 -
           stats$sizes * deviation^2 / denominator^2),
      log_between = weight * 0.5 * between * stats$sizes *
        (stats$sizes * deviation^2 / denominator^2 - 1 / denominator))
  })
  part <- function(name, mode) {
    .additive_block_combine(lapply(pieces, `[[`, name), mode)
  }
  logits <- posterior[, -1L, drop = FALSE] -
    outer(rowSums(posterior), parameters$weights[-1L])
  scores <- cbind(part("mean", structure$means),
                  part("log_within", structure$within),
                  part("log_between", structure$between), logits)
  dimnames(scores) <- list(stats$ids,
                           .additive_names(class_names, vars, structure))
  scores
}

.additive_information <- function(stats, theta, structure, class_names,
                                  vars, step) {

  total <- function(point) {
    colSums(.additive_group_scores(

      structure, class_names, vars))

  # The shared five-point score differences with h = step * max(1, |theta|):
  # -(c + t(c)) / 2 equals the former -((c + t(c)) / 2) exactly, since
  # negation and halving are exact.
  .inference_score_information(total, theta, step, scheme = "five_point",
                               h_rule = "max1")
}

.additive_inference <- function(x, vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg"),
                                step = 1e-4, warn_weak = TRUE) {
  vcov_type <- match.arg(vcov_type)
  stopifnot("`step` must be finite and positive" =
              is.numeric(step) && length(step) == 1L && is.finite(step) && step > 0)
  if (!isTRUE(x$converged)) {
    stop(errorCondition("Inference requires a converged fit.",
                        class = "latents_no_converge", call = NULL))
  }
  if (any(x$between_zero) || any(x$within_floor)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "A between-group variance is estimated at zero or a within-group variance",
      "sits at min_variance; the parameter is on the edge of its space and Wald",
      "inference does not apply."), class = "latents_boundary_fit", call = NULL))
  }
  if (any(x$group_probabilities <= 1e-6) || isTRUE(x$small_classes)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "A group class has (nearly) no membership, so its parameters are not identified.",
      class = "latents_boundary_fit", call = NULL))
  }
  stats <- x$sufficient_statistics
  class_names <- names(x$group_probabilities)
  parameters <- list(means = unname(x$means),
                     between = unname(x$between_variances),
                     within = unname(x$within_variances),
                     weights = unname(x$group_probabilities))
  theta <- .additive_pack(parameters, x$structure, class_names, x$vars)
  scores <- .additive_group_scores(stats, parameters, x$structure,
                                   class_names, x$vars)
  information <- .additive_information(stats, theta, x$structure,
                                       class_names, x$vars, step)
  # The ratio rule (and a non-positive smallest eigenvalue) refuses with the
  # ratio in the message; the ratio is also reported with the inference.
  inverse <- .inference_invert(information, "ratio_le_eps")
  eigenvalues <- eigen(information, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  condition_ratio <- min(eigenvalues) / max(eigenvalues)
  dimnames(inverse) <- dimnames(information)
  gradient <- colSums(scores)
  scaled_score <- sqrt(max(0, drop(crossprod(gradient, inverse %*% gradient))))
  if (scaled_score > 1e-2) {
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "The score at the estimate is not near zero (scaled %.3g); the fit may",
      "not be at a maximum. Refit with a smaller `tol`."), scaled_score),
      class = "latents_unconverged", call = NULL))
  }
  if (vcov_type != "observed") {
    .multilpa_require_clusters(sum((x$sampling_weights %||% rep(1, nrow(scores))) > 0),
                               ncol(scores), "A robust or OPG additive covariance")
    .inference_require_rank(scores, paste(
      "The %d group scores span %d of %d dimensions, too few to form a",
      "%s covariance."), formatted = TRUE, extra = list(vcov_type))
  }
  meat <- crossprod(scores)
  covariance <- switch(vcov_type,
    observed = inverse,
    robust = .inference_sandwich(inverse, meat,
      sum((x$sampling_weights %||% rep(1, nrow(scores))) > 0)),
    opg = chol2inv(chol(meat)))
  dimnames(covariance) <- dimnames(information)
  inference <- list(theta = theta, vcov = covariance, information = information,
                    gradient = gradient, group_scores = scores,
                    scaled_score = scaled_score, condition_ratio = condition_ratio,
                    vcov_type = vcov_type)
  if (isTRUE(warn_weak)) .additive_warn_weak(x, inference)
  inference
}

.additive_warn_weak <- function(x, inference) {
  effective <- .additive_effective_groups(x, inference)
  weak <- is.finite(effective$effective_groups) &
    effective$effective_groups < .additive_weak_class_threshold
  if (any(weak)) {
    # effective = expected class size x information ratio, so the two factors
    # say whether the class is small or poorly separated.
    detail <- sprintf("%s: %.1f effective of %.1f expected groups, %.0f%% of the information kept",
                      effective$group_class[weak], effective$effective_groups[weak],
                      x$n_groups * effective$weight[weak],
                      100 * effective$information_ratio[weak])
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "Group classes supported by fewer than %d effective groups (%s). A small",
      "information share means poor separation; a small expected count means",
      "few groups. Wald intervals for class means and weights can be",
      "miscalibrated; see get_results(x, \"group_classes\")."),
      .additive_weak_class_threshold, paste(detail, collapse = "; ")),
      class = "latents_weak_class", call = NULL))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

.additive_natural <- function(theta, n_classes, vars, structure, class_names) {
  parameters <- .additive_unpack(theta, n_classes, length(vars), structure)
  weights <- parameters$weights
  means <- .additive_block_pack(parameters$means, structure$means)
  variances <- c(.additive_block_pack(parameters$within, structure$within),
                 .additive_block_pack(parameters$between, structure$between))
  estimate <- c(means, variances, weights)
  n_head <- length(means)
  n_var <- length(variances)
  # The first class is the logit reference, so its column is dropped.
  softmax <- .inference_simplex_jacobian(weights, "first")
  jacobian <- matrix(0, length(estimate), length(theta))
  jacobian[seq_len(n_head), seq_len(n_head)] <- diag(n_head)
  positions <- n_head + seq_len(n_var)
  jacobian[positions, positions] <- diag(variances, n_var)
  jacobian[n_head + n_var + seq_len(n_classes),
           n_head + n_var + seq_len(n_classes - 1L)] <- softmax
  names(estimate) <- .additive_names(class_names, vars, structure, "natural")
  dimnames(jacobian) <- list(names(estimate), names(theta))
  list(estimate = estimate, jacobian = jacobian)
}

.additive_parameter_table <- function(x, inference, level = 0.95,
                                      adjust = "none") {
  stopifnot("`level` must be a single finite number in (0, 1)" =
              is.numeric(level) && length(level) == 1L && is.finite(level) &&
              level > 0 && level < 1)
  class_names <- names(x$group_probabilities)
  n_classes <- length(class_names)
  vars <- x$vars
  structure <- x$structure
  blocks <- list(
    means = c(.additive_block_labels(structure$means, class_names, vars),
              list(level = "between", parameter = "mean")),
    within = c(.additive_block_labels(structure$within, class_names, vars),
               list(level = "within", parameter = "variance")),
    between = c(.additive_block_labels(structure$between, class_names, vars),
                list(level = "between", parameter = "variance")))
  table <- rbind(
    do.call(rbind, lapply(blocks, function(block) {
      data.frame(level = block$level, group_class = block$group_class,
                 indicator = block$indicator, parameter = block$parameter,
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })),
    data.frame(level = "group_class", group_class = class_names,
               indicator = NA_character_, parameter = "weight",
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  theta <- .additive_pack(
    list(means = unname(x$means), between = unname(x$between_variances),
         within = unname(x$within_variances),
         weights = unname(x$group_probabilities)),
    structure, class_names, vars)
  natural <- .additive_natural(theta, n_classes, vars, structure, class_names)
  stopifnot("one table row per natural coefficient" =
              nrow(table) == length(natural$estimate))
  table$estimate <- unname(natural$estimate)
  standard_error <- if (is.null(inference)) {
    rep(NA_real_, nrow(table))
  } else {
    .inference_delta_se(natural$jacobian, inference$vcov, "quadratic")
  }
  table$standard_error <- unname(standard_error)
  tested <- table$parameter == "mean"
  table$statistic <- ifelse(tested, table$estimate / table$standard_error,
                            NA_real_)
  table$p_value <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(table$statistic))
  table$p_adjusted <- stats::p.adjust(table$p_value, method = adjust)
  kind <- ifelse(table$parameter == "weight", "probability",
                 ifelse(table$parameter == "variance", "positive", "real"))
  bounds <- .multilpa_wald_bounds(table$estimate, table$standard_error, kind,
                                  .inference_critical(level, "one_minus"))
  table$conf_low <- bounds$low
  table$conf_high <- bounds$high
  rownames(table) <- NULL
  table
}

review_record.source_function:
.additive_newton <- function(stats, parameters, structure, min_variance,
                             max_steps = 25L, step = 1e-4) {
  n_classes <- nrow(parameters$means)
  vars <- stats$vars
  class_names <- paste0("group_class_", seq_len(n_classes))
  theta <- .additive_pack(parameters, structure, class_names, vars)
  unpack <- function(point) {
    .additive_unpack(point, n_classes, length(vars), structure)
  }
  log_likelihood <- function(point) .additive_expectation(stats, unpack(point))$log_likelihood
  current <- log_likelihood(theta)
  steps <- 0L
  decrement <- NA_real_
  # Sequential by nature: each Newton step starts from the last accepted point.
  repeat {
    point <- unpack(theta)
    gradient <- colSums(.additive_group_scores(stats, point, structure,
                                               class_names, vars))
    information <- .additive_information(stats, theta, structure,
                                         class_names, vars, step)
    # Polishing stops, keeping the last accepted point, unless the information
    # is finite and numerically positive definite (then chol() succeeds).
    if (!all(is.finite(information))) break
    eigenvalues <- eigen(information, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
    if (min(eigenvalues) <=
          100 * nrow(information) * .Machine$double.eps * max(eigenvalues)) {
      break
    }
    factor <- chol(information)
    direction <- backsolve(factor, forwardsolve(t(factor), gradient))
    decrement <- sqrt(max(0, sum(gradient * direction)))
    if (decrement < 1e-8 || steps >= max_steps) break
    scale <- 1
    accepted <- FALSE
    while (scale >= 1 / 1024) {
      candidate <- theta + scale * direction
      if (all(unpack(candidate)$within >= min_variance)) {
        value <- log_likelihood(candidate)
        if (is.finite(value) && value >= current - 1e-12 * (1 + abs(current))) {
          accepted <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }
      scale <- scale / 2
    }
    if (!accepted) break
    theta <- candidate
    current <- value
    steps <- steps + 1L
  }
  list(parameters = unpack(theta), steps = steps, decrement = decrement)
}
