.multilpa_step_ml_fit <- function(pieces, values, variance, tol = 1e-12,
                                  max_iter = 5000L) {
  stopifnot("`variance` must be \"varying\" or \"equal\"" =
              variance %in% c("varying", "equal"))
  if (stats::var(values) <= 0) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "The outcome takes one value, so it has no distribution to estimate by class.",
      class = "latents_bad_outcome", call = NULL))
  }
  # Fit and differentiate in a chart whose origin and units are determined
  # by the outcome spread. A finite-difference step around a raw mean near
  # 1e12 can round to zero even though the outcome varies by whole units.
  outcome_center <- mean(values)
  outcome_scale <- stats::sd(values)
  values <- (values - outcome_center) / outcome_scale
  errors <- .multilpa_error_matrix(pieces)
  prior <- colMeans(pieces$posteriors)
  # Each unit's fixed weight on each class: the class's share times the
  # probability that a unit of that class is assigned where this one was.
  weights <- t(errors[, pieces$modal, drop = FALSE]) *
    matrix(prior, length(values), pieces$n_classes, byrow = TRUE)
  log_weights <- log(weights)
  smallest <- 1e-10 * stats::var(values)
  moments <- function(responsibilities, means) {
    squares <- (values - matrix(means, length(values), length(means), byrow = TRUE))^2
    by_class <- colSums(responsibilities * squares)
    if (identical(variance, "equal")) {
      rep(sum(by_class) / length(values), length(means))
    } else by_class / colSums(responsibilities)
  }
  e_step <- function(means, variances) {
    log_density <- vapply(seq_along(means), function(class) {
      stats::dnorm(values, means[class], sqrt(variances[class]), log = TRUE)
    }, numeric(length(values)))
    joint <- log_weights + log_density
    largest <- apply(joint, 1L, max)
    log_marginal <- largest + log(rowSums(exp(joint - largest)))
    list(responsibilities = exp(joint - log_marginal),
         log_likelihood = sum(log_marginal))
  }
  run <- function(means, variances) {
    state <- e_step(means, variances)
    converged <- FALSE
    failed <- FALSE
    iterations <- 0L
    # EM is iterative by nature: each step needs the previous one's estimates,
    # so this loop cannot be vectorised.
    while (iterations < max_iter) {
      iterations <- iterations + 1L
      responsibilities <- state$responsibilities
      # A start that leaves a class with no weight has no estimate for it;
      # the start is dropped rather than carried on with an undefined mean.
      if (!all(colSums(responsibilities) > 0)) {
        failed <- TRUE
        break
      }
      means <- as.vector(crossprod(responsibilities, values)) / colSums(responsibilities)
      variances <- pmax(moments(responsibilities, means), smallest)
      updated <- e_step(means, variances)
      if (!is.finite(updated$log_likelihood)) {
        failed <- TRUE
        break
      }
      change <- abs(updated$log_likelihood - state$log_likelihood)
      state <- updated
      if (change <= tol * (1 + abs(state$log_likelihood))) {
        converged <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    list(means = unname(means), variances = unname(variances),
         responsibilities = state$responsibilities,
         log_likelihood = state$log_likelihood, converged = converged,
         iterations = iterations, weights = weights, failed = failed,
         at_floor = !failed && any(variances <= smallest * (1 + 1e-8)))
  }
  # The step-three likelihood can have several maxima (a heavy-tailed or
  # skewed outcome lets one class absorb the tail), so EM runs from a fixed,
  # non-random set of starts: the proportional (posterior-weighted) moments,
  # Latent GOLD's start, first; then the modal-class means; then the class
  # means at the outcome's quantiles in every order (every cyclic order, both
  # ways, above five classes), from the outcome's own variance and from the
  # proportional spread; then the seeded draws below.
  proportional <- as.vector(crossprod(pieces$posteriors, values)) / colSums(pieces$posteriors)
  spread <- pmax(moments(pieces$posteriors, proportional), smallest)
  modal <- vapply(seq_len(pieces$n_classes), function(class) {
    members <- pieces$modal == class
    if (any(members)) mean(values[members]) else proportional[class]
  }, numeric(1))
  k <- pieces$n_classes
  quantiles <- stats::quantile(values, (seq_len(k) - 0.5) / k, names = FALSE)
  orders <- if (k <= 5L) .multilpa_permutations(k) else {
    shifts <- t(vapply(seq_len(k) - 1L, function(shift) (seq_len(k) + shift - 1L) %% k + 1L,
                       integer(k)))
    rbind(shifts, shifts[, rev(seq_len(k)), drop = FALSE])
  }
  placed <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(orders)), function(row) quantiles[orders[row, ]])
  # A heavy tail can be the likelihood's best class: each class in turn starts
  # at the mean of the outcome's top and bottom 2%, the others proportional.
  tails <- c(mean(values[values >= stats::quantile(values, 0.98)]),
             mean(values[values <= stats::quantile(values, 0.02)]))
  tailed <- do.call(c, lapply(tails, function(tail) lapply(seq_len(k), function(class) {
    replace(proportional, class, tail)
  })))
  # Twenty more starts at random quantiles with random standard deviations
  # (0.3 to 1 of the outcome's) reach basins the ordered placements miss.
  # They are drawn from a fixed seed in a local stream, so the result is the
  # same whatever the caller's seed and the caller's stream is untouched.
  drawn <- (function() {
    .latents_local_seed(20261021L)
    lapply(seq_len(20L), function(draw) {
      sds <- if (identical(variance, "equal")) rep(stats::runif(1L, 0.3, 1), k) else
        stats::runif(k, 0.3, 1)
      list(means = stats::quantile(values, stats::runif(k), names = FALSE),
           variances = sds^2)
    })
  })()
  # A start keeps only its estimates, not its observations-by-classes
  # responsibilities: with five classes there are 272 starts. The winner's
  # are recomputed below from its own estimates, by the same E-step.
  slim <- function(means, variances) {
    attempt <- run(means, variances)
    attempt$responsibilities <- NULL
    attempt
  }
  runs <- c(lapply(c(list(proportional, modal), tailed), slim, variances = spread),
            lapply(placed, slim, variances = rep(1, k)),
            lapply(placed, slim, variances = spread),
            lapply(drawn, function(start) slim(start$means, start$variances)))
  failed <- vapply(runs, `[[`, logical(1), "failed")
  if (all(failed)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "Every start of the step-three model left a class without weight; the",
      "class means are not identified."),
      class = "latents_singular_information", call = NULL))
  }
  scores <- vapply(runs, function(attempt) {
    if (attempt$failed || attempt$at_floor) -Inf else attempt$log_likelihood
  }, numeric(1))
  # A later start replaces the first only when it is clearly higher, so a
  # likelihood with one maximum keeps Latent GOLD's solution exactly. When
  # every start ends at the variance floor, the first that ran is kept.
  best <- if (all(is.infinite(scores))) which(!failed)[1L] else {
    top <- max(scores)
    which(scores >= top - 1e-10 * (1 + abs(top)))[1L]
  }
  fit <- runs[[best]]
  fit$responsibilities <- e_step(fit$means, fit$variances)$responsibilities
  if (!fit$at_floor) fit <- .multilpa_step_ml_polish(fit, values, variance)
  # Keep the conditioned means for inference: subtracting the origin from
  # already rounded reported means would throw away the precision just saved.
  fit$outcome_coordinates <- list(center = outcome_center, scale = outcome_scale,
                                  means = fit$means)
  fit$means <- outcome_center + outcome_scale * fit$means
  fit$variances <- outcome_scale^2 * fit$variances
  fit$log_likelihood <- fit$log_likelihood - length(values) * log(outcome_scale)
  fit
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_step_ml_scores <- function(fit, values, variance, parameters = NULL) {
  classes <- length(fit$means)
  parameters <- parameters %||% .multilpa_step_ml_coordinates(fit, variance)
  means <- parameters[seq_len(classes)]
  sds <- exp(parameters[-seq_len(classes)])
  sds <- if (identical(variance, "equal")) rep(sds, classes) else sds
  log_density <- vapply(seq_len(classes), function(class) {
    stats::dnorm(values, means[class], sds[class], log = TRUE)
  }, numeric(length(values)))
  joint <- log(fit$weights) + log_density
  largest <- apply(joint, 1L, max)
  responsibilities <- exp(joint - largest - log(rowSums(exp(joint - largest))))
  residuals <- values - matrix(means, length(values), classes, byrow = TRUE)
  scaled <- residuals / matrix(sds, length(values), classes, byrow = TRUE)
  mean_scores <- responsibilities * scaled / matrix(sds, length(values), classes,
                                                    byrow = TRUE)
  sd_scores <- responsibilities * (scaled^2 - 1)
  if (identical(variance, "equal")) sd_scores <- matrix(rowSums(sd_scores), ncol = 1L)
  unname(cbind(mean_scores, sd_scores))
}

.multilpa_three_step_ml <- function(pieces, values, level, variance, ci_level,
                                    contrast, adjust, vcov_type) {
  fit <- .multilpa_step_ml_fit(pieces, values, variance)
  if (!fit$converged) {
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "The step-three model did not converge in %d iterations, so its class",
      "means are not a maximum."), fit$iterations),
      class = "latents_unconverged", call = NULL))
  }
  if (fit$at_floor) {
    warning(warningCondition(paste(
      "A class variance of the outcome reached its lower bound: the class has",
      "almost no spread in the outcome, and its standard error is unreliable."),
      class = "latents_boundary", call = NULL))
  }
  quantile <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - ci_level) / 2)
  clustered <- .multilpa_step_clusters(.multilpa_step_ml_influence(fit, values, variance),
                                       pieces, vcov_type)
  # A sandwich for a class carried by a single unit is built from that unit's
  # score, which is zero at its own mean: it would report a standard error of
  # 0 rather than none. The units carrying a class are counted by Kish's
  # effective number, (sum r)^2 / sum r^2: 1 for one unit, 2 for two equal.
  # The units are those the sandwich sums over: groups under "cluster".
  responsibilities <- if (identical(vcov_type, "cluster")) {
    rowsum(fit$responsibilities, pieces$group_index, reorder = FALSE)
  } else fit$responsibilities
  carriers <- colSums(responsibilities)^2 / colSums(responsibilities^2)
  thin <- carriers < 1.5
  if (any(thin)) {
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "Class %s of the step-three model is carried by a single unit, so its",
      "standard error cannot be estimated and is reported as NA."),
      paste(which(thin), collapse = ", ")), class = "latents_small_classes", call = NULL))
    clustered[, thin] <- NA_real_
  }
  if (identical(contrast, "pairs")) {
    # The common origin cancels from contrasts; remove it before subtraction
    # so reported rounding at a large origin cannot erase a small difference.
    means <- fit$outcome_coordinates$means * fit$outcome_coordinates$scale
    return(.multilpa_step_pairs(means, clustered, level, "ml", quantile,
                                adjust, vcov_type))
  }
  errors <- sqrt(colSums(clustered^2))
  result <- data.frame(level = level, method = "ml",
                       class = seq_len(pieces$n_classes), estimate = fit$means,
                       standard_error = errors,
                       conf_low = fit$means - quantile * errors,
                       conf_high = fit$means + quantile * errors,
                       variance = fit$variances,
                       effective_n = colSums(fit$responsibilities),
                       row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  attr(result, "vcov_type") <- vcov_type
  attr(result, "variance") <- variance
  column <- .latents_column
  .latents_table(result, ci_level,
                 sprintf("Distal outcome by class (ml, %s variances, %s%% CI)",
                         variance, format(100 * ci_level)),
                 list(column("Class", "class", "integer"), column("Mean", "estimate"),
                      column(sprintf("%s%% CI", format(100 * ci_level)),
                             c("conf_low", "conf_high"), "ci", "estimate"),
                      column("SE", "standard_error"), column("Variance", "variance"),
                      column("Effective n", "effective_n")))
}

.multilpa_error_frame <- function(x, level) {
  # A noise unit's modal class is 0 and its posteriors lack the noise column,
  # so the error matrix would not be a matrix of probabilities.
  .multilpa_refuse_noise(x, "The classification-error table")
  pieces <- .multilpa_level_assignments(x, level)
  matrix_form <- .multilpa_error_matrix(pieces)
  classes <- seq_len(pieces$n_classes)
  index <- expand.grid(assigned_class = classes, true_class = classes)
  data.frame(level = level, true_class = index$true_class,
             assigned_class = index$assigned_class,
             probability = matrix_form[cbind(index$true_class, index$assigned_class)],
             row.names = NULL)
}

.multilpa_weight_frame <- function(x, level) {
  .multilpa_refuse_noise(x, "The BCH weights table")

  ## t() first, so that transposing the matrix into a vector walks a unit's
  ## classes before moving to the next unit and the frame reads unit by unit.
  data.frame(level = level,
             unit = rep(pieces$units, each = pieces$n_classes),
             assigned_class = rep(pieces$modal, each = pieces$n_classes),
             class = rep(classes, times = length(pieces$modal)),
             weight = as.vector(t(weights)),
             row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

review_record.name: three_step
review_record.purpose: Estimate a distal outcome's mean in each latent class  Estimates the mean of an outcome in each latent class of a fitted model, or the difference between every pair of classes, by the three-step approach, and returns a `data.frame`. The measurement model is fitted first, units are assigned to classes, and the outcome is then related to the assignments with a correction for classification error, so the outcome does not influence the classes. `"bch"` weights give approximately unbiased class means; `"ml"` estimates them by maximum likelihood with the classification errors held fixed; regressing on the modal class attenuates the differences (Vermunt 2010; Bakk, Tekle and Vermunt 2013; Bakk and Vermunt 2016).

documented_contracts: x A covariate-free fitted [multilpa()] or [lta()] model, or a   trajectory model that classifies persons ([mixture_regression()] with   `class_level = "group"`, with or without `random` effects) fitted without   `membership` covariates. Fits with membership covariates and multilevel   growth mixtures (`cluster`) are refused with   `latents_unsupported_three_step`: the correction uses a fixed,   unconditional classification-error matrix and independent units.

data The data frame carrying the outcome, in the fit's row order.   Columns shared with the fit are checked row by row; a frame with too   little identifying information raises a warning that alignment cannot be   verified. For a trajectory model it must be the data frame the model was   fitted to.

outcome Name of a numeric outcome column, without missing or   infinite values, that is not a measurement indicator of `x`. For   `level = "groups"` it must be constant within each group, and for a   trajectory model within each person.

level `"individuals"` (default) relates the outcome to profiles,   `"groups"` to group classes. For a trajectory model the outcome is   related to its person classes, reported with `level = "persons"`;   `"groups"` is refused there with `latents_bad_argument`.

method `"bch"` (default) applies the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars weights;   `"ml"` fits the maximum-likelihood step-three model (see *Details*);   `"proportional"` weights by the posterior probabilities (attenuated);   `"modal"` uses the uncorrected modal assignment, for comparison.
ci_level Confidence level for the intervals (default 0.95).
contrast `"none"` (default) reports one outcome mean per class;   `"pairs"` reports the difference between every pair of classes, with a   test against zero.

adjust Multiplicity correction across the pairwise differences,   passed to [stats::p.adjust()]: `"BH"` (default), `"holm"`,   `"hochberg"`, `"hommel"`, `"bonferroni"`, `"BY"` or `"none"`. Ignored for   `contrast = "none"`.

vcov_type `"cluster"` (default) sums the influence contributions   within the fit's groups and treats the groups as the independent units,   as required when the outcome is measured on observations nested in   groups. `"independent"` treats every observation as an independent unit,   which is appropriate only without nesting (for example a fit with a   single group). The choice is recorded in the result's `vcov_type`   attribute.

variance For `method = "ml"`: `"varying"` (default) estimates a   variance of the outcome in each class, `"equal"` one variance shared by   the classes. Given with another method it raises `latents_bad_argument`.

review_record.source_function:
three_step <- function(x, data, outcome,
                       level = c("individuals", "groups"),
                       method = c("bch", "proportional", "modal", "ml"),
                       ci_level = 0.95, contrast = c("none", "pairs"),
                       adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel",
                                    "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
                       vcov_type = c("cluster", "independent"),
                       variance = c("varying", "equal")) {
  # Whether `variance` was given is read before it is matched: missing() is
  # FALSE once an argument has been reassigned.
  variance_given <- !missing(variance)
  level <- match.arg(level)
  # The released methods keep their abbreviations ("m" is "modal", as it was
  # before "ml" existed); anything else is matched against all four, so "ml"
  # is taken by its full name and an unknown method's error lists every one.
  methods <- eval(formals(three_step)$method)
  released <- pmatch(method[1L], c("bch", "proportional", "modal"))
  method <- if (identical(method, methods)) "bch" else
    if (length(method) == 1L && !is.na(released)) methods[released] else
      match.arg(method, methods)
  variance <- match.arg(variance)
  if (variance_given && !identical(method, "ml")) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "`variance` sets the class variances of the outcome in the ML step-three",
      "model; the other methods weight the outcome and model no variance. Use",
      "`method = \"ml\"`."), class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  contrast <- match.arg(contrast)
  adjust <- match.arg(adjust)
  vcov_type <- match.arg(vcov_type)
  .multilpa_refuse_noise(x, "three_step()")
  if (.latents_is_weighted(x)) .latents_refuse_weights("`three_step()` yet")
  stopifnot(
    "`data` must be a data frame" = is.data.frame(data),
    "`outcome` must name a single column of `data`" =
      is.character(outcome) && length(outcome) == 1L && outcome %in% names(data),
    "`outcome` must be numeric" = is.numeric(data[[outcome]]),
    "`outcome` must not be missing" = !anyNA(data[[outcome]]),
    "`outcome` must be finite" = all(is.finite(data[[outcome]])),
    "`ci_level` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
      is.numeric(ci_level) && length(ci_level) == 1L && ci_level > 0 && ci_level < 1
  )
  if (.trajectory_is_fit(x)) {
    # Trajectory models classify persons: one outcome value per person.
    if (identical(level, "groups")) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "A trajectory model classifies persons and has no group classes, so",
        "`level = \"groups\"` does not apply; its outcome is related to the",
        "person classes."), class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    prepared <- .trajectory_three_step_inputs(x, data, outcome)
    pieces <- prepared$pieces
    values <- prepared$values
    level <- "persons"
  } else {
    .multilpa_check_three_step_fit(x)
    if (outcome %in% .multilpa_measured_items(x)) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
        "`%s` helped define the fitted classes, so it is not a distal outcome.",
        outcome), class = c("multilpa_indicator_reused", "latents_bad_outcome"),
        call = NULL))
    }
    pieces <- .multilpa_level_assignments(x, level)
    .multilpa_check_row_count(x, data)
    .multilpa_check_alignment(x, data)
    values <- .multilpa_outcome_values(x, data, outcome, level)
  }
  if (identical(method, "ml")) {
    return(.multilpa_three_step_ml(pieces, values, level, variance, ci_level,
                                   contrast, adjust, vcov_type))
  }
  weights <- .multilpa_step_weights(pieces, method)
  classes <- seq_len(pieces$n_classes)
  quantile <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - ci_level) / 2)

  totals <- colSums(weights)
  if (any(!is.finite(totals)) || any(totals <= 0)) {
    stop(errorCondition("A class has no positive total outcome weight.",
                        class = "latents_inseparable_classes", call = NULL))
  }
  # BCH weights may be negative. Multiplying and summing a constant outcome
  # directly can then leave a few ulps of cancellation, which looks like a
  # nonzero class contrast with an equally tiny standard error and can produce
  # a false significant p-value. Work on differences from an observed value.
  baseline <- values[[1L]]
  centered <- values - baseline
  centered_estimates <- as.vector(crossprod(weights, centered)) / totals
  estimates <- baseline + centered_estimates
  ## Cluster-robust variance of a weighted mean: the per-unit influence
  ## contributions are summed within each independent group, then across
  ## groups. Holding them as a matrix lets a difference between two classes be
  ## given a standard error from the same quantities, rather than assuming the
  ## two means are independent when they share every unit.
  influence <- sweep(weights * outer(centered, centered_estimates, "-"),
                     2L, totals, "/")
  clustered <- .multilpa_step_clusters(influence, pieces, vcov_type)

  if (identical(contrast, "pairs")) {
    return(.multilpa_step_pairs(centered_estimates, clustered, level, method, quantile,
                                adjust, vcov_type))
  }
  errors <- sqrt(colSums(clustered^2))
  result <- data.frame(level = level, method = method, class = classes,
                       estimate = estimates, standard_error = errors,
                       conf_low = estimates - quantile * errors,
                       conf_high = estimates + quantile * errors,
                       effective_n = totals^2 / colSums(weights^2),
                       row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  attr(result, "vcov_type") <- vcov_type
  column <- .latents_column
  .latents_table(result, ci_level,
                 sprintf("Distal outcome by class (%s, %s%% CI)", method,
                         format(100 * ci_level)),
                 list(column("Class", "class", "integer"), column("Mean", "estimate"),
                      column(sprintf("%s%% CI", format(100 * ci_level)),
                             c("conf_low", "conf_high"), "ci", "estimate"),
                      column("SE", "standard_error"),
                      column("Effective n", "effective_n")))
}

.multilpa_step_pairs <- function(estimates, clustered, level, method, quantile,
                                 adjust, vcov_type) {
  n_classes <- length(estimates)
  if (n_classes < 2L) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "A single class has no other class to be compared with.",
      class = "latents_inseparable_classes", call = NULL))
  }
  pairs <- utils::combn(n_classes, 2L)
  difference <- estimates[pairs[2L, ]] - estimates[pairs[1L, ]]
  errors <- sqrt(colSums((clustered[, pairs[2L, ], drop = FALSE] -
                            clustered[, pairs[1L, ], drop = FALSE])^2))
  statistic <- rep(NA_real_, length(errors))
  valid <- is.finite(errors) & errors > 0
  statistic[valid] <- difference[valid] / errors[valid]
  raw <- rep(NA_real_, length(errors))
  raw[valid] <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(statistic[valid]))
  result <- data.frame(
    level = level, method = method, class = pairs[2L, ],
    reference_class = pairs[1L, ], estimate = difference,
    standard_error = errors, statistic = statistic, p_value = raw,
    p_adjusted = stats::p.adjust(raw, method = adjust),
    conf_low = difference - quantile * errors,
    conf_high = difference + quantile * errors,
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  attr(result, "adjust") <- adjust
  attr(result, "vcov_type") <- vcov_type
  column <- .latents_column
  percent <- format(100 * (2 * stats::pnorm(quantile) - 1))
  .latents_table(result, NULL,
                 sprintf("Distal outcome: class differences (%s, %s%% CI)", method, percent),
                 list(column("Class", "class", "integer"),
                      column("vs", "reference_class", "integer"),
                      column("Difference", "estimate"),
                      column(sprintf("%s%% CI", percent), c("conf_low", "conf_high"), "ci",
                             "estimate"),
                      column("p", "p_value", "p"),
                      column(sprintf("p (%s)", adjust), "p_adjusted", "p")))
}

review_record.name: r3step
review_record.purpose: Regress latent class membership on covariates by the three-step approach  Fits a multinomial logit of latent class membership on covariates after the measurement model (the R3STEP approach) and returns its coefficients as a `data.frame`. The assigned class is treated as an error-prone indicator of the true class, with the classification-error rates fixed at their step-one values; regressing the modal class directly attenuates the coefficients (Vermunt 2010; Asparouhov and Muthen 2014).

documented_contracts: x A covariate-free fitted [multilpa()] or [lta()] model, or a   trajectory model from [mixture_regression()] that classifies persons   (with or without `random`), whose person classes are then predicted.   Fits with membership covariates and multilevel growth mixtures   (`cluster`) are refused with `latents_unsupported_three_step`: the   correction uses a fixed, unconditional classification-error matrix and   independent units.

data The data frame carrying the covariates, in the fit's row order.   Columns shared with the fit are checked row by row; a frame with too   little identifying information raises a warning that alignment cannot be   verified.

covariates Character vector of numeric columns, without missing or   infinite values, that are not measurement indicators of `x`. For   `level = "groups"` each must be constant within a group; for a   trajectory model each must be constant within a person and not part of   the trajectory regression (`latents_bad_covariate`).

level `"individuals"` (default) predicts profile membership,   `"groups"` group-class membership. For a trajectory model the rows have   `level = "persons"` and outcomes `class_1`, `class_2`, ...; `"groups"` is   refused there with `latents_bad_argument`.
ci_level Confidence level for the intervals (default 0.95).

vcov_type `"robust"` (default) uses the sandwich clustered on the   fit's groups with the small-sample (CR1) factor `G / (G - 1)` for `G`   groups, as the default of [three_step()]. `"observed"` uses the observed   information; for the pooled regression it treats every observation as   independent, and with `by_group_class = TRUE` it is the model-based   variance of the two-level likelihood. `"robust"` requires more   independent groups than the regression has coefficients, because the   group score contributions sum to zero at the estimate; otherwise it is   refused with `latents_too_few_groups`, and `"observed"` remains   available.

adjust Multiplicity correction across the covariate terms of every   non-reference class (not the intercepts), passed to   [stats::p.adjust()]: `"BH"` (default), `"holm"`, `"hochberg"`,   `"hommel"`, `"bonferroni"`, `"BY"` or `"none"`.

by_group_class `FALSE` (default) fits one pooled multinomial logit   with a single intercept per profile. `TRUE` fits the two-level form of   the one-step model: each group class has its own profile intercepts, the   covariate slopes are shared across group classes, and a group's   observations share one latent group class whose proportions are   estimated jointly. Between-group differences not explained by the   covariates are then captured by the group classes; the pooled regression   attenuates the slopes and inflates their clustered standard errors in   that case. Only for `level = "individuals"` on a covariate-free   [multilpa()] fit; refused with `latents_bad_argument` otherwise.

initial_covariates,transition_covariates For an [lta()] fit with one   group class: covariates of the profile at the first occasion (constant   within a person) and of every transition (read at the destination   occasion, so they may vary over occasions). Either one fits the   three-step latent Markov model described below instead of the   occasion-by-occasion profile regression; `covariates` must then be   empty, and `level` and `by_group_class` do not apply. Refused with   `latents_bad_argument` on a fit that is not a transition model.

A base `data.frame` with one row per non-reference class and term,   and the columns `level`, `outcome`, `term`, `estimate`,   `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and   `conf_high`. `p_value` is uncorrected; `p_adjusted` applies `adjust`   (also recorded in the `adjust` attribute) and is `NA` on the intercept   rows. A coefficient with zero standard error has `NA_real_` statistic   and p-value. Coefficients are log odds against the last class, as in   `multilpa(profile_covariates = )`; the reference class is named in the   `reference_class` attribute and the variance used in the `vcov_type`   attribute. With `by_group_class = TRUE` there is one intercept row per   group class (`group_class_1`, `group_class_2`, ...), followed by the   shared slopes and, at `level = "groups"`, the group-class logits against   the last group class; the result also carries the attributes   `by_group_class` and `log_likelihood` (the maximised log likelihood).    With `initial_covariates` or `transition_covariates`, one row per   coefficient of the step-three chain: `block` (`"initial"` or   `"transition"`), `from` (the origin profile of a transition, `NA` for an   initial logit), `to`, `term`, `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`,   `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`, with the attributes   `log_likelihood`, `classification_errors` (the step-two error matrix,   rows the true profile), `vcov_type` and `adjust`. Initial logits are   against the last profile and transition logits against staying, as in   `lta(initial_covariates =, transition_covariates =)`; `p_adjusted` covers   the covariate terms.

review_record.source_function:
r3step <- function(x, data, covariates = character(),
                   level = c("individuals", "groups"), ci_level = 0.95,
                   vcov_type = c("robust", "observed"),
                   adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel",
                                "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
                   by_group_class = FALSE, initial_covariates = character(),
                   transition_covariates = character()) {
  level <- match.arg(level)
  vcov_type <- match.arg(vcov_type)
  adjust <- match.arg(adjust)
  if (length(initial_covariates) > 0L || length(transition_covariates) > 0L) {
    return(.r3step_transitions(x, data, covariates, level, ci_level, vcov_type,
                               adjust, by_group_class, initial_covariates,
                               transition_covariates))
  }
  trajectory <- .trajectory_is_fit(x)
  if (!trajectory) .multilpa_refuse_noise(x, "r3step()")
  if (.latents_is_weighted(x)) .latents_refuse_weights("`r3step()` yet")
  stopifnot(
    "`data` must be a data frame" = is.data.frame(data),
    "`covariates` must name columns of `data`" =
      is.character(covariates) && length(covariates) >= 1L &&
      all(covariates %in% names(data)),
    "`covariates` must be numeric" =
      all(vapply(data[covariates], is.numeric, logical(1))),
    "`covariates` must not be missing" = !anyNA(data[covariates]),
    "`covariates` must be finite" =
      all(vapply(data[covariates], function(value) all(is.finite(value)), logical(1))),
    "`ci_level` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
      is.numeric(ci_level) && length(ci_level) == 1L && ci_level > 0 && ci_level < 1,
    "`by_group_class` must be TRUE or FALSE" =
      is.logical(by_group_class) && length(by_group_class) == 1L &&
      !is.na(by_group_class)
  )
  if (trajectory) {
    # Trajectory models classify persons: one covariate value per person.
    if (identical(level, "groups") || by_group_class) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "A trajectory model classifies persons and has no group classes, so",
        "`level = \"groups\"` and `by_group_class = TRUE` do not apply."),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    prepared <- .trajectory_r3step_inputs(x, data, covariates)
    pieces <- prepared$pieces
    design <- prepared$design
    level <- "persons"
  } else {
    .multilpa_check_three_step_fit(x)
    if (by_group_class && !identical(level, "individuals")) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "`by_group_class = TRUE` gives each group class its own profile",
        "intercepts, so it applies to `level = \"individuals\"` only."),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    if (by_group_class && inherits(x, "multilpa_transitions")) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "`by_group_class = TRUE` is not available for a transition fit, whose",
        "group classes govern transitions rather than a profile mix."),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    reused <- intersect(covariates, .multilpa_measured_items(x))
    if (length(reused) > 0L) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
        "Measurement indicator(s) %s already helped define the fitted classes and cannot be used as external predictors.",
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", reused), collapse = ", ")),
        class = c("multilpa_indicator_reused", "latents_bad_covariate"),
        call = NULL))
    }
    pieces <- .multilpa_level_assignments(x, level)
    .multilpa_check_row_count(x, data)
    .multilpa_check_alignment(x, data)
    .r3step_require_classes(pieces)
    design <- .multilpa_r3step_design(x, data, covariates, level)
  }
  .r3step_require_classes(pieces)
  errors <- .multilpa_error_matrix(pieces)
  if (by_group_class) {
    if (identical(vcov_type, "robust")) {
      .multilpa_require_clusters(
        length(unique(pieces$group_index)),
        (x$n_group_classes + length(covariates)) * (pieces$n_classes - 1L) +
          x$n_group_classes - 1L,
        what = "A cluster-robust covariance for the membership regression",
        alternative = paste("`vcov_type = \"observed\"` uses the model-based",
                            "information instead."))
    }
    return(.multilpa_r3step_by_group_class(
      x, design[, -1L, drop = FALSE], pieces, errors, ci_level, vcov_type,
      adjust))
  }
  ## The search runs on orthonormal coordinates of the design, which move with
  ## neither the units nor the origin of a covariate; a covariate held far from
  ## zero relative to its spread is otherwise nearly collinear with the
  ## intercept, and BFGS then stops far from the maximum or not at all.
  basis <- .multilpa_design_basis(design) %||%
    diag(.multilpa_design_scale(design), ncol(design))
  terms <- colnames(design)
  design <- t(backsolve(basis, t(design), transpose = TRUE))
  ## The likelihood of the assigned class, given the covariates and an error
  ## matrix fixed at its step-one value.
  by_assigned <- t(errors)[pieces$modal, , drop = FALSE]
  n_free <- pieces$n_classes - 1L
  shape <- function(theta) matrix(theta, ncol(design), n_free)
  ## Refuse a sandwich the groups cannot support before paying for the fit.
  if (identical(vcov_type, "robust")) {
    .multilpa_require_clusters(
      length(unique(pieces$group_index)), ncol(design) * n_free,
      what = "A cluster-robust covariance for the membership regression",
      alternative = paste("`vcov_type = \"observed\"` uses the model-based",
                          "information instead, which does not allow for the",
                          "nesting."))
  }

  objective <- function(theta) {
    prior <- .multilpa_logit_prior(shape(theta), design)
    -sum(log(pmax(rowSums(prior * by_assigned), 1e-300)))
  }
  score_rows <- function(theta) {
    prior <- .multilpa_logit_prior(shape(theta), design)
    joint <- prior * by_assigned
    posterior <- joint / rowSums(joint)
    residual <- (posterior - prior)[, seq_len(n_free), drop = FALSE]
    do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_free), function(k) design * residual[, k]))
  }
  gradient <- function(theta) -colSums(score_rows(theta))

  ## The likelihood with the error matrix held fixed is not concave. When a
  ## covariate nearly separates the classes it can hold a ridge whose basin
  ## BFGS enters from zero and settles on, far from the finite maximum (Mplus
  ## UG ex7.3: -log L 81.7 on the ridge against 62.6 at the maximum). The
  ## proportional-assignment estimate, a multinomial logit weighted by the
  ## posteriors, is concave and finite and lies in the maximum's basin; the
  ## search runs from it and from zero and keeps the better converged end.
  proportional_objective <- function(theta) {
    prior <- .multilpa_logit_prior(shape(theta), design)
    -sum(pieces$posteriors * log(pmax(prior, 1e-300)))
  }
  proportional_gradient <- function(theta) {
    prior <- .multilpa_logit_prior(shape(theta), design)
    residual <- (pieces$posteriors - prior)[, seq_len(n_free), drop = FALSE]
    -colSums(do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_free), function(k) design * residual[, k])))
  }
  control <- list(maxit = 1000L, reltol = 1e-12)
  zero <- rep(0, ncol(design) * n_free)
  starts <- list(zero, stats::optim(zero, proportional_objective, proportional_gradient,
                                    method = "BFGS", control = control)$par)
  attempts <- lapply(starts, function(start)
    stats::optim(start, objective, gradient, method = "BFGS", control = control))
  converged <- vapply(attempts, function(attempt) identical(attempt$convergence, 0L),
                      logical(1))
  if (!any(converged)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      sprintf("The membership regression did not converge (optim code %d).",
              attempts[[1L]]$convergence),
      class = "latents_no_converge", call = NULL))
  }
  attempts <- attempts[converged]
  fitted <- attempts[[which.min(vapply(attempts, `[[`, numeric(1), "value"))]]
  information <- .multilpa_observed_hessian(
    function(step) objective(fitted$par + step),
    function(step) gradient(fitted$par + step),
    rep(1, length(fitted$par)), 1e-4)
  covariance <- information$inverse
  if (identical(vcov_type, "robust")) {
    scores <- rowsum(score_rows(fitted$par), pieces$group_index, reorder = FALSE)
    covariance <- .inference_sandwich(covariance, .multilpa_cross_product(scores),
                                      nrow(scores))
  }
  ## Back to the covariates' own units and origin, one logit column at a time.
  natural <- kronecker(diag(n_free), backsolve(basis, diag(ncol(design))))
  .multilpa_r3step_frame(as.vector(natural %*% fitted$par),
                         natural %*% covariance %*% t(natural), terms, n_free,
                         pieces$n_classes, level, ci_level, vcov_type, adjust)
}

.multilpa_r3step_frame <- function(estimates, covariance, terms, n_free,
                                   n_classes, level, ci_level, vcov_type,
                                   adjust) {
  errors <- sqrt(pmax(diag(covariance), 0))
  statistic <- rep(NA_real_, length(errors))
  valid <- is.finite(errors) & errors > 0
  statistic[valid] <- estimates[valid] / errors[valid]
  quantile <- .inference_critical(ci_level, "one_minus")
  # Named as parameter_inference() names the same classes.
  prefix <- switch(level, groups = "group_class_", persons = "class_", "profile_")
  labels <- expand.grid(term = terms, outcome = paste0(prefix, seq_len(n_free)),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  raw <- rep(NA_real_, length(errors))
  raw[valid] <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(statistic[valid]))
  ## The intercepts are estimated, not tested: correcting across them would
  ## enlarge the family with hypotheses nobody asked about and make every
  ## covariate look less significant than the data say.
  tested <- labels$term != "(Intercept)"
  adjusted <- rep(NA_real_, length(raw))
  adjusted[tested] <- stats::p.adjust(raw[tested], method = adjust)
  result <- data.frame(
    level = level, outcome = labels$outcome, term = labels$term,
    estimate = estimates, standard_error = errors, statistic = statistic,
    p_value = raw, p_adjusted = adjusted,
    conf_low = estimates - quantile * errors,
    conf_high = estimates + quantile * errors,
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  attr(result, "reference_class") <- n_classes
  attr(result, "vcov_type") <- vcov_type
  attr(result, "adjust") <- adjust
  result
}

.multilpa_r3step_by_group_class <- function(x, z, pieces, errors, ci_level,
                                            vcov_type, adjust) {
  model <- .multilpa_r3step_group_model(x, z, pieces, errors)
  n_classes <- pieces$n_classes
  n_free <- n_classes - 1L
  n_group_classes <- x$n_group_classes
  fitted <- stats::optim(model$start, model$objective, model$gradient,
                         method = "BFGS",
                         control = list(maxit = 1000L, reltol = 1e-12))
  if (!identical(fitted$convergence, 0L)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      sprintf("The membership regression did not converge (optim code %d).",
              fitted$convergence),
      class = "latents_no_converge", call = NULL))
  }
  information <- .multilpa_observed_hessian(
    function(step) model$objective(fitted$par + step),
    function(step) model$gradient(fitted$par + step),
    rep(1, length(fitted$par)), 1e-4)
  covariance <- information$inverse
  if (identical(vcov_type, "robust")) {
    scores <- model$group_scores(fitted$par)
    covariance <- .inference_sandwich(covariance, .multilpa_cross_product(scores),
                                      nrow(scores))
  }
  ## Back to the units and origin the covariates arrived in.
  estimates <- as.vector(model$transform %*% fitted$par)
  covariance <- model$transform %*% covariance %*% t(model$transform)
  .multilpa_r3step_group_frame(estimates, covariance, colnames(z), n_free,
                               n_group_classes, n_classes, ci_level, vcov_type,
                               adjust, -fitted$value)
}

.multilpa_r3step_group_model <- function(x, z, pieces, errors) {
  n_classes <- pieces$n_classes
  n_free <- n_classes - 1L
  n_group_classes <- x$n_group_classes
  n_covariates <- ncol(z)
  group_index <- pieces$group_index
  n_groups <- max(group_index)
  by_assigned <- t(errors)[pieces$modal, , drop = FALSE]
  ## The search runs on the orthonormal coordinates of `cbind(1, z)` (see
  ## `.multilpa_design_basis()`), which move with neither the units nor the
  ## origin of a covariate. With `cbind(1, z) = Q R`, `z = r' + Q_z R_z`, so
  ## `alpha_h + z beta = (alpha_h + r' beta) + Q_z (R_z beta)`: the search
  ## estimates the bracketed intercepts and `R_z beta`, and `transform` maps
  ## them back to the covariates' own units and origin.
  basis <- .multilpa_design_basis(cbind(1, z))
  shift <- if (is.null(basis)) rep(0, n_covariates) else basis[1L, -1L]
  slope_basis <- if (is.null(basis)) {
    diag(.multilpa_design_scale(z), n_covariates)
  } else basis[-1L, -1L, drop = FALSE]
  scaled_z <- t(backsolve(slope_basis, t(sweep(z, 2L, shift, "-")),
                          transpose = TRUE))
  n_alpha <- n_group_classes * n_free
  n_beta <- n_covariates * n_free
  slope_inverse <- backsolve(slope_basis, diag(n_covariates))
  ## beta = R_z^-1 beta'; alpha_h = alpha'_h - r' R_z^-1 beta'.
  transform <- diag(n_alpha + n_beta + n_group_classes - 1L)
  transform[n_alpha + seq_len(n_beta), n_alpha + seq_len(n_beta)] <-
    kronecker(diag(n_free), slope_inverse)
  transform[seq_len(n_alpha), n_alpha + seq_len(n_beta)] <-
    kronecker(diag(n_free), -matrix(1, n_group_classes, 1L) %*%
                (shift %*% slope_inverse))
  unpack <- function(theta) {
    list(alpha = matrix(theta[seq_len(n_alpha)], n_group_classes, n_free),
         beta = matrix(theta[n_alpha + seq_len(n_beta)], n_covariates, n_free),
         gamma = theta[n_alpha + n_beta + seq_len(n_group_classes - 1L)])
  }
  pieces_at <- function(theta) {
    parameters <- unpack(theta)
    slope_part <- scaled_z %*% parameters$beta
    per_class <- lapply(seq_len(n_group_classes), function(h) {
      linear <- cbind(sweep(slope_part, 2L, parameters$alpha[h, ], "+"), 0)
      prior <- exp(linear - apply(linear, 1L, max))
      prior <- prior / rowSums(prior)
      joint <- prior * by_assigned
      marginal <- pmax(rowSums(joint), 1e-300)
      list(prior = prior, posterior = joint / marginal,
           evidence = as.vector(rowsum(log(marginal), group_index, reorder = FALSE)))
    })
    log_eta <- c(parameters$gamma, 0)
    log_eta <- log_eta - .multilpa_log_sum_exp(matrix(log_eta, 1L))
    scores <- sweep(vapply(per_class, `[[`, numeric(n_groups), "evidence"),
                    2L, log_eta, "+")
    log_group <- .multilpa_log_sum_exp(scores)
    list(per_class = per_class, eta = exp(log_eta),
         group_posteriors = exp(sweep(scores, 1L, log_group, "-")),
         log_likelihood = sum(log_group))
  }
  group_scores <- function(theta) {
    state <- pieces_at(theta)
    residuals <- lapply(state$per_class, function(piece) {
      (piece$posterior - piece$prior)[, seq_len(n_free), drop = FALSE]
    })
    alpha_block <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_free), function(k) {
      vapply(seq_len(n_group_classes), function(h) {
        state$group_posteriors[, h] *
          as.vector(rowsum(residuals[[h]][, k], group_index, reorder = FALSE))
      }, numeric(n_groups))
    }))
    beta_block <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_free), function(k) {
      Reduce(`+`, lapply(seq_len(n_group_classes), function(h) {
        state$group_posteriors[, h] *
          rowsum(scaled_z * residuals[[h]][, k], group_index, reorder = FALSE)
      }))
    }))
    gamma_block <- sweep(state$group_posteriors[, seq_len(n_group_classes - 1L),
                                                drop = FALSE],
                         2L, state$eta[seq_len(n_group_classes - 1L)], "-")
    cbind(alpha_block, beta_block, gamma_block)
  }
  objective <- function(theta) -pieces_at(theta)$log_likelihood
  gradient <- function(theta) -colSums(group_scores(theta))

  ## Started from the step-one solution: the profile mix within each group
  ## class, no slopes, and the group-class proportions.
  mix <- pmax(x$profile_probabilities, 1e-8)
  start <- c(as.vector(log(mix[, seq_len(n_free), drop = FALSE] / mix[, n_classes])),
             rep(0, n_beta),
             log(pmax(x$group_probabilities[seq_len(n_group_classes - 1L)], 1e-8) /
                   max(x$group_probabilities[n_group_classes], 1e-8)))
  list(objective = objective, gradient = gradient, group_scores = group_scores,
       start = start, transform = transform)
}

.multilpa_r3step_group_frame <- function(estimates, covariance, terms, n_free,
                                         n_group_classes, n_classes, ci_level,
                                         vcov_type, adjust, log_likelihood) {
  errors_se <- sqrt(pmax(diag(covariance), 0))
  ## Alpha is group classes by free classes and beta covariates by free
  ## classes, both stored column-major, so `expand.grid()` with the row index
  ## varying fastest labels them in the order they are packed.
  alpha_labels <- expand.grid(term = paste0("group_class_", seq_len(n_group_classes)),
                              outcome = paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_free)),
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  beta_labels <- expand.grid(term = terms,
                             outcome = paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_free)),
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  labels <- rbind(
    data.frame(level = "individuals", outcome = alpha_labels$outcome,
               term = alpha_labels$term, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(level = "individuals", outcome = beta_labels$outcome,
               term = beta_labels$term, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(level = rep("groups", n_group_classes - 1L),
               outcome = sprintf("group_class_%d", seq_len(n_group_classes - 1L)),
               term = rep("(Intercept)", n_group_classes - 1L),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  statistic <- rep(NA_real_, length(estimates))
  valid <- is.finite(errors_se) & errors_se > 0
  statistic[valid] <- estimates[valid] / errors_se[valid]
  raw <- rep(NA_real_, length(estimates))
  raw[valid] <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(statistic[valid]))
  ## Only the covariate slopes are tested; intercepts and the group-class
  ## logits are estimated, not hypotheses, as in the pooled regression.
  tested <- labels$level == "individuals" & labels$term %in% terms
  adjusted <- rep(NA_real_, length(raw))
  adjusted[tested] <- stats::p.adjust(raw[tested], method = adjust)
  quantile <- .inference_critical(ci_level, "one_minus")
  result <- data.frame(
    labels, estimate = estimates, standard_error = errors_se,
    statistic = statistic, p_value = raw, p_adjusted = adjusted,
    conf_low = estimates - quantile * errors_se,
    conf_high = estimates + quantile * errors_se,
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  attr(result, "reference_class") <- n_classes
  attr(result, "vcov_type") <- vcov_type
  attr(result, "adjust") <- adjust
  attr(result, "by_group_class") <- TRUE
  attr(result, "log_likelihood") <- log_likelihood
  result
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_transition_view <- function(x, centers = NULL) {
  stopifnot(inherits(x, "multilpa_transitions"))
  means <- x$means
  if (!is.null(centers) && ncol(means) > 0L) means <- sweep(means, 2L, centers, "-")
  structure(list(
    means = means, variances = x$variances, covariances = x$covariances,
    response_probabilities = x$response_probabilities,
    profile_probabilities = x$initial_probabilities,
    group_probabilities = x$group_probabilities,
    n_profiles = x$n_profiles, n_group_classes = x$n_group_classes,
    n_groups = x$n_groups, group_index = x$group_index, group_ids = x$group_ids,
    vars = x$vars, continuous = x$continuous, categorical = x$categorical,
    variance_model = x$variance_model, covariance_model = x$covariance_model,
    min_probability = x$min_probability), class = "multilpa")
}

.multilpa_transition_shared_blocks <- function(view, scale) {
  widths <- .multilpa_coordinate_widths(view, scale)
  n_measurement <- sum(widths[c("means", "variances", "response_probabilities")])
  list(measurement = seq_len(n_measurement),
       profile = n_measurement + seq_len(widths[["profile"]]),
       group = n_measurement + widths[["profile"]] + seq_len(widths[["group"]]))
}

.multilpa_transition_group_scores <- function(theta, x, layout, view, widths,
                                              codes = NULL) {
  parameters <- .multilpa_transition_decode(theta, view, widths[["measurement"]],
                                            widths[["group"]])
  expectation <- .multilpa_transition_expectation(x, layout, parameters, codes)
  n_profiles <- view$n_profiles
  n_types <- view$n_group_classes
  group_index <- view$group_index
  ## Measurement: the cross-sectional scores, weighted by the sequence
  ## posteriors of each observation.
  measurement <- if (identical(view$covariance_model, "full")) {
    .multilpa_full_measurement_group_score(parameters, expectation, view)
  } else {
    observed <- !is.na(x)
    blocks <- lapply(seq_len(n_profiles), function(profile) {
      residuals <- sweep(x, 2L, parameters$means[profile, ], "-")
      residuals[!observed] <- 0
      weights <- expectation$subject_posteriors[, profile]
      list(means = rowsum(sweep(residuals, 2L, parameters$variances[profile, ], "/") *
                            weights, group_index, reorder = FALSE),
           variances = rowsum(0.5 * (sweep(residuals^2, 2L,
             parameters$variances[profile, ], "/") - observed) * weights,
             group_index, reorder = FALSE))
    })
    list(means = do.call(cbind, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "means")),
         covariances = if (identical(view$variance_model, "equal")) {
           Reduce(`+`, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "variances"))
         } else do.call(cbind, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "variances")))
  }
  response <- .multilpa_response_scores(codes, expectation$subject_posteriors,
                                        parameters$response_probabilities,
                                        group_index)
  group <- sweep(expectation$group_posteriors, 2L, parameters$group_probabilities,
                 "-")[, seq_len(n_types - 1L), drop = FALSE]
  counts <- .multilpa_transition_group_counts(x, layout, parameters, codes,
                                              expectation$group_posteriors)
  free <- seq_len(n_profiles - 1L)
  initial <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(type) {
    first <- counts$initial[[type]]
    (first - outer(rowSums(first), parameters$initial_probabilities[type, ]))[
      , free, drop = FALSE]
  }))
  transition <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(type) {
    pairs <- counts$transition[[type]]
    do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_profiles), function(from) {
      ## Columns of `pairs` are laid out as the transition matrix is,
      ## column-major: from profile `from` to profile `to` is column
      ## (to - 1) * K + from.
      moves <- pairs[, (seq_len(n_profiles) - 1L) * n_profiles + from, drop = FALSE]
      (moves - outer(rowSums(moves),
                     parameters$transition_probabilities[from, , type]))[
        , free, drop = FALSE]
    }))
  }))
  cbind(measurement$means, measurement$covariances, response, group, initial,
        transition)
}

.multilpa_transition_jacobian <- function(x, view) {
  natural_blocks <- .multilpa_transition_shared_blocks(view, "natural")
  free_blocks <- .multilpa_transition_shared_blocks(view, "unconstrained")
  shared <- .multilpa_inference_jacobian(view)[
    c(natural_blocks$measurement, natural_blocks$group),
    c(free_blocks$measurement, free_blocks$group), drop = FALSE]
  n_profiles <- x$n_profiles
  n_types <- x$n_group_classes
  distributions <- c(
    lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(type) x$initial_probabilities[type, ]),
    unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(type) {
      lapply(seq_len(n_profiles), function(from) {
        x$transition_probabilities[from, , type]
      })
    }), recursive = FALSE))
  ## Each distribution is its own simplex, with the derivative diag(p) - p p'
  ## restricted to the free (non-reference) logits.
  blocks <- lapply(distributions, .inference_simplex_jacobian, reference = "last")
  sequence_block <- matrix(0, n_profiles * length(blocks),
                           (n_profiles - 1L) * length(blocks))
  invisible(lapply(seq_along(blocks), function(index) {
    rows <- (index - 1L) * n_profiles + seq_len(n_profiles)
    columns <- (index - 1L) * (n_profiles - 1L) + seq_len(n_profiles - 1L)
    sequence_block[rows, columns] <<- blocks[[index]]
  }))
  top <- cbind(shared, matrix(0, nrow(shared), ncol(sequence_block)))
  bottom <- cbind(matrix(0, nrow(sequence_block), ncol(shared)), sequence_block)
  rbind(top, bottom)
}

.multilpa_transition_labels <- function(names, view) {
  prefix <- sub("\\[.*$", "", names)
  sequence <- prefix %in% c("initial_probability", "initial_logit",
                            "transition_probability", "transition_logit")
  labels <- data.frame(level = character(length(names)),
                       outcome = character(length(names)),
                       term = character(length(names)),
                       parameter = character(length(names)),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (any(!sequence)) {
    labels[!sequence, ] <- .multilpa_tidy_labels(names[!sequence], view)[
      c("level", "outcome", "term", "parameter")]
  }
  if (any(sequence)) {
    inside <- strsplit(sub("^[^\\[]*\\[", "", sub("\\]$", "", names[sequence])),
                       ",", fixed = TRUE)
    type <- vapply(inside, `[[`, character(1), 1L)
    initial <- prefix[sequence] %in% c("initial_probability", "initial_logit")
    to <- vapply(inside, function(part) part[[length(part)]], character(1))
    from <- vapply(inside, function(part) if (length(part) == 3L) part[[2L]] else
      NA_character_, character(1))
    ## The decomposition coef() already uses for these parameters: the profile
    ## moved to (or started in) is the outcome, the group class and, for a
    ## move, the profile moved from are the term.
    labels$level[sequence] <- "profile"
    labels$outcome[sequence] <- paste0("profile_", to)
    labels$term[sequence] <- ifelse(initial, paste0("group_class_", type),
                                    paste0("group_class_", type, ":profile_", from))
    labels$parameter[sequence] <- prefix[sequence]
  }
  labels
}

The scores follow the Fisher identity (each is an expected count from the forward-backward pass minus the count implied by the fitted probabilities), and the observed information is the numerical Jacobian of that analytic score.

documented_contracts: x A fitted `multilpa_transitions` model from [lta()].

data Optional data frame the model was fitted to. Not needed for   the Wald path, since the fit stores its indicators, codes, groups and   occasions; when given it must reproduce them. Required for   `method = "bootstrap"`.
level Confidence level of the intervals. Default `0.95`.
step Finite-difference step for the observed information.
vcov_type `"observed"` (default; observed information), `"robust"`   (the sandwich clustered on groups, which are the sequences) or `"opg"`   (the outer product of the group scores).
adjust Multiplicity correction for `p_adjusted`: `"none"` (default)   or one of the [stats::p.adjust()] methods.

method `"wald"` (default) or `"bootstrap"`. The bootstrap resamples   persons with replacement, refits the same specification and matches each   replicate's profiles and group classes to the original's;   `standard_error` is the standard deviation of the replicates,   `conf_low` and `conf_high` their percentile interval, and `statistic`,   `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA`.
iter,n_starts,max_iter,tol,seed Number of bootstrap resamples, the   controls of each refit, and an optional seed (the caller's random state   is restored).

boundary Accepted for consistency with the generic. Transition   inference holds no parameter at a bound: without an active bound   `"fix"` gives the same table as `"error"`, and a fit with an active bound   raises `latents_boundary_fit` under either.
... For `confint()`, further arguments to `parameter_inference()`,   such as `vcov_type`. `vcov()` takes none and warns   (`latents_unused_argument`) about any it is given.

A base `data.frame` with one row per natural parameter and the   columns of [parameter_inference()]: `level`, `outcome`, `term`,   `parameter`, `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`,   `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`, named as [coef()] names them.   An initial probability (`parameter = "initial_probability"`,   `level = "profile"`) has `outcome` the profile and `term` the group   class; a transition probability (`"transition_probability"`) has   `outcome` the profile moved to and `term` `group_class_h:profile_j`, the   group class and the profile moved from. Probabilities and variances have   no Wald test. The Wald table has attributes `covariance` (natural   scale), `covariance_unconstrained`, `level`, `step`, `method` and   `vcov_type`.

parameter_inference.multilpa_transitions <- function(x, data = NULL, level = 0.95,
                                                     step = 1e-4,
                                                     vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg"),
                                                     adjust = .multilpa_p_adjust_methods,
                                                     method = c("wald", "bootstrap"),
                                                     iter = 199L, n_starts = 10L,
                                                     max_iter = 5000L, tol = 1e-10,
                                                     seed = NULL,
                                                     boundary = c("error", "fix")) {
  stopifnot(inherits(x, "multilpa_transitions"),
            "`level` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
              is.numeric(level) && length(level) == 1L && is.finite(level) &&
              level > 0 && level < 1,
            "`step` must be a single positive number" =
              is.numeric(step) && length(step) == 1L && is.finite(step) && step > 0)
  # Nothing is held at a bound here and a bound-active fit is refused, so
  # "fix" and "error" agree wherever a table is returned.
  match.arg(boundary)
  adjust <- match.arg(adjust)
  if (identical(match.arg(method), "bootstrap")) {
    return(.lta_bootstrap_dispatch(x, data, level, iter, n_starts, max_iter, tol,
                                   seed, adjust))
  }
  vcov_type <- match.arg(vcov_type)
  inference <- .multilpa_transition_covariance(x, data, step, vcov_type)
  estimates <- .multilpa_transition_encode(x, "natural")
  covariance <- inference$covariance
  standard_errors <- sqrt(pmax(diag(covariance), 0))
  critical <- .inference_critical(level, "upper")
  statistic <- unname(estimates / standard_errors)
  labels <- .multilpa_transition_labels(names(estimates), inference$view)
  result <- data.frame(
    labels, estimate = unname(estimates), standard_error = unname(standard_errors),
    statistic = statistic, p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(statistic)),
    conf_low = unname(estimates - critical * standard_errors),
    conf_high = unname(estimates + critical * standard_errors),
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  continuous <- .multilpa_continuous_names(x)
  bounds <- .multilpa_wald_bounds(
    result$estimate, result$standard_error,
    .multilpa_interval_kind(result$parameter, result$term, continuous), critical)
  result$conf_low <- bounds$low
  result$conf_high <- bounds$high
  bounded <- result$parameter %in% c("variance", "probability", "response",
                                     "initial_probability",
                                     "transition_probability") |
    (result$parameter == "covariance" &
       result$term %in% paste(continuous, continuous, sep = ":"))
  result$statistic[bounded] <- NA_real_
  result$p_value[bounded] <- NA_real_
  result <- .multilpa_adjust_p(result, adjust)
  names_natural <- .multilpa_parameter_names(labels)
  dimnames(covariance) <- list(names_natural, names_natural)
  attributes(result) <- c(attributes(result), list(
    covariance = covariance,
    covariance_unconstrained = inference$covariance_unconstrained,
    level = level, step = step, method = "wald", vcov_type = vcov_type))
  result
}

.multilpa_transition_covariance <- function(x, data, step, vcov_type) {
  .multilpa_check_transition_regularity(x, vcov_type)
  x_matrix <- x$indicator_data
  if (is.null(x_matrix)) x_matrix <- matrix(numeric(0), x$n_observations, 0L)
  x_matrix <- matrix(as.numeric(x_matrix), nrow(x_matrix), ncol(x_matrix))
  if (!is.null(data)) .multilpa_check_transition_data(x, data)
  centers <- if (ncol(x_matrix) > 0L) colMeans(x_matrix, na.rm = TRUE) else numeric(0)
  centred <- if (ncol(x_matrix) > 0L) sweep(x_matrix, 2L, centers, "-") else x_matrix
  codes <- x$categorical_data
  layout <- .multilpa_sequence_layout(x$group_index, x$time_values, x$n_groups,
                                      x$occasions)
  view <- .multilpa_transition_view(x, centers)
  blocks <- .multilpa_transition_shared_blocks(view, "unconstrained")
  widths <- c(measurement = length(blocks$measurement), group = length(blocks$group))
  theta <- .multilpa_transition_encode(x, "unconstrained", centers)
  stopifnot("the coordinates must match the parameters the fit counts" =
              length(theta) == x$n_parameters)
  negative <- function(value) {
    -.multilpa_transition_expectation(
      centred, layout,
      .multilpa_transition_decode(value, view, widths[["measurement"]],
                                  widths[["group"]]), codes)$log_likelihood
  }
  if (abs(-negative(unname(theta)) - x$log_likelihood) >
      1e-8 * (1 + abs(x$log_likelihood))) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "The stored data do not reproduce the fitted log likelihood.",
      class = "latents_bad_inference_data", call = NULL))
  }
  gradient <- function(value) {
    -colSums(.multilpa_transition_group_scores(value, centred, layout, view,
                                               widths, codes))
  }
  ## Each coordinate on its own unit, as in the cross-sectional path: means in
  ## their indicator's within-profile standard deviation, logits as they are.
  scale <- rep(1, length(theta))
  n_means <- length(x$means)
  if (n_means > 0L) scale[seq_len(n_means)] <- as.vector(t(sqrt(x$variances)))
  dimension <- length(.multilpa_continuous_names(x))
  if (identical(x$covariance_model, "full") && dimension > 0L) {
    covariance_scale <- .multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale(
      x$variances, dimension,
      if (identical(x$variance_model, "equal")) 1L else seq_len(x$n_profiles))
    scale[n_means + seq_along(covariance_scale)] <- covariance_scale
  }
  start <- unname(theta)
  information <- .multilpa_observed_hessian(
    function(displacement) negative(start + displacement * scale),
    function(displacement) gradient(start + displacement * scale) * scale,
    scale, step,
    cache_key = list(path = "transitions", fit = x, indicators = centred,
                     codes = codes, start = start))
  scaled_inverse <- information$inverse
  if (vcov_type %in% c("robust", "opg")) {
    scores <- sweep(.multilpa_transition_group_scores(start, centred, layout, view,
                                                      widths, codes),
                    2L, scale, "*")
    .inference_require_rank(scores[
      .multilpa_inference_groups(x, observed_only = TRUE), , drop = FALSE],
      "The contributing group scores are rank deficient; robust or OPG inference is unavailable.")
    cross <- .multilpa_cross_product(scores)
    scaled_inverse <- if (identical(vcov_type, "opg")) {
      .multilpa_opg_inverse(cross)
    } else .inference_sandwich(scaled_inverse, cross,
                                sum(.multilpa_inference_groups(x)))
  }
  covariance_unconstrained <- scaled_inverse * tcrossprod(scale)
  dimnames(covariance_unconstrained) <- list(names(theta), names(theta))
  jacobian <- .multilpa_transition_jacobian(x, view)
  list(covariance = .inference_delta_covariance(jacobian, covariance_unconstrained),
       covariance_unconstrained = covariance_unconstrained, view = view)
}

vcov.multilpa_transitions <- function(object, data = NULL, step = 1e-4,
                                      vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg"),
                                      scale = c("natural", "unconstrained"), ...) {
  # `type = "robust"`, the name the general transition fit uses, used to fall
  # into `...` and return the observed-information covariance without a word.
  .latents_warn_unused_arguments(list(...), "vcov()",
                                 "Choose the covariance with `vcov_type =`.")

  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  inference <- .multilpa_transition_covariance(object, data, step, vcov_type)
  if (identical(scale, "unconstrained")) {
    covariance <- inference$covariance_unconstrained
    names_used <- .multilpa_parameter_names(.multilpa_transition_labels(
      rownames(covariance), inference$view))
  } else {
    covariance <- inference$covariance
    names_used <- .multilpa_parameter_names(.multilpa_transition_labels(
      names(.multilpa_transition_encode(object, "natural")), inference$view))
  }
  dimnames(covariance) <- list(names_used, names_used)
  covariance
}

review_record.name: .growth_class_key
review_record.purpose: Build growth/trajectory class share and aesthetic keys.

inputs.contract_source: One row per class: share, display rank, label, colour, line type and shape @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.growth_class_key <- function(x) {
  posterior <- .trajectory_view(x)$posterior
  weights <- x$spec$sampling_weights %||% rep(1, nrow(posterior))
  share <- colSums(posterior * weights) / sum(weights)
  n_classes <- length(share)
  ordering <- order(-share, seq_len(n_classes))
  rank <- integer(n_classes)
  rank[ordering] <- seq_len(n_classes)
  label <- sprintf("Class %d (%s)", seq_len(n_classes), .gg_percent(share))
  data.frame(class = .growth_class_names(x), rank = rank, share = share,
             label = factor(label, levels = label[ordering]),
             # The grey is kept for terms shared by every class.
             colour = rep_len(.gg_class_palette, n_classes)[rank],
             linetype = rep_len(c("solid", "dashed", "dotdash", "longdash", "twodash",
                                  "dotted"), n_classes)[rank],
             shape = rep_len(.gg_shapes, n_classes)[rank],
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

review_record.name: .growth_spread
review_record.purpose: Compute population random-effect spread around class means.

inputs.contract_source: Where `spread` of each class's persons' trajectories lie  From the random effects alone: mean +- z sqrt(z(t)' G z(t)), with other random-effect variables at their typical values. @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.growth_spread <- function(x, bands, time, spread) {
  if (spread <= 0) return(NULL)
  grid <- unique(bands$trajectory_time)
  variables <- setdiff(all.vars(x$spec$random), x$spec$id)
  rows <- if (length(variables) == 0L) data.frame(row = seq_along(grid)) else
    .mixture_typical_rows(x$spec$model_data[unique(c(time, variables))], time, grid)
  random_design <- stats::model.matrix(x$spec$random, rows)
  covariances <- .growth_covariances(x$spec, x$params)
  z <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - spread) / 2)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(covariances), function(k) {
    variance <- rowSums((random_design %*% covariances[[k]]) * random_design)
    mean <- bands$estimate[bands$class == .growth_class_names(x)[k]]
    data.frame(class = .growth_class_names(x)[k], trajectory_time = grid,
               spread_low = mean - z * sqrt(variance), spread_high = mean + z * sqrt(variance),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}

inputs.contract_source: @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.growth_plot_trajectories <- function(x, key, time, facet, max_persons, spread, level,
                                      main, subtitle) {
  time <- .growth_time_variable(x, time)
  bands <- as.data.frame(.growth_trajectory_table(x, level, .trajectory_inference(x),
                                                  time))
  bands$trajectory_time <- bands[[time]]
  label_of <- function(class) key$label[match(class, key$class)]
  bands$class_label <- label_of(bands$class)
  spread_band <- if (inherits(x, "latents_growth_mixture")) {
    .growth_spread(x, bands, time, spread)
  }
  means <- .growth_observed_means(x, time, level)
  observed <- as.data.frame(.growth_individual_table(x, time))
  observed$trajectory_time <- observed[[time]]
  observed$person <- observed[[x$spec$id]]
  people <- unique(observed[c("person", "class")])
  per_class <- floor(max_persons / nrow(key))
  shown <- if (per_class < 1L) NULL else
    unlist(lapply(split(people$person, people$class), function(ids) {
      ids[unique(round(seq(1, length(ids), length.out = min(length(ids), per_class))))]
    }), use.names = FALSE)
  observed <- observed[observed$person %in% shown, , drop = FALSE]
  observed <- observed[order(observed$person, observed$trajectory_time), , drop = FALSE]
  observed$class_label <- label_of(observed$class)
  layers <- list()
  if (nrow(observed) > 0L) {
    layers$persons <- ggplot2::geom_line(
      data = observed, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, observed, group = person,
                                    colour = class_label),
      alpha = 0.10, linewidth = 0.3)
  }
  if (!is.null(spread_band)) {
    spread_band$class_label <- label_of(spread_band$class)
    layers$spread <- ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
      data = spread_band, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, ymin = spread_low,
                                       ymax = spread_high, fill = class_label),
      alpha = 0.10)
  }
  layers$band <- ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
    data = bands, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high,
                               fill = class_label), alpha = 0.30)
  layers$mean <- ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = bands, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, estimate, colour = class_label,
                               linetype = class_label), linewidth = 1.3)
  if (!is.null(means)) {
    means$class_label <- label_of(means$class)
    layers$observed_errors <- ggplot2::geom_linerange(
      data = means, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, ymin = observed_low, ymax = observed_high,
                                 colour = class_label), linewidth = 0.5)
    layers$observed_means <- ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = means, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, observed_mean, fill = class_label,
                                 shape = class_label), colour = "white", size = 2.4,
      stroke = 0.5)
  }
  caption <- paste(c(
    sprintf("Line and dark band: class mean trajectory and its %s%% confidence band.",
            format(100 * level)),
    if (!is.null(spread_band))
      sprintf("Light band: where %s%% of the class's persons' trajectories lie.",
              format(100 * spread)),
    if (!is.null(means)) "Points: observed class means (posterior-weighted) with intervals.",
    if (nrow(observed) > 0L) "Thin lines: persons, coloured by their most likely class."),
    collapse = "\n")
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() + layers + .growth_scales(key) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = time, y = x$spec$response_name) + .gg_theme()
  description <- if (inherits(x, "latents_growth_mixture")) {
    sprintf("%d persons, %d classes; random %s (%s covariance)", length(x$stats$n),
            x$spec$n_classes, .growth_random_description(x$spec), x$spec$random_covariance)
  } else {
    sprintf("%d persons, %d classes; no random effects (latent class growth)",
            x$spec$n_groups, x$spec$n_classes)
  }
  if (isTRUE(facet)) {
    return(plot + ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ class_label) +
             .gg_titles(main, subtitle, "Class trajectories", description,
                        caption = caption))
  }
  ends <- bands[bands$trajectory_time == max(bands$trajectory_time), , drop = FALSE]
  span <- diff(range(c(bands$conf_low, bands$conf_high,
                       spread_band$spread_low, spread_band$spread_high)))
  ends$label_y <- .gg_spread(ends$estimate, 0.07 * span)
  right <- max(bands$trajectory_time)
  width <- diff(range(bands$trajectory_time))
  plot +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = ends,
                       ggplot2::aes(right + 0.02 * width, label_y, label = class_label,
                                    colour = class_label),
                       hjust = 0, size = 3.7, fontface = "bold") +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(12, 115, 10, 12)) +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle, "Class trajectories", description, caption = caption)
}

inputs.contract_source: @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.growth_plot_individuals <- function(x, key, time, persons, main, subtitle) {
  time <- .growth_time_variable(x, time)
  rows <- as.data.frame(.growth_individual_table(x, time))
  rows$trajectory_time <- rows[[time]]
  rows$person <- rows[[x$spec$id]]
  assignments <- as.data.frame(.growth_assignment_table(x))
  if (length(persons) == 1L && is.numeric(persons)) {
    # Persons spread over each class's range of certainty, from its most to
    # its least clearly classified, so uncertain members are shown too.
    by_class <- split(assignments, assignments$class)
    per_class <- ceiling(persons / length(by_class))
    chosen <- unlist(lapply(by_class, function(members) {
      ranked <- members[[x$spec$id]][order(-members$probability)]
      ranked[unique(round(seq(1, length(ranked), length.out = min(per_class,
                                                                   length(ranked)))))]
    }), use.names = FALSE)
    chosen <- utils::head(chosen, persons)
  } else chosen <- persons
  rows <- rows[rows$person %in% chosen, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition("None of `persons` is in the fitted data.",
                        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  rows$class_label <- key$label[match(rows$class, key$class)]
  probability <- assignments$probability[match(rows$person, assignments[[x$spec$id]])]
  rows$person_label <- factor(sprintf("%s %s \u00b7 %s, p = %.2f", x$spec$id, rows$person,
                                      sub("class_", "class ", rows$class), probability))
  rows <- rows[order(rows$person, rows$trajectory_time), , drop = FALSE]
  ggplot2::ggplot(rows, ggplot2::aes(trajectory_time, colour = class_label)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = class_mean), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = predicted), linewidth = 0.95) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = observed, fill = class_label, shape = class_label),
                        colour = "white", size = 2.2, stroke = 0.4) +

inputs.contract_source: @noRd
