review_record.name: .gg_view_enumeration_quality
review_record.purpose: Draw entropy and minimum AvePP over eligible candidates.

inputs.contract_source: Entropy and lowest AvePP of every candidate, across the grid  The classification-quality view of an enumeration: relative entropy and the lowest average posterior probability (AvePP) of each candidate, at each level, against the number of classes, one line per group-class count (and structure). Higher is sharper. A dashed line marks the AvePP cutoff. A level with one class has neither number, so its panel is left out.  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param measures `"entropy"`, `"avepp"` or both. @param labels `TRUE` labels each series directly while they fit. @param main,subtitle Titles; `NULL` uses the view's own. @param cutoff The AvePP cutoff drawn on the AvePP panels. @return A ggplot object. @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.gg_view_enumeration_quality <- function(x, measures, labels, main, subtitle,
                                         cutoff) {
  grid <- .latents_grid_quality_table(x, cutoff)
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x)
  # A family grid's candidates differ in group classes only, so they go on
  # the x-axis.
  by_classes <- identical(views$axis, "n_group_classes")
  columns <- c(
    if ("entropy" %in% measures) c("Entropy, individuals" = "profile_entropy",
                                   "Entropy, groups" = "group_entropy"),
    if ("avepp" %in% measures) c("Lowest AvePP, individuals" = "avepp_min",
                                 "Lowest AvePP, groups" = "group_avepp_min"))
  present <- columns[vapply(columns, function(column) {
    any(grid$converged %in% TRUE & is.finite(grid[[column]]))
  }, logical(1))]
  if (length(present) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "No converged candidate has two or more classes, so there is no entropy",
      "or AvePP to plot."), class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))
  }
  # With no group level the panels are simply "Entropy" and "Lowest AvePP".
  if (!any(grepl("groups$", names(present)))) {
    names(present) <- sub(", individuals$", "", names(present))
  }
  long <- .gg_enumeration_frame(grid, present, by_classes)
  long$title <- factor(long$title, levels = names(present))
  series_levels <- unique(long$series[order(grid$n_group_classes, grid$model)])
  long$series <- factor(long$series, levels = series_levels)
  ok <- long[long$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
  n_series <- nlevels(long$series)
  colours <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito, n_series), series_levels)
  shapes <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_shapes, n_series), series_levels)
  # As in the criteria view: direct labels fit beside a single panel only.
  labelled <- isTRUE(labels) && n_series > 1L && n_series <= 5L &&
    length(present) == 1L
  legend <- n_series > 1L && !labelled
  guide <- if (legend) "legend" else "none"
  avepp_panels <- grep("AvePP", names(present), value = TRUE)
  reference <- data.frame(title = factor(avepp_panels, levels = names(present)),
                          y = rep(cutoff, length(avepp_panels)))
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(ok, ggplot2::aes(n_profiles, value, colour = series,
                                           group = series)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = series, fill = series),
                        size = 2.3, colour = "white", stroke = 0.6)
  if (nrow(reference) > 0L) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_hline(
      data = reference, ggplot2::aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5)
  }
  if (labelled) {
    ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ok, list(ok$title, ok$series),
                                        drop = TRUE),
                                  \(s) s[which.max(s$n_profiles), ]))
    ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ends, ends$title, drop = TRUE), \(p) {
      span <- diff(range(ok$value[ok$title == p$title[1L]], cutoff))
      p$y <- .gg_spread(p$value, gap = 0.1 * max(span, 1e-8))
      p
    }))
    ends$x <- max(ok$n_profiles) + 0.28
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = ends, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = series, colour = series),
      hjust = 0, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  failures <- sum(!grid$converged)
  plot +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(title), scales = "free_y",
                        ncol = if (length(present) > 2L) 2L else NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = sort(unique(grid[[views$axis]])),
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(0.3, if (labelled) 1.1 else 0.3))) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle, "Classification quality by candidate model",
               sprintf("%d candidates%s; higher is sharper%s", nrow(grid),
                       if (failures == 0L) "" else
                         sprintf(", %d did not converge", failures),
                       if (nrow(reference) == 0L) "" else
                         sprintf("; dashed line: AvePP %s", format(cutoff)))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = sprintf("Number of %s", views$word), y = NULL) +
    .gg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.spacing = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "lines"),
                   strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
                     face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = ggplot2::rel(0.95)),
                   legend.position = if (legend) "bottom" else "none",
                   legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

review_record.name: .latents_named_plot_registry
review_record.purpose: Declare the mapping between named verbs and generic views.

inputs.contract_source: Which view of a fit's own plot() each named plot function draws  The one table behind the named fit plot functions. Each row says that the named function `verb`, given `what`, draws `plot(x, what = view)` for a fit of that `kind` (see `.latents_plot_kind()`). A function, kind and `what` with no row are refused with `.latents_refuse_named_plot()`; a mapping is listed only where the view shows the same quantity, so most kinds map few functions. Profile, class and transition models draw `plot_diagnostics()` from their posteriors at both levels in that function itself, so they have no `plot_diagnostics` rows. @return A `data.frame`, one row per mapped function, kind and `what`:   `kind`, `verb`, `what` (`""` for a function without `what`) and `view`   (the plot() view; `NA` when that plot() draws a single view and takes no   `what`). @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.latents_named_plot_registry <- function() {
  rows <- function(kind, verb, what, view) {
    data.frame(kind = kind, verb = verb, what = what, view = view,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  regressions <- c("growth_mixture", "trajectory_regression",
                   "mixture_regression")
  rbind(
    rows("profile_model", "plot_profiles",
         c("lines", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs"),
         c("profiles", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs")),
    rows("profile_model", c("plot_responses", "plot_sequences",
                            "plot_prevalence", "plot_transitions"), "",
         c("responses", "sequences", "probabilities", "transitions")),
    # The class's curve of the outcome: over time for trajectories, over the
    # first numeric predictor for a regression of observations.
    rows(regressions, "plot_profiles", "lines",
         c("trajectories", "trajectories", "fitted")),
    # Each unit's posterior probability of its most likely class.
    rows(regressions, "plot_diagnostics", "posteriors", "posteriors"),
    rows("group_class_family", "plot_profiles", "lines", "means"),
    rows("cross_level", c("plot_profiles", "plot_prevalence"), c("lines", ""),
         c("profiles", "composition")),
    # The pooled profile means and variances ("measurement"), and the pooled
    # probability of each profile within each group class ("profile"): the
    # prevalence that plot_prevalence() draws for a profile model.
    rows("pooled", c("plot_profiles", "plot_prevalence"), c("lines", ""),
         c("measurement", "profile")),
    rows("general_transitions", "plot_transitions", "", NA_character_))
}

review_record.name: .latents_refuse_named_plot
review_record.purpose: Explain an unsupported named-view request.

inputs.contract_source: Refuse a named plot function a fit has no view for, naming its views  The message lists the views of the fit's own plot() and, for the model kinds other than profile, class and transition models, which named functions draw them. @param x A fitted model. @param verb The named function. @param what Its `what` (`""` for a function without one, `"all"` when no   view of the function is mapped). @return Does not return; raises `latents_nothing_to_plot` (also of class   `latents_bad_argument`, which these refusals had before). @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.latents_refuse_named_plot <- function(x, verb, what = "") {
  asked <- function(verb, what) {
    ifelse(nzchar(what), sprintf("%s(what = \"%s\")", verb, what),
           sprintf("%s()", verb))
  }
  offered <- .latents_plot_offered_views(x)
  offered_text <- if (length(offered) == 0L) "its plot() draws a single view" else
    sprintf("its plot() offers %s",
            paste(sprintf("\"%s\"", offered), collapse = ", "))
  kind <- .latents_plot_kind(x)
  registry <- .latents_named_plot_registry()
  mapped <- if (identical(kind, "profile_model")) registry[0L, ] else
    registry[registry$kind %in% kind, , drop = FALSE]
  named_text <- if (nrow(mapped) == 0L) "" else
    sprintf("; of the named plot functions, %s", paste(
      sprintf("%s draws %s", asked(mapped$verb, mapped$what),
              ifelse(is.na(mapped$view), "it", sprintf("\"%s\"", mapped$view))),
      collapse = " and "))
  stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
    "%s has no view of a `%s` fit: %s%s.", asked(verb, what), class(x)[1L],
    offered_text, named_text),
    class = c("latents_nothing_to_plot", "latents_bad_argument"), call = NULL))
}

inputs.contract_source: @rdname latents-plots @export

plot_tree <- function(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL, n_group_classes = NULL,
                      n_profiles = NULL, model = NULL, candidates = NULL,
                      from = NULL, to = NULL,
                      level = c("individuals", "groups"), combine = FALSE) {
  .latents_require_grid_views(x, "tree", "plot_tree")
  # A family grid's candidates have group classes only, so its tree is theirs.
  if (identical(level, eval(formals(plot_tree)$level)) &&
      identical(.latents_grid_kind(x), "families")) level <- "groups"
  level <- .latents_check_tree_arguments(level, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                                         model, combine)
  candidates <- .latents_tree_candidates(x, candidates, from, to, model)
  if (!is.null(from)) model <- NULL
  .gg_require()
  .gg_view_tree(x, level = level, n_profiles = n_profiles,
                n_group_classes = n_group_classes, model = model,
                candidates = candidates, combine = combine, main = main,
                subtitle = subtitle)
}

.multilpa_draw_view <- function(x, what, data, scale, category, labels,
                                intervals, cell_labels, main, subtitle,
                                statistic = "mean") {
  if (what %in% c("entropy", "posteriors", "avepp")) {
    .multilpa_refuse_noise(x, sprintf("plot(what = \"%s\")", what),
                           class = "latents_nothing_to_plot")
  }
  with_errors <- isTRUE(intervals)
  switch(what,
    profiles = .gg_view_profiles(
      x, scale, labels,
      if (with_errors) .multilpa_mean_error_matrix(x, data), main, subtitle,
      statistic = statistic, intervals = with_errors),
    bars = .gg_view_bars(
      x, scale,
      if (with_errors) .multilpa_mean_error_matrix(x, data),
      main, subtitle),
    heatmap = .gg_view_heatmap(x, main, subtitle),
    raincloud = .gg_view_raincloud(x, scale, main, subtitle),
    parallel = .gg_view_parallel(x, main, subtitle),
    pairs = .gg_view_pairs(x, main, subtitle),
    responses = .gg_view_responses(
      x, category, labels,
      if (with_errors) .multilpa_response_error_table(x, data), main,
      subtitle),
    probabilities = .gg_view_probabilities(x, labels, main, subtitle),
    sequences = .gg_view_sequences(x, labels, cell_labels, main, subtitle),
    transitions = .gg_view_transitions(x, main, subtitle),
    sizes = .gg_view_sizes(x, main, subtitle),
    entropy = .gg_view_entropy(x, main, subtitle),
    posteriors = .gg_view_posteriors(x, main, subtitle),
    avepp = .gg_view_avepp(x, main, subtitle))
}

                                                    "bic_individual",
                                                    "icl_individual"),
                                      combine = TRUE, labels = TRUE,
                                      mark_minimum = TRUE, main = NULL,
                                      subtitle = NULL, ..., cutoff = 0.8,
                                      using = "bic_groups") {
  stopifnot("`x` must be an `multilpa_enumeration` result" =
              inherits(x, "multilpa_enumeration"))
  # The released view names were matched with match.arg(), so their unique
  # abbreviations remain valid alongside the new criterion names.
  if (is.null(what) || identical(what, c("enumeration", "tree"))) {
    what <- "enumeration"
  }
  legacy <- if (is.character(what) && length(what) == 1L && !is.na(what)) {
    pmatch(what, c("enumeration", "tree"))
  } else NA_integer_
  if (!is.na(legacy)) what <- c("enumeration", "tree")[legacy]
  if (identical(what, "tree")) {
    # The tree takes its own arguments; any other is refused by name.
    tree_arguments <- list(...)
    .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
      tree_arguments[setdiff(names(tree_arguments), .latents_tree_arguments())],
      "plot(what = \"tree\")", paste(
        "The tree takes `n_group_classes`, `n_profiles`, `model`, `candidates`,",
        "`from`, `to`, `level`, `combine`, `main` and `subtitle`."))
    # In 0.9.21 `criterion` always had a value and the tree did not use it.
    .latents_warn_unused_arguments(
      if (missing(criterion) || is.null(criterion)) list() else
        list(criterion = criterion),
      "plot(what = \"tree\")", "The tree shows no criterion.")
    return(do.call(plot_tree, c(list(x), tree_arguments,
                                list(combine = if (missing(combine)) FALSE else combine,
                                     main = main, subtitle = subtitle))))
  }
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "plot()", .multilpa_enumeration_plot_advice())
  # 0.9.21 chose the view with `what = "enumeration"` and the criteria with
  # `criterion`; both spellings still draw the same plot.
  what <- .latents_former_argument(
    what, !missing(what) && !identical(what, "enumeration"),
    if (missing(criterion)) NULL else criterion,
    c("what", "criterion"))
  if ("tree" %in% what) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`what = \"tree\"` draws the tree on its own; ask for criteria separately.",
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  # The view's name before criteria were chosen through `what`.
  if (identical(what, "enumeration")) what <- eval(formals(plot_enumeration)$what)
  plot_enumeration(x, what = what, combine = combine, labels = labels,
                   mark_minimum = mark_minimum, main = main,
                   subtitle = subtitle, cutoff = cutoff, using = using)
}

review_record.name: .multilpa_distinct_criteria
review_record.purpose: Deduplicate equivalent criterion panels.

inputs.contract_source: The criteria worth a panel, named for display  A single-level grid has one unit per observation, so every criterion's group-level and individual-level versions are the same numbers; drawing both repeats a panel. Such a pair is kept once under the criterion's plain name. A grid whose every candidate has one group class classifies nothing at the group level, so the group version of a classification criterion (AWE, ICL, CLC) is its penalty alone, and ICL over groups equals BIC over groups. When both versions are asked for, only the individual one is kept, under the criterion's plain name. @param grid The enumeration table. @param criterion Requested criterion columns. @return The criteria to draw, named by their display titles. @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.multilpa_distinct_criteria <- function(grid, criterion) {
  classification <- c("awe", "icl", "clc")
  # An empty table (titles alone) has no candidates to judge.
  no_group_classes <- nrow(grid) > 0L && !is.null(grid$n_group_classes) &&
    all(grid$n_group_classes %in% 1L)
  if (no_group_classes) {
    stems <- sub("_groups$", "", criterion)
    redundant <- grepl("_groups$", criterion) & stems %in% classification &
      paste0(stems, "_individual") %in% criterion
    criterion <- criterion[!redundant]
  }
  base <- sub("_(groups|individual)$", "", criterion)
  level <- ifelse(grepl("_groups$", criterion), "groups",
                  ifelse(grepl("_individual$", criterion), "individuals", ""))
  same_at_both <- vapply(base, function(stem) {
    both <- paste0(stem, c("_groups", "_individual"))
    all(both %in% names(grid)) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(grid[[both[1L]]], grid[[both[2L]]]))
  }, logical(1))
  plain <- same_at_both | !nzchar(level) |
    (no_group_classes & base %in% classification & level == "individuals")
  keep <- !duplicated(ifelse(same_at_both, base, criterion))
  titles <- ifelse(plain, toupper(base), sprintf("%s (%s)", toupper(base), level))
  stats::setNames(criterion[keep], titles[keep])
}

                                                 "raincloud", "parallel",

                                                 "sequences", "sizes",
                                                 "entropy", "posteriors",

                                     data = NULL,
                                     scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
                                     category = "last", labels = TRUE,
                                     intervals = TRUE, cell_labels = TRUE,
                                     main = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                                     ..., statistic = c("mean", "median", "mode")) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted `multilpa_covariates` model" =
              inherits(x, "multilpa_covariates"))
  .multilpa_check_plot_arguments(list(...), labels, intervals, cell_labels,
                                 category)
  # Asked for by name or by a unique abbreviation, as match.arg() would take
  # it, so "prob" gets the reason too rather than a bare match.arg() error.
  offered <- c(eval(formals(plot.multilpa_covariates)$what), "probabilities")
  asks_prevalence <- is.character(what) && length(what) == 1L && !is.na(what) &&
    identical(offered[pmatch(what, offered)], "probabilities")
  if (asks_prevalence) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      paste("A covariate model has no single profile prevalence: it varies with",
            "each unit's covariates. Use parameter_inference() for the logits."),
      class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))

    return(.gg_every_view(x, match.call(), parent.frame()))

                      category = category, labels = labels,

                      main = main, subtitle = subtitle, statistic = statistic)

review_record.name: .multilpa_mean_error_matrix
review_record.purpose: Retrieve or explain unavailable Gaussian mean errors.

inputs.contract_source: Measurement standard errors shaped like the means matrix  @param x A fitted model. @param data The data frame the model was fitted to, or `NULL` to use the   columns the fit carries. @return A profiles-by-indicators matrix of standard errors; or a single   string saying why there are none, for the plot's subtitle. @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.multilpa_mean_error_matrix <- function(x, data) {
  # A fit carries the columns it was built from, so the intervals cost the
  # caller nothing to ask for and are drawn by default. Families whose standard
  # errors are not implemented refuse by condition class; the means are still
  # worth drawing without whiskers, so the refusal is caught and reported as
  # a reason rather than propagated out of a plot call. The reason travels to
  # the subtitle, so a plot without whiskers says why.
  because <- function(reason) function(condition) reason
  errors <- tryCatch(
    .multilpa_measurement_errors(x, .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)),
    latents_unsupported_inference = because("no intervals for this model"),
    latents_unsupported_noise = because("no intervals with a noise component"),
    latents_singular_information = because("no intervals: singular information"),
    latents_incomplete_fit = because("no intervals: incomplete fit"),
    latents_bad_inference_data = because("no intervals: data do not reproduce the fit"),
    latents_boundary_fit = because("no intervals: an estimate is at its bound"),
    latents_no_converge = because("no intervals: the fit did not converge"))
  if (is.character(errors)) return(errors)
  vars <- .multilpa_continuous_names(x)
  cells <- expand.grid(indicator = vars, profile = seq_len(x$n_profiles),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  values <- .multilpa_match_error(errors, "mean", cells$profile, cells$indicator)
  if (all(is.na(values))) return("no intervals for this model")
  matrix(values, x$n_profiles, length(vars), byrow = TRUE)
}

.multilpa_response_error_table <- function(x, data) {
  because <- function(reason) function(condition) reason
  # Probabilities on their bound are held there, so every other one keeps its
  # interval instead of one bound-active probability removing them all.
  tryCatch(
    {
      inference <- parameter_inference(x, .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data),
                                       boundary = "fix")
      inference <- inference[inference$level == "measurement", , drop = FALSE]
      attr(inference, "held") <- length(attr(inference, "fixed_at_bound") %||%
                                          character()) > 0L
      inference
    },
    latents_unsupported_inference = because("no intervals for this model"),
    latents_unsupported_noise = because("no intervals with a noise component"),
    latents_singular_information = because("no intervals: singular information"),
    latents_incomplete_fit = because("no intervals: incomplete fit"),
    latents_bad_inference_data = because("no intervals: data do not reproduce the fit"),
    latents_boundary_fit = because("no intervals: a probability is at its bound"),
    latents_no_converge = because("no intervals: the fit did not converge"))
}

inputs.exact_source:
predict.multilpa <- function(object, newdata = NULL,
                             type = c("class", "posterior", "density"), ...) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  prepared <- if (is.null(newdata)) .multilpa_training_rows(object) else
    .multilpa_prediction_rows(object, newdata)
  parameters <- object[intersect(c("means", "variances", "covariances",
                                   "profile_probabilities",
                                   "group_probabilities",
                                   "response_probabilities", "ordinal_intercepts",
                                   "ordinal_locations", "count_means",
                                   "count_dispersion", "direct_effects"),
                                 names(object))]
  if (isTRUE(object$noise)) {
    # The fit reports the noise share apart from the Gaussian profiles' shares
    # (together they sum to one); the E-step takes it as a last column.
    parameters$profile_probabilities <- cbind(parameters$profile_probabilities,
                                              noise = object$noise_probability)
    parameters$noise_log_density <- rep(-log(object$hypervolume),
                                        nrow(prepared$x))
  }
  if (identical(type, "density")) {
    return(data.frame(row = prepared$rows,
                      log_density = .multilpa_row_log_density(
                        prepared, parameters)))
  }
  expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(prepared$x, prepared$group_index,
                                       parameters, prepared$codes,
                                       extra = prepared$extra)
  .multilpa_prediction_table(object, prepared, expectation,
                             posteriors = identical(type, "posterior"))
}

inputs.exact_source:
.multilpa_row_log_density <- function(prepared, parameters) {
  shares <- drop(parameters$group_probabilities %*%
                   parameters$profile_probabilities)
  single <- parameters
  single$profile_probabilities <- matrix(shares, nrow = 1L)
  single$group_probabilities <- 1
  expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(prepared$x,
                                       seq_len(nrow(prepared$x)), single,
                                       prepared$codes, extra = prepared$extra)
  expectation$group_log_likelihood
}

review_record.name: .multilpa_prediction_table
review_record.purpose: Return row assignments, certainty and optional posterior columns.

inputs.contract_source: Tidy prediction table @noRd
inputs.exact_source:
.multilpa_prediction_table <- function(object, prepared, expectation,
                                       posteriors) {
  posterior <- expectation$subject_posteriors
  noisy <- isTRUE(object$noise)
  modal <- max.col(posterior, ties.method = "first")
  n_profiles <- object$n_profiles
  table <- data.frame(row = prepared$rows)
  if (prepared$two_level) table[[object$id]] <- prepared$groups
  table$profile <- ifelse(noisy & modal == ncol(posterior), 0L, modal)
  table$posterior <- posterior[cbind(seq_len(nrow(posterior)), modal)]
  if (prepared$two_level && object$n_group_classes > 1L) {
    group_modal <- max.col(expectation$group_posteriors, ties.method = "first")
    table$group_class <- group_modal[prepared$group_index]
    table$group_posterior <- expectation$group_posteriors[
      cbind(prepared$group_index, table$group_class)]
  }
  if (posteriors) {
    columns <- paste0("probability_profile_", seq_len(n_profiles))
    if (noisy) columns <- c(columns, "probability_noise")
    probability <- as.data.frame(posterior)
    names(probability) <- columns
    table <- cbind(table, probability)
  }
  table
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_assignments <- function(x, data = NULL, truth = NULL) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x))
  frame <- .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)
  .multilpa_check_row_count(x, frame)
  .multilpa_check_alignment(x, frame)
  # A noise component is one more class: profile 0, as mclust numbers it, with
  # its own posterior column.
  class_posteriors <- .multilpa_class_posteriors(x)
  posteriors <- as.data.frame(unname(class_posteriors))
  names(posteriors) <- c(sprintf("posterior_profile_%d", seq_len(x$n_profiles)),
                         if (isTRUE(x$noise)) "posterior_noise")
  # How much of this row's membership the modal profile did not account for.
  # Modal assignment throws it away, so the table that reports the assignment
  # reports what reporting it cost.
  # A posterior that rounds to 1 + 2e-16 would otherwise report a negative
  # uncertainty; the estimates themselves are left as computed.
  uncertainty <- pmax(1 - apply(class_posteriors, 1L, max), 0)
  labels <- data.frame(profile = x$subject_profiles)
  # A single-level fit has one group class that every row belongs to, so the
  # column would say nothing.
  if (!is.null(x$group_classes) && !isTRUE(x$single_level)) {
    labels$group_class <- x$group_classes[x$group_index]
  }
  added <- cbind(labels, uncertainty = uncertainty, posteriors)
  clashes <- intersect(names(frame), names(added))
  if (length(clashes) > 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "`data` already has a column named %s, which the assignments would overwrite.",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", clashes), collapse = ", ")),
      class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  result <- cbind(frame, added)
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  if (is.null(truth)) return(result)
  .multilpa_recovery_frame(result, truth, x)
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_recovery_rows <- function(name, joined, x) {
  values <- joined[[name]]
  # Which level a truth column describes is read off the data, not guessed: a
  # column taking one value within every group is a property of the group, and
  # one that varies inside any group cannot be.
  #
  # That reading needs groups with something inside them. Where every group
  # holds one observation -- an `id = NULL` fit, or a two-level fit with no
  # repeated units -- "constant within group" is true of every column by
  # construction, and the test would send every truth column to the group level
  # and cross-tabulate it against a group class that is the same for all of
  # them. There is no group-level question to ask of singleton groups, so the
  # answer is the profile.
  #
  # The sizes are counted from the group index every fit carries: a covariate
  # fit stores no `group_sizes`, and `max()` of that absent field sent every
  # group-level truth to the profile comparison.
  grouped <- !is.null(x$group_classes) &&
    max(tabulate(x$group_index)) > 1L &&
    .multilpa_constant_within(values, x$group_index)
  assignment <- if (grouped) "group_class" else "profile"
  # A group-level truth labels groups, not the observations inside them.
  # Counting every row would give larger groups more weight in recovery.
  units <- if (grouped) !duplicated(x$group_index) else
    rep(TRUE, length(values))
  values <- values[units]
  assigned <- joined[[assignment]][units]
  # `useNA = "ifany"` so a missing label is a visible value rather than a row
  # that quietly leaves the table.
  tabulation <- table(class = assigned, value = values, useNA = "ifany")
  # Factors may retain unused levels. They have no units and hence no
  # defined within-truth proportion; only observed truth values are rows.
  tabulation <- tabulation[, colSums(tabulation) > 0L, drop = FALSE]
  counts <- as.data.frame(tabulation, responseName = "n",
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  data.frame(
    assignment = assignment,
    class = as.integer(counts$class),
    truth = name,
    value = counts$value,
    n = counts$n,
    # Within a truth value, so the column reads as the share of the units
    # carrying that label which the model put in each class.
    proportion = as.vector(sweep(tabulation, 2L, colSums(tabulation), "/")),
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

.multilpa_profile_frame <- function(x, data = NULL,
                                    scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
                                    standard_errors = !is.null(data)) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  vars <- .multilpa_continuous_names(x)
  n_profiles <- x$n_profiles
  # `spread` of one and `centre` of zero leave the raw scale untouched, so the
  # two scales share one code path and cannot drift apart.
  basis <- if (identical(scale, "standardized") && length(vars) > 0L) {
    .multilpa_standardization(x, vars)
  } else {
    list(centre = rep(0, length(vars)),
         spread = rep(1, length(vars)))
  }
  means <- sweep(sweep(x$means, 2L, basis$centre, "-"), 2L, basis$spread, "/")
  variances <- sweep(x$variances, 2L, basis$spread^2, "/")
  frame <- data.frame(
    profile = rep(seq_len(n_profiles), each = length(vars)),
    indicator = rep(vars, times = n_profiles),
    mean = as.vector(t(means)),
    variance = as.vector(t(variances)),
    # Derived rather than read from the fit, because not every result class
    # stores a standard-deviation matrix.
    standard_deviation = sqrt(as.vector(t(variances))))
  if (!isTRUE(standard_errors)) return(frame)
  # An all-categorical fit has no Gaussian rows, but its table keeps the
  # columns every other fit's has, so a caller can bind or select them.
  if (nrow(frame) == 0L) {
    frame$mean_standard_error <- numeric()
    frame$variance_standard_error <- numeric()
    return(frame)
  }
  errors <- .multilpa_table_errors(x, data)
  if (is.null(errors)) {
    frame$mean_standard_error <- NA_real_
    frame$variance_standard_error <- NA_real_
    return(frame)
  }
  row_spread <- rep(basis$spread, times = n_profiles)
  # Standardizing divides each estimate by a constant, so its standard error
  # divides by the same constant; a table must not mix the two scales.
  frame$mean_standard_error <- .multilpa_match_error(errors, "mean",
    frame$profile, frame$indicator) / row_spread
  frame$variance_standard_error <- .multilpa_variance_error(
    errors, frame$profile, frame$indicator) / row_spread^2
  frame
}

.multilpa_probability_frame <- function(x) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be an `multilpa` fit, or its summary" =
              inherits(x, "multilpa") || inherits(x, "summary_multilpa"))
  n_types <- x$n_group_classes
  n_profiles <- x$n_profiles
  frame <- data.frame(
    group_class = rep(seq_len(n_types), each = n_profiles),
    profile = rep(seq_len(n_profiles), times = n_types),
    probability = as.vector(t(x$profile_probabilities)),
    group_class_probability = rep(unname(x$group_probabilities), each = n_profiles))
  if (!isTRUE(x$noise)) return(frame)
  # The noise component's share, as profile 0 (one group class only).
  rbind(frame, data.frame(group_class = 1L, profile = 0L,
                          probability = x$noise_probability,
                          group_class_probability = unname(x$group_probabilities[1L])))
}

.multilpa_posterior_frame <- function(x, format = "long") {
  stopifnot("`format` must be \"long\" or \"wide\"" =
              format %in% c("long", "wide"))
  # A noise component is class 0, the last posterior column.
  class_posteriors <- .multilpa_class_posteriors(x)
  classes <- c(seq_len(x$n_profiles), if (isTRUE(x$noise)) 0L)
  modal <- classes[max.col(class_posteriors, ties.method = "first")]
  if (identical(format, "wide")) {
    posteriors <- as.data.frame(unname(class_posteriors))
    names(posteriors) <- c(sprintf("posterior_profile_%d", seq_len(x$n_profiles)),
                           if (isTRUE(x$noise)) "posterior_noise")
    return(cbind(data.frame(row = seq_len(x$n_observations),
                            group = x$group_values[x$group_index],
                            profile = modal),
                 posteriors))
  }
  # One row per individual and profile. The wide form's column set grows with the
  # number of profiles, so no caller can address it generically; it stays
  # available because joining posteriors back onto the fitting data wants one row
  # per individual, but it is no longer what the accessor hands back by default.
  data.frame(
    row = rep(seq_len(x$n_observations), times = length(classes)),
    group = rep(x$group_values[x$group_index], times = length(classes)),
    profile = rep(classes, each = x$n_observations),
    posterior = as.vector(class_posteriors),
    modal = rep(classes, each = x$n_observations) ==
      rep(modal, times = length(classes)))
}

  modal <- max.col(x$group_posteriors, ties.method = "first")
  sizes <- tabulate(x$group_index, nbins = length(x$group_values))
  if (identical(format, "long")) {
    n_groups <- length(x$group_values)
    return(data.frame(
      group = rep(x$group_values, times = x$n_group_classes),
      group_size = rep(sizes, times = x$n_group_classes),
      log_likelihood = rep(unname(x$group_log_likelihood),
                           times = x$n_group_classes),
      group_class = rep(seq_len(x$n_group_classes), each = n_groups),
      posterior = as.vector(x$group_posteriors),
      modal = rep(seq_len(x$n_group_classes), each = n_groups) ==
        rep(modal, times = x$n_group_classes)))
  }
  posteriors <- as.data.frame(unname(x$group_posteriors))
  names(posteriors) <- sprintf("posterior_group_class_%d", seq_len(x$n_group_classes))
  # Sizes and modal classes are derived rather than read from the fit, because
  # not every result class stores them as fields.
  cbind(data.frame(group = x$group_values,
                   group_size = sizes,
                   group_class = modal,
                   log_likelihood = unname(x$group_log_likelihood)),
        posteriors)
}

print.multilpa_enumeration <- function(x, ...) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be an `multilpa_enumeration` result" =
              inherits(x, "multilpa_enumeration"))
  table <- .multilpa_enumeration_grid(x)
  cat(sprintf("Class enumeration: %d candidate models%s\n", nrow(table),
              .latents_enumeration_type_label(x)))
  columns <- intersect(c("candidate", "n_profiles", "n_group_classes", "model",
                         "log_likelihood", "n_parameters", "aic", "bic_groups",
                         "bic_individual", "icl_individual", "profile_entropy",
                         "group_entropy", "avepp_min", "avepp_max",
                         "avepp_mean", "avepp_below",
                         "group_avepp_min", "group_avepp_max",
                         "group_avepp_mean", "group_avepp_below",
                         "converged", "boundary",
                         "n_best_replicated"),
                       names(table))
  # A column with no value in any row (the covariance structure of an LCA
  # grid) carries nothing to read.
  columns <- columns[vapply(columns, function(column) !all(is.na(table[[column]])),
                            logical(1))]
  print(table[, columns, drop = FALSE], row.names = FALSE, ...)
  # A candidate that produced no fit is reported apart from one that was
  # fitted but stopped short of convergence: the remedies differ.
  failed <- is.na(table$log_likelihood)
  unconverged <- !failed & !(table$converged %in% TRUE)
  if (any(failed)) {
    cat(sprintf(paste("%d candidate(s) failed to fit; the `error` column of",
                      "as.data.frame(x) gives the reason.\n"), sum(failed)))
  }
  if (any(unconverged)) {
    cat(sprintf("%d candidate(s) were fitted but did not converge; see as.data.frame(x).\n",
                sum(unconverged)))
  }
  cat("No candidate is selected automatically. Compare one convention consistently.\n")
  invisible(x)
}

.multilpa_start_response_frame <- function(x) {
  blocks <- x$response_probabilities
  if (length(blocks) == 0L) {
    return(data.frame(profile = integer(), indicator = integer(),
                      category = integer(), probability = numeric()))
  }
  ## A start now carries the indicator and category labels when it came from
  ## `starting_values()`, and those are what a reader wants to see -- the fitted
  ## object's own response table reports them. An unlabelled start, which is
  ## still a supported input, has only positions to report, so fall back to them
  ## rather than inventing names.
  block_names <- names(blocks)
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(blocks), function(indicator) {
    block <- as.matrix(blocks[[indicator]])
    categories <- colnames(block)
    data.frame(profile = rep(seq_len(nrow(block)), times = ncol(block)),
               indicator = if (is.null(block_names)) indicator else
                 block_names[indicator],
               category = if (is.null(categories))
                 rep(seq_len(ncol(block)), each = nrow(block)) else
                 rep(categories, each = nrow(block)),
               probability = as.vector(block),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

review_record.name: compare_models
review_record.purpose: Compare fitted models on the same data  Returns a table with one row per model giving its log likelihood, number of parameters, information criteria, classification quality and convergence, together with `delta_bic`, each model's BIC above the smallest, and `bic_weight`, the Schwarz weight `exp(-delta_bic / 2)` normalised over the models compared (Wagenmakers and Farrell 2004). The weight is the approximate posterior probability of each model, assuming one of them is true and all have equal prior probability. No row is marked as best.  Information criteria are comparable only on the same data: every model must be fitted to the same outcome or indicators, persons (or groups) and observations, or the comparison is refused.  Candidates of an enumeration grid are selected by name, as the grid's `candidate` column shows them (`compare_models(grid, "profiles3_groups4", "profiles3_groups5")`), or by class counts (`compare_models(grid, c(3, 4), c(3, 5))`, where a single number means one group class). Alternatively, `n_profiles` and `n_group_classes` select candidates: `compare_models(grid, n_profiles = 3)` compares every candidate with 3 profiles, and `compare_models(grid)` compares them all. Latent class grids work the same way, with `classes` in the names, and the `n_profiles` column counting classes. Fits from [multilpa()], [lpa()], [lca()], [lta()] or [get_candidate()] can also be passed directly.

documented_contracts: ... Either an enumeration grid from [enumerate_classes()] followed   by the candidates to compare (none for all of them, or a selection   through `n_profiles` and `n_group_classes`); or two or more fits from   [multilpa()], [lpa()], [lca()], [lta()] or [get_candidate()]; or two or   more fits from [mixture_regression()] (with or without `random`). Named   fits are labelled by their names, unnamed fits by their expression, and   candidates by their candidate name. Labels must be distinct.
n_profiles,n_group_classes With a grid, the class counts of the   candidates to compare; `NULL` (the default) takes every count. Candidates   whose fit failed are left out, with a message.

cutoff For profile and class models, the average posterior   probability below which a class is counted in `avepp_below` and   `group_avepp_below`; a single number in (0, 1], default 0.8. Not used for   mixture regressions.

plot.latents_comparison <- function(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL, ...) {
  .latents_warn_unused_arguments(
    list(...), "plot()",
    "Style the returned plot with ggplot2, for example `+ ggplot2::theme()`.")
  .gg_require()
  table <- as.data.frame(x)
  # Profile and class models report each criterion under the groups
  # convention, mixture regressions under one name.
  criteria <- c(aic = "AIC", bic = "BIC", bic_groups = "BIC", sabic = "SABIC",
                sabic_groups = "SABIC")
  criteria <- criteria[names(criteria) %in% names(table)]
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(criteria), function(column) {
    data.frame(model = factor(table$model, levels = table$model),
               criterion = factor(criteria[[column]], levels = unname(criteria)),
               value = table[[column]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  ggplot2::ggplot(long, ggplot2::aes(model, value, group = criterion,
                                     colour = criterion, shape = criterion)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.6) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = .gg_okabe_ito[c(1L, 4L, 3L)]) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = c(16L, 17L, 15L)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Information criterion (lower is better)") +
    .gg_theme() + .gg_top_legend() +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle, "Model comparison",
               "Each criterion across the compared models")
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_compare_fits <- function(fits, labels, cutoff) {
  if (length(fits) < 2L) {
    stop(errorCondition("`compare_models()` needs two or more fits.",
                        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(labels)) {
    stop(errorCondition("Every model needs a distinct name.",
                        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  stopifnot("`cutoff` must be a single number between 0 and 1" =
              is.numeric(cutoff) && length(cutoff) == 1L && is.finite(cutoff) &&
              cutoff > 0 && cutoff <= 1)
  # The data a likelihood is computed on: the same units in the same groups
  # with the same indicator values.
  signature <- .latents_comparison_signature
  reference <- signature(fits[[1L]])
  same <- vapply(fits, function(fit) isTRUE(all.equal(signature(fit), reference)),
                 logical(1))
  if (!all(same)) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "%s %s fitted to different data from %s: information criteria compare",
      "models only on the same indicators and observations."),
      paste(labels[!same], collapse = ", "), if (sum(!same) > 1L) "are" else "is",
      labels[1L]), class = "latents_incomparable_models", call = NULL))
  }
  statistics <- c("min", "max", "mean", "below")
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(fits), function(i) {
    fit <- fits[[i]]
    level_summary <- function(posteriors, prefix) {
      values <- .multilpa_avepp_summary(posteriors, cutoff)
      columns <- as.data.frame(as.list(stats::setNames(values,
                                                       paste0(prefix, statistics))))
      columns[[paste0(prefix, "below")]] <- as.integer(values[["below"]])
      columns
    }
    diagnostic <- .latents_comparison_diagnostic_view(fit)
    # Shares are of the rows the fit counts (see `drop_empty`), with the
    # weights of those rows.
    counted <- .multilpa_classified_posteriors(diagnostic)
    weights <- .multilpa_level_weights(diagnostic, "individuals", nrow(counted)) %||% 1
    counts <- fit$effective_profile_counts %||%
      colSums(counted[, seq_len(ncol(fit$subject_posteriors)), drop = FALSE] * weights)
    # Noise is outside the Gaussian profiles, but still occupies sample mass.
    # Profile shares are relative to all classified observations, not to the
    # Gaussian portion alone.
    total <- sum(counted * weights)
    shares <- counts / total
    cbind(
      data.frame(model = labels[i], n_profiles = as.integer(fit$n_profiles),
                 n_group_classes = as.integer(fit$n_group_classes %||% 1L),
                 structure = if (length(.multilpa_continuous_names(fit)) == 0L)
                   NA_character_ else .latents_comparison_structure(fit),
                 n_parameters = as.integer(fit$n_parameters),
                 log_likelihood = fit$log_likelihood, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      .multilpa_enumeration_indices(diagnostic),
      data.frame(profile_entropy = .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(fit)),
                 group_entropy = if (is.null(fit$group_posteriors)) NA_real_ else
                   .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(fit))),
      level_summary(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(fit), "avepp_"),
      level_summary(.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(fit), "group_avepp_"),
      data.frame(smallest_share = if (length(shares) == 0L) NA_real_ else min(shares),
                 converged = isTRUE(fit$converged),
                 n_best_replicated = fit$n_best_replicated %||% NA_integer_))
  })
  table <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  table$delta_bic <- table$bic_groups - min(table$bic_groups)
  relative <- exp(-table$delta_bic / 2)
  table$bic_weight <- relative / sum(relative)
  column <- .latents_column
  delta <- if (isTRUE(l10n_info()$`UTF-8`)) "\u0394BIC" else "dBIC"
  # The printed view names latent classes as classes, and leaves out the
  # group columns when no model compared has group classes; the table itself
  # keeps every column.
  latent_class <- all(vapply(fits, function(fit)
    length(.multilpa_continuous_names(fit)) == 0L, logical(1)))
  grouped <- any(table$n_group_classes > 1L)
  table <- .latents_table(table, title = "Model comparison", display = c(
    list(column("Model", "model", "text"),
         column(if (latent_class) "Classes" else "Profiles", "n_profiles",
                "integer")),
    if (grouped) list(column("Group classes", "n_group_classes", "integer")),
    list(column("k", "n_parameters", "integer"), column("LogLik", "log_likelihood"),
         column("BIC", "bic_groups"), column(delta, "delta_bic"),
         column("Weight", "bic_weight", "share"),
         column("ICL", "icl_individual"), column("Entropy", "profile_entropy"),
         column("Min AvePP", "avepp_min"),
         column(sprintf("< %g", cutoff), "avepp_below", "integer")),
    if (grouped) list(column("Group entropy", "group_entropy"),
                      column("Group min AvePP", "group_avepp_min"))))
  # No row is marked: delta_bic and bic_weight carry the evidence, and the
  # choice stays with the reader.
  attr(table, "models") <- stats::setNames(fits, labels)
  class(table) <- c("latents_comparison", class(table))
  table
}

.latents_comparison_signature <- function(fit) {
  general <- inherits(fit, "multilpa_lta")
  raw <- if (general) sweep(fit$x, 2L, fit$centers, "+") else
    .multilpa_uncentered_indicators(fit)
  # Engines use different storage types for an absent Gaussian block.
  if (!is.null(raw) && ncol(raw) == 0L) raw <- NULL
  # Categorical responses as their labels, item by item: a model that pairs
  # two items jointly is fitted to the same data as one that does not.
  list(vars = fit$original_vars %||% fit$vars,
       id = if (isTRUE(fit$single_level)) NULL else fit$id,
       groups = as.character(fit$group_values %||% fit$group_ids),
       group_index = fit$group_index, indicators = raw,
       categorical = .latents_categorical_labels(fit),
       extra = .latents_draw_extra_columns(fit$extra_data),
       weights = unname(fit$sampling_weights), time = fit$time_values,
       centering = fit$centering %||% "none",
       scaling = fit$scaling %||% "none",
       drop_empty = fit$drop_empty %||% TRUE)
}

  definitions <- c(deviance = "-2L",
                   aic = "-2L + 2q",
                   kic = "-2L + 3(q + 1)",
                   bic = "-2L + q log(n)",
                   sabic = "-2L + q log((n + 2) / 24)",
                   caic = "-2L + q (log(n) + 1)",
                   awe = "-2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n))",
                   icl = "-2L + q log(n) + 2 EN",
                   clc = "-2L + 2 EN")
  stopifnot("Every criterion must have a definition" =
              all(criterion %in% names(definitions)))
  unname(definitions[criterion])
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_information_criteria <- function(x, definitions = FALSE,
                                 format = c("wide", "long")) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x),
            "`definitions` must be TRUE or FALSE" =
              isTRUE(definitions) || isFALSE(definitions))
  format <- match.arg(format)
  if (isTRUE(definitions) && identical(format, "wide")) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`definitions` describes one criterion per row, which the wide form has not. Use format = \"long\".",
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  q <- x$n_parameters
  deviance <- -2 * x$log_likelihood
  conventions <- data.frame(
    convention = c("groups", "individuals"),
    n = c(.multilpa_group_sample_size(x),
          x$n_informative %||% x$n_observations))
  entropies <- c(groups = if (is.null(x$group_posteriors)) NA_real_ else
                   .multilpa_entropy_sum(.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(x)),
                 individuals = .multilpa_entropy_sum(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(x)))
  scale_free <- data.frame(
    criterion = c("deviance", "aic", "kic"),
    convention = NA_character_, n = NA_integer_,
    penalty = c(0, 2 * q, 3 * (q + 1)))
  scaled <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(conventions)), function(row) {
    convention <- conventions$convention[row]
    n <- conventions$n[row]
    entropy_sum <- entropies[[convention]]
    penalties <- c(bic = q * log(n),
                   sabic = q * log((n + 2) / 24),
                   caic = q * (log(n) + 1),
                   awe = 2 * q * (1.5 + log(n)) + 2 * entropy_sum,
                   icl = q * log(n) + 2 * entropy_sum,
                   # The only criterion here that does not use the sample size.
                   # Its convention still matters, because it decides which
                   # level's classification uncertainty is being penalized.
                   clc = 2 * entropy_sum)
    data.frame(criterion = names(penalties), convention = convention, n = n,
               penalty = unname(penalties))
  }))
  result <- rbind(scale_free, scaled)
  # Every row is the same deviance plus its own penalty, so the `value` column
  # means one thing throughout: smaller is a better-supported model. The penalty
  # itself is not a column: nobody reports it, and it is the difference between
  # two numbers the table already carries.
  result$value <- deviance + result$penalty
  result <- result[c("criterion", "convention", "n", "value")]
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  if (identical(format, "wide")) return(.multilpa_criteria_wide(result, x))
  if (isTRUE(definitions)) {
    result$definition <- .multilpa_criterion_definitions(result$criterion)
  }
  result
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_classification_summary <- function(probabilities, level, weights = NULL) {
  average <- .multilpa_average_posterior_matrix(probabilities)
  n_classes <- ncol(probabilities)
  classes <- seq_len(n_classes)
  assigned <- max.col(probabilities, ties.method = "first")
  n_modal <- tabulate(assigned, nbins = n_classes)
  estimated_n <- if (is.null(weights)) colSums(probabilities) else
    colSums(probabilities * weights)
  estimated_proportion <- estimated_n /
    if (is.null(weights)) nrow(probabilities) else sum(weights)
  diagonal <- average[cbind(classes, classes)]
  data.frame(level = level, class = .multilpa_class_labels(probabilities),
             n_modal = n_modal,
             proportion_modal = n_modal / nrow(probabilities),
             estimated_n = estimated_n,
             estimated_proportion = estimated_proportion,
             average_posterior = diagonal,
             odds_correct_classification =
               .multilpa_odds_correct(diagonal, estimated_proportion))
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_odds_correct <- function(average, proportion) {
  stopifnot("`average` and `proportion` must have equal length" =
              length(average) == length(proportion))
  sized <- !is.na(average) & !is.na(proportion) & proportion > 0 & proportion < 1
  # Within rounding of one, 1 - average is floating-point noise, and dividing
  # by it would report odds such as 7e15 that measure only that noise.
  perfect <- sized & average >= 1 - sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
  defined <- sized & !perfect & average > 0
  odds <- rep(NA_real_, length(average))
  odds[perfect] <- Inf
  odds[defined] <- (average[defined] / (1 - average[defined])) /
    (proportion[defined] / (1 - proportion[defined]))
  odds
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_entropy_table <- function(x) {
  stopifnot("`object` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x))
  posteriors <- list(individuals = .multilpa_classified_posteriors(x),
                     groups = .multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(x))
  posteriors <- Filter(Negate(is.null), posteriors)
  result <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(posteriors), function(level) {
    probabilities <- posteriors[[level]]
    data.frame(level = level, n_classes = ncol(probabilities),
               n_units = nrow(probabilities),
               entropy_sum = .multilpa_entropy_sum(probabilities),
               relative_entropy = .multilpa_relative_entropy(probabilities))
  }))
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  result
}

    # A grid with one solution per model has no tree.
    "latents_no_tree",
    # A fit without locally dependent pairs has no table of them.
    "latents_no_local_dependence",
    # Nor does a fit without direct effects.
    "latents_no_direct_effects")
}

review_record.source_function:
.multilpa_diagnostic_catalogue <- function() {
  # `level` follows the fit rather than a fixed default: a two-level model is
  # asked about at both levels, and a family with one level has only one to
  # report. This is the rule `diagnostics()` already applies.
  by_level <- function(verb) {
    .multilpa_table(function(x, level = NULL)
      verb(x, level = .multilpa_default_level(x, level)), "level")
  }
  list(
    classification = by_level(.multilpa_classification_table),
    average_posteriors = by_level(.multilpa_average_posteriors),
    classification_errors = by_level(.multilpa_classification_errors),
    bch_weights = by_level(.multilpa_bch_weights),
    entropy = .multilpa_table(.multilpa_entropy_table),
    residuals = .multilpa_table(
      function(x, data = NULL, by = c("profile", "overall"),
               adjust = .multilpa_p_adjust_methods)
        .multilpa_bivariate_residuals(x, data = data, by = match.arg(by),
                                      adjust = match.arg(adjust)),
      c("data", "by", "adjust")),
    information_criteria = .multilpa_table(
      function(x, definitions = FALSE, format = c("wide", "long"))
        .multilpa_information_criteria(x, definitions = definitions,
                                       format = match.arg(format)),
      c("definitions", "format")),
    model = .multilpa_table(.multilpa_fit_frame))
}

  stopifnot(
    "`digits` must be a single number between 1 and 22" =

      is.numeric(rows) && length(rows) == 1L && is.finite(rows) && rows >= 0 &&
      rows == as.integer(rows))
  invisible(NULL)
}

review_record.source_function:
.latents_grid_views <- function(x, verb = "This function") {
  kind <- .latents_grid_kind(x)
  if (is.na(kind)) .latents_refuse_non_grid(x, verb)
  no_profiles <- paste(
    "it lays the candidates out by number of profiles and number of group",
    "classes, and a family grid's candidates have group classes only",
    "(compare them in as.data.frame(x))")
  spec <- switch(
    kind,
    profiles = list(
      criteria = .multilpa_enumeration_criteria(),
      default = c("aic", "bic_groups", "bic_individual", "icl_individual"),
      using = "bic_groups", axis = "n_profiles", word = .latents_class_word(x),
      refused = character()),
    transitions = list(
      criteria = c(AIC = "aic", BIC = "bic", "BIC (individuals)" = "bic_individual"),
      default = c("aic", "bic", "bic_individual"), using = "bic",
      axis = "n_profiles", word = "profiles", refused = character()),
    families = list(
      criteria = c(AIC = "aic", BIC = "bic", "BIC (individuals)" = "bic_individual"),
      default = c("aic", "bic", "bic_individual"), using = "bic",
      axis = "n_group_classes", word = "group classes",
      refused = c(
        deltas = no_profiles, heatmap = no_profiles, smallest = no_profiles,
        trust = no_profiles, selection = no_profiles)),
    regressions = list(
      criteria = c(AIC = "aic", BIC = "bic", "BIC (rows)" = "bic_rows",
                   SABIC = "sabic", ICL = "icl"),
      default = c("aic", "bic", "sabic", "icl"), using = "bic",
      axis = "n_profiles", word = "classes", refused = character()))
  spec$kind <- kind
  spec$views <- setdiff(.latents_grid_view_names(), names(spec$refused))
  spec
}

review_record.source_function:
.latents_grid_view_table <- function(x) {
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x, "plot_views")
  criteria <- unname(views$criteria)
  titles <- names(views$criteria) %||% toupper(criteria)
  if (identical(views$kind, "profiles")) {
    titles <- names(.multilpa_distinct_criteria(data.frame(), criteria))
  }
  named <- .latents_grid_view_names()
  described <- c(
    entropy = "Relative entropy of every candidate, at each level with two or more classes",
    avepp = "The lowest average posterior probability of every candidate, with the cutoff dashed",
    diagnostics = "Entropy and lowest AvePP together",
    deltas = "The decrease in the criterion in `using` with each added class and each added group class",
    heatmap = "The criterion in `using` over classes and group classes, relative to the lowest",
    smallest = "The share of the smallest class of every candidate, with 5% dashed",
    trust = "Convergence, boundary and replication of every candidate",
    selection = "Every selection view the grid offers, and diagnostics, as a list",
    tree = "How classes split as more are added, one plot per tree (see plot_tree())")
  data.frame(
    type = c(criteria, "all", named),
    group = c(rep("criteria", length(criteria) + 1L),
              ifelse(named %in% c("entropy", "avepp", "diagnostics"), "quality",
                     ifelse(named == "tree", "tree", "selection"))),
    supported = c(rep(TRUE, length(criteria) + 1L), named %in% views$views),
    description = c(sprintf("%s across the candidates; lower is preferred", titles),
                    "Every criterion of the grid, as panels of one plot",
                    unname(described[named])),
    reason = c(rep(NA_character_, length(criteria) + 1L),
               unname(views$refused[named])),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

.latents_plot_former_grid <- function(x, what, what_given, criterion, main,
                                      subtitle, extra) {
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x, "plot")
  # Without `what` or `criterion` the grid's summary is drawn, as
  # plot_enumeration() draws it: every default criterion as a panel.
  what <- if (!what_given && is.null(criterion)) views$default else
    .latents_grid_criterion(.latents_former_argument(
      what, what_given, criterion, c("what", "criterion")), views)
  supplied <- names(extra) %||% rep("", length(extra))
  passed <- c("combine", "labels", "mark_minimum", "cutoff", "using",
              if (identical(what, "tree")) .latents_tree_arguments())
  forwarded <- nzchar(supplied) & supplied %in% passed
  .latents_warn_unused_arguments(extra[!forwarded], "plot()",
                                 .latents_grid_plot_advice())
  do.call(plot_enumeration, c(list(x, what = what, main = main,
                                   subtitle = subtitle), extra[forwarded]))
}

review_record.source_function:
.latents_label <- function(values) {
  values <- as.character(values)
  # A class logit's intercept within one group class.
  values <- sub("^\\(Intercept\\):group_class_([0-9]+)$", "Intercept, group class \\1",
                values)
  # An ordinal regression's threshold between two categories, "lower|upper".
  values <- sub("^threshold:(.*[|].*)$", "Threshold \\1", values)
  values <- sub("^class_([0-9]+)$", "Class \\1", values)
  values <- sub("^group_class_([0-9]+)$", "Group class \\1", values)
  values <- sub("^profile_([0-9]+)$", "Profile \\1", values)
  values <- gsub("(Intercept)", "Intercept", values, fixed = TRUE)
  values <- gsub(":", " x ", values, fixed = TRUE)
  values[values %in% c("common", "all")] <- "All classes"
  words <- c(variance = "Variance", sd = "SD", correlation = "Correlation",
             covariance = "Covariance")
  known <- values %in% names(words)
  values[known] <- words[values[known]]
  values
}

.latents_render_card <- function(x, display) {
  frame <- as.data.frame(x)
  labels <- vapply(display, `[[`, character(1), "label")
  values <- vapply(display, function(spec) .latents_cells(frame, spec)[1L], character(1))
  # An entry the fit does not have (for example groups of a single-level
  # fit) is left out rather than printed empty.
  labels <- labels[nzchar(values)]
  values <- values[nzchar(values)]
  width <- max(nchar(labels, type = "width"))
  c(if (!is.null(attr(x, "title"))) c(attr(x, "title"), ""),
    sprintf("%s  %s", formatC(labels, width = -width), values))
}

review_record.source_function:
summary.multilpa <- function(object, ...) {
  stopifnot("`object` must be an `multilpa` fit" = inherits(object, "multilpa"))
  # Built field by field rather than by subsetting the fit with a vector of
  # names: subsetting a list by a name it does not carry yields a `NULL`
  # element keyed `NA`, so an absent field became an unnamed hole in the
  # summary instead of a documented default.
  result <- list(
    call = object$call,
    n_observations = object$n_observations,
    n_informative = object$n_informative %||% object$n_observations,
    n_groups = object$n_groups,
    n_profiles = object$n_profiles,
    n_group_classes = object$n_group_classes,
    variance_model = object$variance_model,
    covariance_model = object$covariance_model %||% "diagonal",
    # "error" is the mode every fit made before the field was recorded used;
    # "listwise" is not a mode this package has.
    missing = object$missing %||% "error",
    single_level = isTRUE(object$single_level),
    continuous = .multilpa_continuous_names(object),
    categorical = object$categorical %||% character(),
    fixed = object$fixed %||% character(),
    staged = isTRUE(object$staged),
    means = object$means,
    variances = object$variances,
    standard_deviations = object$standard_deviations,
    covariances = object$covariances,
    response_probabilities = object$response_probabilities,
    profile_probabilities = object$profile_probabilities,
    group_probabilities = object$group_probabilities,
    effective_profile_counts = object$effective_profile_counts %||%
      colSums(object$subject_posteriors),
    effective_group_counts = object$effective_group_counts %||%
      colSums(object$group_posteriors),
    weights = object$weights,
    log_likelihood = object$log_likelihood,
    n_parameters = object$n_parameters,
    n_parameters_with_measurement =
      object$n_parameters_with_measurement %||% object$n_parameters,
    aic = object$aic,
    bic = object$bic,
    bic_individual = object$bic_individual,
    converged = object$converged,
    iterations = object$iterations,
    boundary = object$boundary,
    min_variance = object$min_variance,
    small_classes = object$small_classes,
    starts = object$starts,
    best_start = object$best_start,
    n_best_replicated = object$n_best_replicated,
    # The starts run to the end; under emEM the table also holds the screened.
    n_starts = object$n_starts %||% nrow(object$starts),
    replication_tolerance = object$replication_tolerance)
  if (isTRUE(object$noise)) {
    result$noise <- TRUE
    result$noise_posteriors <- object$noise_posteriors
  }
  stopifnot("the summary must not carry an unnamed field" =
              !anyNA(names(result)) && !any(names(result) == ""))
  # Every table the fit can produce, built once here, so `get_results()` on the
  # summary serves the same tables the fit would and `print()` can show them
  # all without recomputing anything.
  result$tables <- get_results(object, "all")
  class(result) <- "summary_multilpa"
  result
}

.multilpa_fit_frame <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "multilpa_covariates")) {
    return(.multilpa_covariate_fit_frame(x))
  }
  # A field an older fit or another family does not carry is absent, not
  # short: `NULL` and a length-two vector would both corrupt the row.
  data.frame(n_observations = .multilpa_one(x$n_observations, NA_integer_),
             n_informative = .multilpa_one(x$n_informative %||% x$n_observations,
                                           NA_integer_),
             n_groups = .multilpa_one(x$n_groups, NA_integer_),
             n_profiles = .multilpa_one(x$n_profiles, NA_integer_),
             n_group_classes = .multilpa_one(x$n_group_classes, NA_integer_),
             centering = .multilpa_one(x$centering %||% "none", NA_character_),
             scaling = .multilpa_one(x$scaling %||% "none", NA_character_),
             # A pattern fit is estimated as a full covariance; its label names
             # the diagonal it extends and the pairs, not VVV or EEE.
             covariance_structure = .multilpa_one(
               if (is.null(x$covariance_pattern)) x$covariance_structure else
                 .latents_pattern_label(x), NA_character_),
             n_parameters = .multilpa_one(x$n_parameters, NA_integer_),
             n_parameters_with_measurement =
               .multilpa_one(x$n_parameters_with_measurement %||%
                               x$n_parameters, NA_integer_),
             log_likelihood = .multilpa_one(x$log_likelihood, NA_real_),
             aic = .multilpa_one(x$aic, NA_real_),
             bic_groups = .multilpa_one(x$bic, NA_real_),
             bic_individual = .multilpa_one(x$bic_individual, NA_real_),
             converged = .multilpa_one(x$converged, NA),
             iterations = .multilpa_one(x$iterations, NA_integer_),
             boundary = .multilpa_one(x$boundary, NA),
             small_classes = .multilpa_one(x$small_classes, NA),
             best_start = .multilpa_one(x$best_start, NA_integer_),
             n_best_replicated = .multilpa_one(x$n_best_replicated, NA_integer_),
             weights = .multilpa_one(x$weights, NA_character_),
             row.names = NULL)
}

review_record.source_function:
diagnostics <- function(x, data = NULL, plots = TRUE,
                        by = c("profile", "overall"), ...) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x),
            "`plots` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(plots) || isFALSE(plots))
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "diagnostics()",
    paste("The only argument of a gathered table it forwards is `by`;",
          "ask get_results() for that table directly for anything else."))
  by <- match.arg(by)
  data <- .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)
  has_groups <- !is.null(x$group_posteriors)
  level <- if (has_groups) "both" else "individuals"
  result <- list(
    entropy = .multilpa_entropy_table(x),
    classification = .multilpa_classification_table(x, level = level),
    average_posteriors = .multilpa_average_posteriors(x, level = level),
    # Residuals need a discrete group-class model and no noise component; a
    # fit without them has no such table, as `get_results(x, "all")` says, and
    # the other three diagnostics are still reported.
    residuals = tryCatch(.multilpa_bivariate_residuals(x, data, by = by),
                         latents_no_group_classes = function(condition) NULL,
                         latents_unsupported_noise = function(condition) NULL),
    fit = x)
  class(result) <- "multilpa_diagnostics"
  if (isTRUE(plots) && .gg_available()) print(plot(result))
  result
}

review_record.source_function:
report <- function(x, data = NULL, plots = TRUE,
                   by = c("profile", "overall"), rows = 10L, ...) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x),
            "`plots` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(plots) || isFALSE(plots))
  # Checked here as well as in diagnostics(), so a refused argument is refused
  # before three sections have already been printed.
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "report()",
    "It forwards `by` to diagnostics() and `rows` to print(summary(x)).")
  by <- match.arg(by)
  data <- .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)
  print(summary(x), rows = rows)
  cat("\n")
  print(descriptives(x))
  cat("\n")
  quality <- diagnostics(x, data = data, plots = FALSE, by = by)
  print(quality)
  if (isTRUE(plots) && .gg_available()) {
    views <- .multilpa_supported_views(x)
    # A view can still refuse for a reason only the method knows -- a family
    # with no plot at all, a panel with nothing in it. `report()` is a first
    # look, so it moves on; it says which views it could not draw rather than
    # dropping them silently.
    refused <- unlist(lapply(views, function(view) {
      drawn <- tryCatch({
        print(if (is.na(view)) plot(x) else plot(x, what = view))
        NULL
      },
      latents_no_plot = function(condition) view,
      latents_nothing_to_plot = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_time = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_categorical = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_continuous = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_indicator_data = function(condition) view)
      drawn
    }))
    if (length(refused) > 0L) {
      cat(sprintf("\nNot drawn for this model: %s\n",
                  paste(ifelse(is.na(refused), "the default plot", refused),
                        collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }
  invisible(x)
}

review_record.name: enumerate_classes
review_record.purpose: Enumerate numbers of individual profiles and group classes  Fits every requested combination of profile count, group-class count and covariance structure and returns the candidates with their information criteria and classification diagnostics.

input_contract.signature_source:
enumerate_classes <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles = 1:4,
                              n_group_classes = 1:3, model = "basic",
                              seed = NULL, family = "profiles",
                              between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
                              time = NULL, ..., cores = 1L, type = NULL,
                              verbose = cores > 1L)

parameter_descriptions.declared_description: The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in   (students in schools, reports in students). Required; `NULL` enumerates   single-level models, with a message. [enumerate_lpa()] and   [enumerate_lca()] fit single-level models directly.
Positive integer profile counts to try. Default `1:4`.
Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default   `1:3`. With `id = NULL` it is 1 and may be left out.

The covariance structures to cross with the class counts.   `"basic"` (the default) fits four structures: `"EEI"` (equal variances,   no covariances), `"VVI"` (varying variances, no covariances), `"EEE"`   (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and `"VVV"` (a covariance   matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated   indicators tends to favour additional profiles. `"all"` fits all 14   structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by   their three-letter codes, as [multilpa()]'s `model` takes them: the   letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's   covariance matrix, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across profiles,   with `I` for no covariances. `NULL` crosses no structures. With one   continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance)   are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is   crossed. A structure set through `variance_model`, `covariance_model`,   `volume`, `shape` or `orientation` in `...` replaces the default.
Optional seed for each fit: a whole number `set.seed()`   accepts. Anything else raises `latents_bad_argument` before any candidate   is fitted.

`"profiles"` (the default) enumerates the profile model over   `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes` and `model`. One or more of the   group-class families `"additive"`, `"dispersion"` and   `"additive_dispersion"` enumerates those instead, over `family`,   `n_group_classes` and `between_variance`; these need `id`, `n_profiles`   and `model` are then refused, and the result is a   `latents_family_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and   [get_candidate()].

For group-class families: the between-variance   restrictions to cross, `"varying"`, `"equal"` or both (the default). The   dispersion family is always fitted with `"equal"`. Refused for the   profile family.

The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models   ([lta()]) over `n_profiles` (default `2:4`) and `n_group_classes`   (default `1`), with every other `lta()` argument given in `...` held   fixed. `model`, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only   the profile family is available. The result is a   `latents_transition_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and   [get_candidate()].

Number of processor cores to fit the candidates on (default   1). Each candidate sets and restores its own random seed, so with `seed`   given the result is identical to `cores = 1`. Candidates are fitted by   forked processes on macOS and Linux, and by a socket cluster on Windows   and on macOS when R uses Apple's Accelerate BLAS (socket workers load the   installed package). Warnings and messages from the workers are passed on   in grid order once all have finished. Without `seed`, the random starts   differ between runs on any number of cores. Lost worker results are retried   once with half as many workers (rounded up). One `latents_worker_lost`   warning reports how many tasks were lost and recovered, and suggests fewer   cores. A task still lost becomes a failed start (for flat start grids) or   a failed candidate; the other results are retained. On sockets, bounded   chunks preserve earlier results when a connection breaks; completed tasks   within the failed chunk may also be retried. Each core holds its own copy   of the fits it computes; `parallel::detectCores()` gives the number   available.   Transition grids (`time`) and profile grids (including categorical-only   latent class models) distribute individual starts across one pool,   longest estimated first, with at most `cores` workers and no nested   workers. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool; `search`   keeps the same defaults as [multilpa()]. Setup, ordered starting values,   start selection and finalisation stay in the current process. Profile   models with membership covariates or joined categorical `local_dependence`   pairs instead occupy one worker per candidate in the same pool, with   serial starts. Group-class families also keep candidate-level parallelism.

Whether to report progress: one message each when the   candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid   is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when `cores > 1`,   where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (`family`) are not   reported.

Optional model type: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`. `NULL`   (the default) keeps the existing routing and measurement settings.   `"lca"` treats every indicator as categorical, as [multilca()] does:   indicators named in `ordinal` or `count` keep those distributions, and   `categorical` adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response   codes are categorical with `type = "lca"`. `"lpa"` requires continuous   indicators and refuses non-empty `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count`.   Both require `time = NULL`. `"lta"` requires `time` and takes its   measurement settings from `categorical`, as [lta()] does; it does not   make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires   `family = "profiles"`; leave `type = NULL` for group-class families.

Further arguments to [multilpa()] (or to [lta()] with `time`),   applied to every candidate, such as `n_starts` (random starts per   candidate), `max_iter`, `missing`, `categorical`, `centering`, `scaling`,   `drop_empty` and `boundary` (`"exclude"` sets aside starts with a   variance at `min_variance`, degenerate solutions that become more likely   as `n_starts` grows). For example, `enumerate_classes(data, vars, id,   n_profiles = 2:6, n_starts = 20, seed = 1)`. Group-class families take   only `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol` and `min_variance`.
